required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_k)$ be a partition with $|\alpha|=\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_k$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]), and let $n\ge0$ be
an integer. Whenever

$$n\;\ge\;|\alpha|+\alpha_1,$$

define the **first-row padding** of $\alpha$ to size $n$ to be
$$\alpha[n]:=\bigl(n-|\alpha|,\ \alpha_1,\ \alpha_2,\ \dots,\ \alpha_k\bigr).$$

The threshold is exact.

**Above the threshold.** Suppose $n\ge|\alpha|+\alpha_1$. Then
$n-|\alpha|\ge\alpha_1\ge0$, so every entry of the displayed sequence is a
nonnegative integer, the entries sum to $(n-|\alpha|)+|\alpha|=n$, and the
sequence is weakly decreasing because $n-|\alpha|\ge\alpha_1$ and $\alpha$ is
weakly decreasing ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).
If $\alpha$ is nonempty then $\alpha_1\ge1$, hence $n-|\alpha|\ge1$ and the
displayed sequence is a partition of $n$ with positive parts. If
$\alpha=\varnothing$ then the displayed sequence is $(n)$; this is a partition
of $n$ for every $n\ge1$, while for $n=0$ one takes $\varnothing[0]:=\varnothing$,
the unique partition of $0$. Thus the padding is defined and is a partition of
$n$ on the whole displayed range.

**Below the threshold.** If $\alpha$ is nonempty and $n<|\alpha|+\alpha_1$,
then $n-|\alpha|<\alpha_1$; if also $n\ge|\alpha|$ the leading entry is
nonnegative but smaller than the second entry $\alpha_1$, and if $n<|\alpha|$
it is negative. In both cases the displayed sequence is not a partition, so
$\alpha[n]$ is left undefined. The threshold $|\alpha|+\alpha_1$ is therefore
the exact size at which the padded family begins: at
$n=|\alpha|+\alpha_1$ the padding equals $(\alpha_1,\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\dots)$,
which is a partition with a repeated first part when $\alpha$ is nonempty.

**Neutrality of the notation.** This definition records a family of partitions;
it asserts no constancy of any quantity along the family and no stability
property. The same notation is used by the FI-module and
representation-stability developments, where the padding threshold reappears as
the generation degree of the family under consideration.

actual_declared_use_sites.text: [F3] The coefficient of $s_{\delta}$ in $s_{\alpha[n]}*s_{\beta[n]}$ is $g^\delta_{\alpha[n],\beta[n]}$, and for $\delta=\gamma[n]$ with $n\ge|\gamma|+\gamma_1$ this is the coefficient of the padded label ([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]], [[ex-murnaghan-stability-for-alpha-beta-two]]).

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Work over the field $\mathbb C$ and fix an integer $d\ge 0$
([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], [[def-commutative-ring]]). Let
$\mathcal F_d$ be the free associative unital $\mathbb C$-algebra on the
$d+(d-1)$ symbols $x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ (for $d=0$ there is only
the unit; for $d=1$ only $x_1$), with its word basis and universal property
([[lem-hh-free-associative-ring-and-relations-descent]]), and let
$I_d\mathrel{\trianglelefteq}\mathcal F_d$ be the two-sided ideal
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]])
generated by the following elements:

- $x_ix_j-x_jx_i$ for all $1\le i,j\le d$;
- $s_i^2-1$, $s_is_{i+1}s_i-s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1}$, and $s_is_j-s_js_i$ for
  $|i-j|>1$, for $1\le i,j\le d-1$;
- $s_ix_j-x_js_i$ for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$, $s_ix_{i+1}-x_is_i-1$, and
  $x_{i+1}s_i-s_ix_i-1$, for $1\le i\le d-1$ and $1\le j\le d$.

The **degenerate affine Hecke algebra** is the quotient $\mathbb C$-algebra
$$H_d:=\mathcal F_d/I_d$$
with unit element written $1$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]). We keep the symbols
$x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ for their images, and for $w\in S_d$ we write
$w$ for the image in $H_d$ of any word in the $s_i$ representing $w$; this is
independent of the chosen word once the basis theorem below is proved. For
$a\in\mathbb C$, the notation $H_d/(x_1-a)$ means the quotient by the two-sided
ideal generated by $x_1-a$.

The verification below establishes exactly the structure of $H_d$ used
throughout this page: the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad r_1,\dots,r_d\ge0,\ w\in S_d,$$
form a $\mathbb C$-basis, so that
$H_d\cong\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C[S_d]$ as a vector
space with polynomial and group-algebra subalgebras
([[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]], [[def-group-ring]]);
$H_0=\mathbb C$ and $H_1=\mathbb C[x_1]$; for every $a$ there is a unique
algebra isomorphism
$$H_d/(x_1-a)\cong\mathbb C[S_d],\qquad x_j\longmapsto a+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j);$$
and total polynomial degree is an algebra filtration whose associated graded is
the semidirect product $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$ in which
$s_i$ acts by swapping $x_i$ and $x_{i+1}$. The cross relation is
inhomogeneous, so it does not turn $H_d$ into a graded algebra with
$\deg x_i=1$ and $\deg s_i=0$.

actual_declared_use_sites.text:
[F2] The defining relations of
[[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] at rank two are
$s^2=1$, $x_1x_2=x_2x_1$, $sx_2=x_1s+1$ and $x_2s=sx_1+1$.
The level-one quotient of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] imposes
$x_1=m$. Only these defining relations, not its tensor-realization proof,
are needed below.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $z\in A$ be a unit. Fix an integer
$n\ge0$.

**The nondegenerate affine presentation.** The algebra
$H_n^{\mathrm{aff}}(A;z)$ is the $A$-algebra presented by commuting units
$X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$
([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]],
[[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]) subject to
$$T_r^2=(z-1)T_r+z,\qquad T_rT_{r+1}T_r=T_{r+1}T_rT_{r+1},\qquad T_rT_s=T_sT_r\quad(|r-s|>1),$$
$$T_rX_rT_r=zX_{r+1},\qquad T_rX_s=X_sT_r\quad(s\notin\{r,r+1\}),$$
the last two relations being the Bernstein relation and the distant mixed
commutation, and with $T_r$ invertible as a consequence of its quadratic
relation. For $n=0$ the algebra is $A$.

**The degenerate affine presentation.** The algebra
$H_n^{\deg}(A)$ is the $A$-algebra presented by commuting generators
$x_1,\dots,x_n$ and symmetric-group generators $s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}$ subject to
the Coxeter relations $s_r^2=1$, $s_rs_{r+1}s_r=s_{r+1}s_rs_{r+1}$,
$s_rs_t=s_ts_r$ for $|r-t|>1$ together with the mixed relations
$$s_rx_r=x_{r+1}s_r-1,\qquad s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1,\qquad s_rx_t=x_ts_r\quad(t\notin\{r,r+1\}).$$

**Auxiliary cyclotomic quotients.** For a monic polynomial
$f(u)=u^{\ell}+a_{\ell-1}u^{\ell-1}+\dots+a_0$ in $A[u]$ of degree $\ell$
impose the single relation $f(X_1)=0$ (respectively $f(x_1)=0$) on the FIRST
polynomial generator and call the resulting quotient the **monic cyclotomic
quotient**; when $\ell=0$, so that $f=1$, the quotient at positive rank is the
zero algebra, while rank zero remains $A$. In the nondegenerate case the
constant term $a_0$ is required to be a unit. The first-strand convention
imposed here (cyclotomic relation on $X_1$, and later induction appending on
the right) is the one used on this page.

**The charged cyclic specialization.** Let $A=F$ be a field, let
$z=q_H\in F^{\times}$ have finite quantum characteristic $e\ge2$
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), and let
$I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ be the cyclic **label set** of residues, with a
dominant cyclic type-A weight $(\lambda_i)_{i\in I}$, $\lambda_i\ge0$, and
$\ell=\sum_i\lambda_i$
([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). If $q_H\ne1$ use the
nondegenerate presentation and put $c_i:=q_H^{\,i}$; if $q_H=1$ (which forces
$\operatorname{char}F=e$) use the degenerate presentation and put
$c_i:=i\cdot1_F$. Impose
$$f(z_1)=\prod_{i\in I}(z_1-c_i)^{\lambda_i}$$
on the first generator ($z_1=X_1$ in the nondegenerate branch and $z_1=x_1$ in
the degenerate branch) and write $H_d^\Lambda$ for the resulting **charged
cyclotomic quotient** of rank $d$. This charged finite-$e$ branch is the scope
of the present page; the arbitrary-base affine and monic definitions above
supply its universal PBW and trace proof inputs. The definition itself asserts
no basis, no spectrum, no primitive block decomposition and no
Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism. The grading variable $v$ of the KLR side is
independent of $q_H$.

**Well-definedness notes.** The nondegenerate parameters $c_i=q_H^i$ are
distinct because $q_H$ has multiplicative order exactly $e$; the degenerate
parameters $c_i=i\cdot1_F$ are distinct because $\operatorname{char}F=e$ makes
$i\cdot1_F\ne j\cdot1_F$ for $0\le i<j<e$. In the nondegenerate branch no
embedding of the label set $\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ into $F$ is claimed or used:
$i$ is only a label for the value $q_H^i$. All these definitions are given by
generators, relations and a two-sided quotient ideal and use no choice
principle.

required_interface.text:
In ZF,

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

actual_declared_use_sites.text:
1. **Well-definedness of $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$.** If $x\notin
   \operatorname{Supp}(s)$ then $s_x=0$ in the stalk $\mathcal F_x$
   ([[def-stalk-of-presheaf]]), and since the stalk maps of a morphism commute
   with the germ maps, $\varphi(s)_x=\varphi_x(s_x)=0$, so
   $\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi(s))\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(s)$. A support
   $\operatorname{Supp}(t)$ is closed in $X$: if $x\notin
   \operatorname{Supp}(t)$ then $t$ agrees with the zero section on some open
   neighbourhood of $x$, by the description of equality of germs
   ([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]]). Hence
   $\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi(s))$ is a closed subset of $X$ contained in the
   compact set $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$; being closed in $X$ it is closed in the
   subspace $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$, so it is a compact subset of that compact
   space ([[thm-closed-subspace-of-a-compact-space-is-compact]]) and therefore
   a compact subset of $X$ ([[lem-compactness-of-a-subspace-is-ambient]]), and
   $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ maps $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)$ into
   $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal G)$. Composites and identities are computed
   componentwise, so $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ is a functor; it is additive because
   $\Gamma(X,-)$ is.
2. **Sheaves of $k$-vector spaces.** If $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of
   $k$-vector spaces, then $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)$ is a $k$-vector subspace of
   $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$: the support of $c\cdot s$ is
   $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$ for $c\ne0$ and $\varnothing$ for $c=0$, and the
   zero section has empty support. For a morphism $\varphi$ of sheaves of
   $k$-vector spaces the map $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ is $k$-linear, since
   $\Gamma(X,\varphi)$ is. The higher derived functors below are computed from
   an injective resolution datum on abelian sheaves, so they are abelian
   groups; the degree-zero part is the $k$-vector space
   $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)$.
3. **Left exactness.** For every short exact sequence
   $0\to\mathcal F'\xrightarrow{\varphi'}\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\varphi}\mathcal F''\to0$
   of abelian sheaves the sequence
   $$0\to\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F')\xrightarrow{\Gamma_c(\varphi')}\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\Gamma_c(\varphi)}\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F'')$$
   is exact. Injectivity: a monomorphism of sheaves has injective stalk maps
   ([[thm-exactness-of-sheaves-stalkwise]]), so
   $\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi'(s'))=\operatorname{Supp}(s')$ and a section
   killed by $\varphi'$ has all germs zero, hence is zero. Exactness at the
   middle: the kernel of $\Gamma(X,\varphi)$ is the image of
   $\Gamma(X,\varphi')$ by left exactness of global sections
   ([[lem-global-sections-left-exact]]); if $s=\varphi'(s')$ has compact
   support, then $s'$ has the same support,
   $\operatorname{Supp}(s')=\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi'(s'))=
   \operatorname{Supp}(s)$, because $\varphi'$ is stalk-injective, so $s'$ lies
   in $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F')$, and the reverse inclusion is immediate from
   $\varphi\circ\varphi'=0$. Thus $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ is an additive left exact
   functor on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ ([[def-left-exact-and-right-exact-functor]]).
4. **The derived functors.** Abelian sheaves on $X$ have enough injectives, and
   the embeddings of [[thm-abelian-sheaves-have-enough-injectives]] supply one
   functorial injective resolution datum $\mathcal F\mapsto I^\bullet(\mathcal F)$
   on the whole category $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$, under the Axiom of Choice
   ([[def-right-derived-object-relative-to-injective-resolution-data]]). The
   **compactly supported cohomology** of $\mathcal F$ is
   $$H^q_c(X,\mathcal F):=R^q\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F):=H^q\bigl(\Gamma_c(X,I^\bullet(\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{del}})\bigr)\qquad(q\ge0),\qquad H^q_c(X,\mathcal F):=0\quad(q<0),$$
   the cohomology of the deleted resolution, as in the pattern of
   [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]; for a morphism $\varphi$ we
   write $H^q_c(X,\varphi):=R^q\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ for the induced map.
5. **Independence of the datum.** If $J$ is another supplied injective
   resolution datum on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$, then $R^q\Gamma_c(X,-)$ computed from
   $J$ is naturally isomorphic to $R^q\Gamma_c(X,-)$ computed from $I$
   ([[thm-right-derived-functors-from-two-supplied-injective-resolution-data-are-naturally-isomorphic]]);
   the Axiom of Dependent Choice needed for that comparison follows from AC
   ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]). The notation
   $H^q_c(X,\mathcal F)$ therefore does not depend on the datum up to this
   canonical natural isomorphism.
6. **Delta functor and the compact case.** Since $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ is additive
   and left exact and the datum is defined on all of $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$, the
   functors $R^q\Gamma_c(X,-)$, $q\ge0$, carry connecting maps that make them a
   cohomological delta functor with $R^0\Gamma_c(X,-)\cong\Gamma_c(X,-)$, and
   every short exact sequence of abelian sheaves has a long exact
   compact-support cohomology sequence, natural in the sequence
   ([[thm-right-derived-functors-form-a-cohomological-delta-functor]]). If $X$
   is compact, then for every global section $s$ its support is closed in $X$ by
   fact 1, hence a closed subset of the compact space $X$ and therefore
   compact, so every global section is compactly supported; hence
   $\Gamma_c(X,-)=\Gamma(X,-)$ and
   $H^q_c(X,\mathcal F)=H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ for every $q$, where $H^q(X,-)$ is
   the sheaf cohomology of [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]
   computed from the same datum.

- **Choice accounting.** The Axiom of Choice is used exactly once in the
  definition, through the injective resolution datum for abelian sheaves
  ([[thm-abelian-sheaves-have-enough-injectives]]); the independence of the
  datum and the delta-functor statement use the Axiom of Dependent Choice,
  which follows from AC ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).
  Nothing else in the definition selects from infinitely many sets.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group
with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), with root lattice $Q$,
simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ and integer pairing
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$, and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with generators $E_i,F_i,K_h$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The lattice $P$ plays
the role of the integral weights of the classical theory
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]); the pairing need not
be perfect, and no identification $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$ is
assumed anywhere.

A **$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module** is a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $M$
together with a direct sum decomposition

$$M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$$

(an internal direct sum of $\mathbb Q(q)$-subspaces, only finitely many nonzero
on each vector) such that, for all $\mu\in P$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$,

$$K_h\ \text{acts on}\ M_\mu\ \text{by the scalar}\ q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle},\qquad E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i},\qquad F_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-\alpha_i}.$$

The subspaces $M_\mu$ are the **chosen label-weight spaces**: the grading is
part of the structure and is not reconstructed from the action, because the
pairing may have a kernel. **Morphisms** of $P$-graded type-one weight modules
are the $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module maps $f\colon M\to N$ with
$f(M_\mu)\subseteq N_\mu$ for every $\mu$; the weight submodules and quotients
considered on this page are those with the induced grading (Verification, steps
3.1 and 4.1).

The module is **integrable** if $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent on every
vector: for every $v\in M$ and every $i$ there are integers $N_e(v,i),N_f(v,i)\ge1$
with $E_i^{N_e(v,i)}v=0$ and $F_i^{N_f(v,i)}v=0$. The exponents may depend on
the vector and on $i$, and both directions are required independently;
integrability is not a uniform nilpotence condition.

The following are additional hypotheses, never part of the definition:
finiteness of the dimension of every $M_\mu$; boundedness of the set of $\mu$
with $M_\mu\ne0$ above (or below); finite generation of $M$. The zero module is
a $P$-graded type-one weight module with the empty grading ($M_\mu=0$ for all
$\mu$), and it is integrable.

Two remarks are recorded here and proved below. First, when the pairing
separates $P$, the spaces $M_\mu$ are exactly the simultaneous eigenspaces of
the $K_h$, and the present definition recovers the usual type-one weight
modules (Verification, steps 2.1 and 4.1). Second, when the pairing does not
separate, distinct labels $\mu\ne\mu'$ may carry the same toral character, and
a simultaneous toral eigenspace must not be equated with a single label space;
the definition therefore takes the label grading as data. The regularization of
finite-cone support and all highest-weight comparisons on this page are proved
later, not assumed here by writing $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$.
No choice principle enters this definition.

Let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module $M$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]) with the induced operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $L/qL$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]). For $b\in B$ write $\mathrm{wt}(b)=\mu$ when $b\in B_\mu$, and define
$$\varepsilon_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde e_i^{\,n}b\neq0\},\qquad \varphi_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde f_i^{\,n}b\neq0\}.$$
Then (see below) both numbers are finite and
$$\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle .$$
The top of the $i$-string through $b$ is the vertex $\tilde e_i^{\,\varepsilon_i(b)}b$, of weight $\mathrm{wt}(b)+\varepsilon_i(b)\alpha_i$; its highest rank-one integer is $\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle+2\varepsilon_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)$.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
In the same positive-first/negative-second completion $\widehat C$ of [[def-root-height-completion-for-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiners]], let $\Theta=\sum_\nu\Theta_\nu$ be the unique normalized bar-coproduct intertwiner of [[thm-the-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiner-exists-and-is-unique]]. Then:

(i) $\Theta^{-1}=\overline\Theta=(\psi\otimes\psi)(\Theta)$, the inverse being taken in the root-height convolution algebra of $\widehat C$ and not switching the positive and negative tensor order;

(ii) for every $\nu$ the exact threefold identities hold:
$$(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{23}(1\otimes K_{-\eta}\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{13},$$
$$(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{12}(1\otimes K_\eta\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{13},$$
with subscripts denoting tensor positions and $\Theta_{\nu'}=0$ when $\nu'\notin Q_+$;

(iii) the two normalized tensor-bar compositions satisfy the field cocycle identity
$$((\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta)\Theta_{12}=((\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta)\Theta_{23},$$
coefficientwise in the transported source completion and on every vector for which the iterated actions are finite;

(iv) the bar-coproduct counterpart needed for the cocycle is
$$(\mathrm{id}\otimes\overline\Delta)\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{13}(1\otimes K_{-\gamma}\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{12}.$$

Removing the normalization $\Theta_0=1$ permits arbitrary scalar multiples of the same linear intertwiner equation, so normalization is essential for uniqueness; no integrality of coefficients and no uncontrolled infinite evaluation is asserted.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $e\in\{2,3,4,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ and let $\lambda\vdash n$ be a partition
with parts $\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\cdots$ and conjugate $\lambda'$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). Then $\lambda$ is
**$e$-regular** when every positive integer occurs as a part of $\lambda$ fewer
than $e$ times, i.e. $z_j(\lambda)<e$ for every $j\ge1$, and **$e$-restricted**
when $\lambda_i-\lambda_{i+1}<e$ for every $i\ge1$ (with $\lambda_i:=0$ for
$i>\ell(\lambda)$).

For finite $e$ these are exactly the $p$-regular and $p$-restricted notions of
[[def-p-regular-and-p-restricted-partitions]] with $p=e$. For $e=\infty$ both
conditions are vacuous, so every partition is both $e$-regular and
$e$-restricted: the inequalities $z_j(\lambda)<\infty$ and
$\lambda_i-\lambda_{i+1}<\infty$ hold because partitions have finitely many
nonzero parts and each difference is a nonnegative integer. Moreover $\lambda$
is $e$-restricted if and only if its conjugate $\lambda'$ is $e$-regular: the
multiplicity of the part $i$ in $\lambda'$ is the number of columns of
$[\lambda]$ of height exactly $i$, namely $\lambda_i-\lambda_{i+1}$, so the
two conditions $z_i(\lambda')=\lambda_i-\lambda_{i+1}<e$ are the same family
of inequalities, and for $e=\infty$ both sides hold. In particular
$\varnothing$ is simultaneously $e$-regular and $e$-restricted for every $e$
([[def-p-regular-and-p-restricted-partitions]]).

actual_declared_use_sites.text:
- **$e$-cores are $e$-regular and $e$-restricted.** Suppose $\lambda$ has $e$
  equal parts and let $a$ be their common value; the $e$ corresponding rows
  have length at least $a$, so the column $a$ of $[\lambda]$ has height
  $\lambda'_a\ge e$. The nodes $(i',a)$ with $1\le i'\le\lambda'_a$ all lie in
  $[\lambda]$, and their hook lengths are
  $h_{i',a}(\lambda)=1+\lambda'_a-i'$, which run through the whole range
  $1,2,\dots,\lambda'_a$; since $\lambda'_a\ge e$, one
  of them equals $e$. Hence an $e$-core has no $e$ equal parts, i.e. it is
  $e$-regular, in the sense of
  [[def-e-regular-and-e-restricted-partitions]]. Conjugation preserves the
  multiset of hook lengths ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]],
  [[def-hook-arm-leg-and-hook-length]]) and a partition is $e$-restricted
  exactly when its conjugate is $e$-regular
  ([[def-e-regular-and-e-restricted-partitions]]); applying the previous
  sentence to $\lambda'$ therefore shows that an $e$-core is $e$-restricted.
  (For finite $e$ the notions agree with $p$-regular and $p$-restricted at
  $p=e$.)

- **$e$-cores are $e$-regular and $e$-restricted.** Suppose $\lambda$ has $e$
  equal parts and let $a$ be their common value; the $e$ corresponding rows
  have length at least $a$, so the column $a$ of $[\lambda]$ has height
  $\lambda'_a\ge e$. The nodes $(i',a)$ with $1\le i'\le\lambda'_a$ all lie in

  $h_{i',a}(\lambda)=1+\lambda'_a-i'$, which run through the whole range
  $1,2,\dots,\lambda'_a$; since $\lambda'_a\ge e$, one
  of them equals $e$. Hence an $e$-core has no $e$ equal parts, i.e. it is
  $e$-regular, in the sense of
  [[def-e-regular-and-e-restricted-partitions]]. Conjugation preserves the
  multiset of hook lengths ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]],
  [[def-hook-arm-leg-and-hook-length]]) and a partition is $e$-restricted

  sentence to $\lambda'$ therefore shows that an $e$-core is $e$-restricted.
  (For finite $e$ the notions agree with $p$-regular and $p$-restricted at

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, and $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$
([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). For $1\le k\le n$ define
$$L_1:=0,\qquad L_k:=q^{-1}T_{(k-1,k)}+q^{-2}T_{(k-2,k)}+\cdots+q^{1-k}T_{(1,k)}\in H\quad(k\ge2),$$
where $T_{(i,k)}$ is the standard basis element indexed by the transposition
$(i\ k)$ ([[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). The $L_k$
are the **Hecke Jucys-Murphy elements**. They are fixed by the star
anti-automorphism $T_w^*=T_{w^{-1}}$
([[lem-the-star-antiautomorphism-of-the-type-a-hecke-algebra]]): each
transposition $(i\ k)$ is its own inverse, so $T_{(i,k)}^*=T_{(i,k)}$, and the
coefficients $q^{i-k}$ are central, whence
$L_k^*=\sum_{i<k}q^{i-k}T_{(i,k)}=L_k$. They commute pairwise and every
symmetric polynomial in $L_1,\dots,L_n$ with coefficients in $R$ is central in
$H$ ([[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]]).

**q-contents.** The quantum integers $[m]_q$ for $m\ge0$ are those of
[[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]]; extend the definition to
negative indices by $[-m]_q:=-q^{-m}[m]_q$ for $m>0$, so that
$[m]_q=(q^m-1)/(q-1)$ for all $m\in\mathbb Z$ when $q\ne1$ — indeed for $m=-r<0$
one has $-q^{-r}(q^r-1)/(q-1)=(q^{-r}-1)/(q-1)$ — and $[m]_1=m$ for all
$m\in\mathbb Z$, since $[-r]_1=-[r]_1=-r$. For a standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$
and $1\le k\le n$ let $\operatorname{content}_t(k)=c-r$ be the content of the
node carrying $k$ ([[def-content-vector-of-a-standard-tableau]]) and define the
**q-content value** $[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q$. If $e=e(F,q)<\infty$ for
a field $F$ then $[m+e]_q=[m]_q$ for every $m\in\mathbb Z$
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), so the
q-content value depends only on the residue of the content modulo $e$. At $q=1$
the identification $H_{R,1}(S_n)\cong R[S_n]$ with $T_w\mapsto w$ — the
$R$-linear base change of the specialization isomorphism of
[[prop-group-algebra-and-finite-field-specializations-of-the-generic-hecke-algebra]]
— sends $L_k$ to the ordinary Jucys-Murphy element
$X_k=\sum_{j<k}(j\ k)$
([[def-jucys-murphy-elements-of-the-symmetric-group-algebra]]), because each
coefficient $q^{j-k}$ specializes to $1$, and
$[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_1=\operatorname{content}_t(k)$.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{\times}$, $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$, and let
$L_1,\dots,L_n$ be the Hecke Jucys-Murphy elements
([[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]]). For every $\lambda\vdash n$,
every standard $\lambda$-tableau $t$ and every $1\le k\le n$ there exist
$a_v\in R$ with
$$m_tL_k=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q\,m_t+\sum_{v\rhd t}a_v\,m_v,$$
where $(m_t)_{t\in\mathrm{Std}(\lambda)}$ is the Murphy basis of the Murphy cell
module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$
([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) and the sum is over standard
$\lambda$-tableaux $v$ strictly dominating $t$ in the dominance order on
tableaux ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]],
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]). In particular $L_k$ acts on
the Murphy cell module $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ with Murphy basis $(m_t)$ by a
triangular matrix whose diagonal entries are the q-content values.
Consequently the $L_k$ commute pairwise and every symmetric polynomial in
$L_1,\dots,L_n$ is central in $H$.

[F6] The initial JM eigenidentity is the dominance-maximal case of
[[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]] with the additive
JM elements of [[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]].

1.2 **The initial weight vector and block.** The row-filled tableau $t^\mu$ dominates every standard tableau of its shape at every prefix. Thus the triangular JM formula of [[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]] has no off-diagonal terms at this vector. Star fixes $L_r$, so conversion to the left cell module gives $L_rz_\mu=[c-r]_\xi z_\mu$ for the node $(r,c)$ containing that entry. The multiplicative JM recurrence $X_{a+1}=\xi^{-1}T_aX_aT_a$ and the quadratic relation give $X_a=1+(\xi-1)L_a$: its inductive step is $L_{a+1}=\xi^{-1}T_aL_aT_a+\xi^{-1}T_a$. Hence $X_az_\mu=\xi^{i_a}z_\mu$ by $1+(\xi-1)[m]_\xi=\xi^m$, valid also for negative content. The weight idempotents and $y_a=(1-\xi^{-i_a}X_a)e(i)$ now give $e(i_{t^\mu})z_\mu=z_\mu$ and $y_az_\mu=0$. Since the vectors generated from $z_\mu$ have sequences obtained by permuting its residues, the whole cyclic module lies in content block $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$. [F1, F2, F5, F6, algebra]

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group
with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), with root lattice $Q$,
simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ and integer pairing
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$, and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with generators $E_i,F_i,K_h$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The lattice $P$ plays
the role of the integral weights of the classical theory
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]); the pairing need not
be perfect, and no identification $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$ is
assumed anywhere.

A **$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module** is a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $M$
together with a direct sum decomposition

$$M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$$

(an internal direct sum of $\mathbb Q(q)$-subspaces, only finitely many nonzero
on each vector) such that, for all $\mu\in P$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$,

$$K_h\ \text{acts on}\ M_\mu\ \text{by the scalar}\ q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle},\qquad E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i},\qquad F_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-\alpha_i}.$$

The subspaces $M_\mu$ are the **chosen label-weight spaces**: the grading is
part of the structure and is not reconstructed from the action, because the
pairing may have a kernel. **Morphisms** of $P$-graded type-one weight modules
are the $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module maps $f\colon M\to N$ with
$f(M_\mu)\subseteq N_\mu$ for every $\mu$; the weight submodules and quotients
considered on this page are those with the induced grading (Verification, steps
3.1 and 4.1).

The module is **integrable** if $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent on every
vector: for every $v\in M$ and every $i$ there are integers $N_e(v,i),N_f(v,i)\ge1$
with $E_i^{N_e(v,i)}v=0$ and $F_i^{N_f(v,i)}v=0$. The exponents may depend on
the vector and on $i$, and both directions are required independently;
integrability is not a uniform nilpotence condition.

The following are additional hypotheses, never part of the definition:
finiteness of the dimension of every $M_\mu$; boundedness of the set of $\mu$
with $M_\mu\ne0$ above (or below); finite generation of $M$. The zero module is
a $P$-graded type-one weight module with the empty grading ($M_\mu=0$ for all
$\mu$), and it is integrable.

Two remarks are recorded here and proved below. First, when the pairing
separates $P$, the spaces $M_\mu$ are exactly the simultaneous eigenspaces of
the $K_h$, and the present definition recovers the usual type-one weight
modules (Verification, steps 2.1 and 4.1). Second, when the pairing does not
separate, distinct labels $\mu\ne\mu'$ may carry the same toral character, and
a simultaneous toral eigenspace must not be equated with a single label space;
the definition therefore takes the label grading as data. The regularization of
finite-cone support and all highest-weight comparisons on this page are proved
later, not assumed here by writing $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$.
No choice principle enters this definition.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The **linear
contravariant anti-involution** $\sigma$ of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is defined on
generators by

$$\sigma(q)=q,\qquad\sigma(K_h)=K_h,\qquad\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1},\qquad\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i,$$

extended as an anti-algebra map, $\sigma(xy)=\sigma(y)\sigma(x)$. It is
$\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, preserves the torus (it does not invert it), and is an
involution (Verification, step 1.1). It is distinct from the semilinear
contravariant anti-involution $\tau$ with $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$,
$\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].

Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
so $\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$ for all $i$, and let $(M,v_\lambda)$ be a
**normalized highest weight module**: $M$ is a $P$-graded type-one quantum
weight module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) with
$v_\lambda\in M_\lambda$, $E_iv_\lambda=0$ for all $i$, and $M=U_q(\mathfrak g)v_\lambda$.
(The normalized simple highest weight module $L(\lambda)$ is the companion
construction later on this page; the present definition applies to any
normalized highest weight module, in particular to the Verma module and to its
simple quotient.)

A **contravariant form** on $(M,v_\lambda)$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon M\times M\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(i) $B$ is symmetric: $B(u,v)=B(v,u)$ for all $u,v\in M$;

(ii) $B$ is **homogeneous** for the label grading: $B(M_\mu,M_\tau)=0$
whenever the two labels have different toral characters, that is, whenever
$\langle\mu,h\rangle\ne\langle\tau,h\rangle$ for some $h\in P^{\vee}$;

(iii) $B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$ (the normalization);

(iv) $B$ is $\sigma$-invariant: $B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$ for all
$x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)$ and all $u,v\in M$.

Because $\sigma$ is $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear and fixes the torus, condition (iv)
is equivalent to the adjunction displays

$$B(K_hu,v)=B(u,K_hv),\qquad B(E_iu,v)=B(u,q_iF_iK_i^{-1}v),\qquad B(F_iu,v)=B(u,q_i^{-1}K_iE_iv),$$

for all $u,v\in M$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$ (Verification, step 2.1).

For $\lambda$ dominant and $L(\lambda)$ the normalized simple highest weight
module, such a form exists, is unique, and is nondegenerate on $L(\lambda)$;
moreover distinct label-weight spaces with distinct characters are orthogonal
by (ii). Uniqueness is proved here (Verification, step 4.1), as is the
orthogonality; consequently, when the pairing separates $P$, the distinct
label-weight spaces of $L(\lambda)$ are orthogonal and the restriction of $B$
to each finite-dimensional label-weight space is nondegenerate (Verification,
step 5.1). The
existence, the identification of the radical on the Verma module and the
descent to $L(\lambda)$ are proved in the local Cartan-projection lemma
`lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form`, which
is the declared justification of this definition. That lemma is proved on this
page, and its statement is the supplier of the existence and nondegeneracy
clauses above; establishing those clauses is its content rather than a claim of
this definition.

actual_declared_use_sites.text:
4.2 The exact integral upper basis and the form identification. On the QG standard frame the ambient form is orthonormal. For an addition $\mu=
u+\gamma$ of residue $i$, the node coefficient of $F_i$ is $q^{N_i^r}$, while that of $q^{-1}K_iE_i$ on the reverse edge is $q^{N_i(
u)-1-N_i^l}$. The splitting identity $N_i^r+N_i^l=N_i(
u)-1$ makes them equal ([[def-the-node-order-and-n-i-exponents-for-fock-space]], [[thm-the-fock-space-node-formulas-satisfy-the-quantum-affine-relations]]). The diagonal toral operators are self-adjoint, and symmetry supplies the reverse $E_i$ identity; thus the ambient form is contravariant for $\sigma(F_i)=q^{-1}K_iE_i$ and $\sigma(E_i)=qF_iK_i^{-1}$. Its restriction to the vacuum basic module is normalized by $B(\varnothing,\varnothing)=1$, and uniqueness of the normalized highest-weight contravariant form identifies it with the QG form ([[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]]). The linear relabelling $J$ permutes the orthonormal standard frame and transports the action, so the same identification holds on $M_{\mathrm{sym}}$. Consequently [F3] makes the vectors of step 2.2 the transported upper global basis, free over $A$ in the restricted integral dual lattice and perfectly paired with the lower $A$-span. Their standard-frame coefficients can be rational as in step 3.1; this does not contradict integrality in the upper basis and implies no lower-$A$ selfduality or $A$-unit Gram matrix. [given, F3, step 2.2, step 3.1]

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
For a fixed residue $i$ list the addable and removable $i$-nodes of a partition
**by increasing content** $c-r$; larger content is read as further right or
higher. For an addable $i$-node $\gamma$ of $\lambda$ (so that
$\mu=\lambda+\gamma$) define

$$N_i^r(\lambda,\gamma):=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes of }\lambda\text{ with content}>\text{content}(\gamma)\}-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes of }\lambda\text{ with content}>\text{content}(\gamma)\},$$

and for a removable $i$-node $\gamma$ of $\mu$ (so that
$\lambda=\mu-\gamma$) define $N_i^l(\lambda,\mu)$ by the same formula inside the
smaller diagram $\lambda=\mu-\gamma$ with $>$ replaced by $<$, always excluding
$\gamma$ itself. The node formulas are then

$$F_i|\lambda\rangle=\sum_{\gamma}q^{N_i^r(\lambda,\gamma)}|\lambda+\gamma\rangle,\qquad E_i|\mu\rangle=\sum_{\gamma}q^{-N_i^l(\mu-\gamma,\mu)}|\mu-\gamma\rangle,$$

over the addable respectively removable $i$-nodes. The **node order** is the
content order just fixed, and it is used to define the finite signature
selection: a Chevalley coefficient minimiser is not in general a Kashiwara
arrow, and even a nonzero single Chevalley term can have zero crystal arrow.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the category-$\mathcal O$ suppliers. Fix a finite genuine integral parabolic central summand $\mathcal C$ over $\mathbb C$, with its finite highest-weight structure from [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]. Connectedness is not required. Write $(\Lambda,\preceq)$ for its label poset, $L_\lambda$ for its simples, $\Delta_\lambda$ for its generalized standards, and $\nabla_\lambda=D\Delta_\lambda$ for its costandards. The duality $D$ is exact, contravariant and simple-preserving.

The projective cover $P_\lambda$ and injective envelope $I_\lambda=DP_\lambda$ have exact sequences
$$0\longrightarrow K_\lambda\longrightarrow P_\lambda\longrightarrow\Delta_\lambda\longrightarrow0,\qquad0\longrightarrow\nabla_\lambda\longrightarrow I_\lambda\longrightarrow C_\lambda\longrightarrow0,$$
where $K_\lambda$ has a finite standard flag with labels strictly greater than $\lambda$, and $C_\lambda=DK_\lambda$ has a finite costandard flag with such labels. Generally $I_\lambda$ is larger than $\nabla_\lambda$. Standards have simple heads, costandards simple socles, and their composition labels are $\preceq\lambda$. In this split setting,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=\delta_{\lambda\mu}\mathbb C,\qquad\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=0\quad(j>0),$$
and BGG reciprocity is $(P_\lambda:\Delta_\mu)=[\nabla_\mu:L_\lambda]=[\Delta_\mu:L_\lambda]$. Higher Ext vanishing is justified below from the standard-kernel sequences and the local Hom/$\operatorname{Ext}^1$ statement.

A **finite standard flag** of $N$ is a finite chain $0=N_0\subset N_1\subset\cdots\subset N_r=N$ with sections $\Delta_{\lambda_i}$; a **finite costandard flag** has sections $\nabla_{\lambda_i}$. The zero object has the empty flag. Write $\mathcal F(\Delta)$ and $\mathcal F(\nabla)$ for the corresponding full subcategories. They are exact categories with the short exact sequences inherited from $\mathcal C$, closed under finite sums, extensions and direct summands. Their flag multiplicities are independent of the chosen flag and satisfy
$$(N:\Delta_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(N,\nabla_\lambda),\qquad(M:\nabla_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,M).$$
For arbitrary objects of the fixed finite summand, the equivalent homological criteria are
$$\mathcal F(\Delta)=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^1(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^j(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\},$$
$$\mathcal F(\nabla)=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\}.$$
The duality exchanges the two flag categories. A **tilting object** belongs to their intersection.

An indecomposable tilting object is **normalized at** $\lambda$, and written $T_\lambda$, if it has an inclusion $\Delta_\lambda\hookrightarrow T_\lambda$ whose cokernel is standard-filtered by labels strictly smaller than $\lambda$. Its bottom standard occurs once and $\lambda$ is its unique maximal composition-support label. Such an object, when it exists, is unique up to isomorphism. Existence and classification are supplied later; they are not used to prove the criteria. For a lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing $\lambda$, this same object is normalized tilting in the corresponding Serre subcategory; it is unchanged by the truncation.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the positive biadjoint
residue $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ action of
[[lem-residue-casimir-operators-give-local-affine-hecke-actions]].

At a coincident eigenvalue the completed degenerate affine Hecke algebra on $r$
steps is $\mathrm{Mat}_{r!}$ over the completed symmetric polynomial centre.
The first-$i$ image in its central fibre is $\mathrm{Mat}_{i!}(Z_{i,r})$, where
$$Z_{i,r}=\mathbb C[c_1,\dots,c_i]/(h_{r-i+1},\dots,h_r)$$
(with $c_j$ the elementary symmetric functions of $x_1,\dots,x_i$ and
$\sum_jh_jz^j=(1-c_1z+\cdots+(-1)^ic_iz^i)^{-1}$) is a finite local
complete-intersection Frobenius ring of dimension $\binom{r}{i}$ with
one-dimensional socle. Divided residue functors and the complementary-idempotent
restriction have the corresponding simple head and socle.

Consequently $e_iL(A)$ and $f_iL(A)$ are either $0$ or self-dual
indecomposables with simple isomorphic head and socle labelled
$\tilde e_iA$, respectively $\tilde f_iA$. Vanishing is exactly the absence of
the corresponding crystal edge. This retains the complete residue-translation
crystal claim, not only its $K_0$ action.

$$[M(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)=\sum_{C\sim_{\mathrm{col}}B}(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}P_{d(C)w_0,\,d(A)w_0}(1),$$
where $C$ runs over the column permutations of $B$. This uses singular ordinary
**spherical** coefficients for the entry stabilizer inside finite Levi
cancellation, so it covers mixed singular-ambient/parabolic-Levi blocks. It does
not identify a singular category with genuine parabolic $\mathcal O$ and does
not identify the two polynomial families by an opposite convention.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The exact residue
functors of
[[def-residue-translation-functors-on-the-sum-of-parabolic-o-blocks]] on the
genuine finite-$n$ parabolic blocks have multiplicity-free
generalized-standard flags given by the valid single-entry moves $i\to i+1$ and
$i+1\to i$.

(1) Their $K_0$ operators are the full integrable $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ Fock
Chevalley action, satisfying the integral Chevalley/Serre relations on the
standard basis.

(2) For each simple $L(A)$, a residue translate vanishes exactly when the
corresponding crystal edge is absent; otherwise it is a self-dual
indecomposable with simple equal head and socle $L(\tilde f_iA)$, respectively
$L(\tilde e_iA)$.

(3) The full tensor Fock module is represented by all standard classes; the
ground-state class, with
$M(A_\Lambda)=L(A_\Lambda)=P(A_\Lambda)$, generates only its multiplicity-one
highest constituent.

No action on labels alone proves the $K_0$ relations or the head/socle
statement.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Fix an integer $n\ge0$ and work over $\mathbb C$. Let $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ be
partitions of $n$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]), and let
$S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$ be the tensor product of their complex
Specht modules, a finite-dimensional complex $S_n$-module
([[def-tensor-product-of-complex-representations]],
[[def-column-antisymmetrizer-polytabloid-and-specht-module]]). The
**Kronecker coefficient** $g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ of a third partition
$\nu\vdash n$ is the multiplicity of $S^\nu$ in this tensor product:

$$g(\lambda,\mu,\nu):=\frac{\dim_{\mathbb C}\bigl(S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu\bigr)_{(S^\nu)}}{\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\nu},$$

where $\bigl(S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu\bigr)_{(S^\nu)}$ is the isotypic
component of type $S^\nu$
([[def-isotypic-component-of-a-completely-reducible-representation]]).

**Well-definedness.** The module $S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$ is
finite-dimensional, and $\operatorname{char}\mathbb C=0$ does not divide the
order of the finite group $S_n$, so complex Maschke's theorem gives complete
reducibility
([[thm-maschkes-theorem-for-finite-groups-over-fields-whose-characteristic-does-not-divide-the-group-order]],
[[cor-finite-dimensional-representations-are-completely-reducible-when-char-k-does-not-divide-group-order]],
[[def-completely-reducible-representation]]). The complex Specht modules
$S^\nu$, $\nu\vdash n$, are a complete list of pairwise inequivalent
irreducible $S_n$-modules
([[thm-complex-specht-modules-are-irreducible]],
[[thm-complex-irreducibles-of-symmetric-groups-are-specht-modules]],
[[cor-distinct-specht-modules-are-inequivalent]]). Consequently a decomposition
into irreducibles has the form
$S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu\cong\bigoplus_{\nu\vdash n}m_\nu S^\nu$
with nonnegative integer multiplicities $m_\nu$, and the isotypic component of
type $S^\nu$ is the direct sum of exactly the $m_\nu$ copies of $S^\nu$
appearing in any such decomposition; in particular
$\dim_{\mathbb C}(S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu)_{(S^\nu)}=m_\nu\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\nu$
and $\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\nu>0$ because $S^\nu$ is irreducible. Hence
$g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)=m_\nu$ is a nonnegative integer, independent of the chosen
decomposition, and $g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ is by definition the multiplicity of
$S^\nu$ in $S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$.

**The internal product.** For partitions $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ call
$$(\lambda,\mu)\longmapsto S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$$
the **internal (Kronecker) product** of the $S_n$-representations $S^\lambda$
and $S^\mu$. Unlike the outer induction product
$\operatorname{Ind}_{S_a\times S_b}^{S_{a+b}}(S^\alpha\boxtimes S^\beta)$ of
[[thm-outer-littlewood-richardson-rule]], which takes a pair of modules of
degrees $a$ and $b$ to a module of degree $a+b$, the internal product keeps the
rank: both inputs and the output are $S_n$-modules of the same degree $n$. The
two operations are different constructions on different data; the outer product
is mentioned here only for contrast and is not used in this definition.

No form of the Axiom of Choice is used: the tensor product, Maschke's theorem,
the Specht classification and the isotypic decomposition are finite-dimensional
complex representation theory of a finite group.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a metric space
([[def-metric-space]]) having a neighbourhood basis of contractible open sets at
every point, and let $k$ be a field. Write $k_X$ for its constant sheaf. There
are natural isomorphisms
$$H^q(X,k_X)\cong H^q_{\operatorname{sing}}(X;k)$$
in every degree, where the left side is derived cohomology in the category of
sheaves of $k$-vector spaces (computed with the functorial $k$-linear injective
resolutions supplied by
[[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]; compare
[[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). The same assertion holds on
every open subset of $X$. In particular a nonempty contractible space with this
local property has constant-sheaf cohomology $k$ in degree zero and zero
otherwise. This applies to every finite-polyhedral open star and to its
nonempty intersection with a closed simplex.

actual_declared_use_sites.text: [F11] Under AC, a metric space with a contractible-open neighbourhood basis has actual derived constant-sheaf cohomology equal to singular cohomology ([[lem-locally-contractible-metric-spaces-have-singular-constant-sheaf-cohomology]]).

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module $M$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]) with the induced operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $L/qL$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]). For $b\in B$ write $\mathrm{wt}(b)=\mu$ when $b\in B_\mu$, and define
$$\varepsilon_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde e_i^{\,n}b\neq0\},\qquad \varphi_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde f_i^{\,n}b\neq0\}.$$
Then (see below) both numbers are finite and
$$\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle .$$
The top of the $i$-string through $b$ is the vertex $\tilde e_i^{\,\varepsilon_i(b)}b$, of weight $\mathrm{wt}(b)+\varepsilon_i(b)\alpha_i$; its highest rank-one integer is $\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle+2\varepsilon_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)$.

In the crystal graph of $(L,B)$ the arrows $b\to\tilde f_ib$ are the inverse raising edges: on an existing edge, $\varepsilon_i$ increases by $1$, $\varphi_i$ decreases by $1$ and the weight decreases by $\alpha_i$, and the $i$-chains of $B$ are the finite strings with $\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)+1$ vertices.

For a crystal basis of the negative half $U_q^-$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]) one uses the same arrows and the same finite $\varepsilon_i$, but defines the **formal** $\varphi_i:=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$ as an integer of the abstract root-graded crystal; it may be negative, and it is not the lowering-chain length. The actual lowering-chain length of a negative-half vertex is denoted $\ell_i^-$ and equals $+\infty$, because $\tilde f_i$ is injective there; the negative half is not asserted to be an integrable finite-string module. No choice principle is used.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $M$ be an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) and fix $i\in I$. By [[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]] every $u\in M_\lambda$ has a unique admissible decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}=\ker(E_i)\cap M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i},$$
with $u_n=0$ whenever $n>\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$. Define the **Kashiwara operators**
$$\tilde e_i u:=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_i u:=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}u_n .$$
Both are linear maps on $M$, shifting the label weight by $+\alpha_i$, respectively $-\alpha_i$. Along each string, $\tilde e_i$ moves $F_i^{(n)}u_n$ to $F_i^{(n-1)}u_n$ and kills the top position $n=0$, while $\tilde f_i$ moves it to $F_i^{(n+1)}u_n$ and kills a string exactly at its bottom, where $n=\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(u_n)\rangle$.

Let $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$ be the projections onto the top positions and the bottom positions of these strings:
$$p_{\mathrm{top}}u:=u_0,\qquad p_{\mathrm{bottom}}u:=\sum_{n:\,n=\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n)}u_n .$$
Then
$$\ker\tilde e_i=\ker E_i,\qquad \ker\tilde f_i=\ker F_i,\qquad \tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{top}},\qquad \tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{bottom}},$$
so $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ are inverse to each other on each existing string edge. Module homomorphisms commute with both operators, $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$. On $\ker E_i$ one has $\tilde f_i=F_i$, and on $\ker F_i$ one has $\tilde e_i=E_i$. At interior positions the operators differ from the generators: in the rank-one module $L_i(2)$ with highest vector $v$ and $u=F_iv$, one has $F_iu=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$ while $\tilde f_iu=F_i^{(2)}v$, and $[2]_i\neq1$. No choice principle is used. The analogous Kashiwara operators on the negative half $U_q^-$ are the shifts of its unique $e_i'$-string decomposition ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), constructed using the skew derivation of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]. Their strings have no bottom: $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ and $\tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-P_i$, where $P_i$ projects onto $\ker e_i'$; the second identity follows by subtracting the position-zero coefficient $u_0=P_iu$ from the string expansion. These string-shift operators are distinct from the skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$. No negative-half operator is used in the module verification below.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $B_1$ and $B_2$ be crystals, meaning the data $(B,wt,\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i,\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i)$ attached to a crystal basis $(L,B)$ of an integrable module by [[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]] and [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $wt:B\to P$ is the weight function, $\varepsilon_i(b)=\max\{n:\tilde e_i^nb\ne0\}$ and $\varphi_i(b)=\max\{n:\tilde f_i^nb\ne0\}$ are finite, $\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,wt(b)\rangle$, and $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ are the partial maps $B\to B\cup\{0\}$ of [[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]].

The **tensor product crystal** $B_1\otimes B_2$ is the following data on $B_1\times B_2$, whose elements are written $b_1\otimes b_2$:

(i) $wt(b_1\otimes b_2):=wt(b_1)+wt(b_2)$;

(ii) $\tilde f_i(b_1\otimes b_2):=\tilde f_ib_1\otimes b_2$ if $\varphi_i(b_1)>\varepsilon_i(b_2)$, and $\tilde f_i(b_1\otimes b_2):=b_1\otimes\tilde f_ib_2$ if $\varphi_i(b_1)\le\varepsilon_i(b_2)$;

(iii) $\tilde e_i(b_1\otimes b_2):=\tilde e_ib_1\otimes b_2$ if $\varphi_i(b_1)\ge\varepsilon_i(b_2)$, and $\tilde e_i(b_1\otimes b_2):=b_1\otimes\tilde e_ib_2$ if $\varphi_i(b_1)<\varepsilon_i(b_2)$.

By convention a product is $0$ as soon as the operator applied to the selected factor is $0$; the **left factor is preferred** exactly in the displayed cases, so the assignment is left-to-right, matching the left-to-right order of the module tensor product $M_1\otimes M_2$ under the coproduct of [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. The **equality case** $\varphi_i(b_1)=\varepsilon_i(b_2)$ is split: $\tilde e_i$ acts on the first factor while $\tilde f_i$ acts on the second. The asymmetry is not free: with the same strict or non-strict comparison used for both operators the partial-inverse axiom fails, as the counterexample on the companion page records, while the displayed convention is internally consistent by the lemma on this page computing $\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i$ of $B_1\otimes B_2$.

The functions $\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i$ of $B_1\otimes B_2$ are read off from the two-case operators as maximal iterated powers, exactly as in [[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]]. This definition only fixes combinatorial data and asserts nothing about an arbitrary pair of crystals: it does not claim that every such datum arises from a module tensor product. When $B_1,B_2$ are the crystals of crystal bases of integrable modules, the tensor product theorem later on this page proves that $(L_1\otimes_{A_0}L_2,\,B_1\otimes B_2)$ is a crystal basis of $M_1\otimes M_2$ with these operators, and only through that theorem are the values finite and nonnegative a priori. No choice principle is used.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
Let $M_1,M_2$ be integrable chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight modules with crystal bases $(L_1,B_1)$, $(L_2,B_2)$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]), and let $M_1\otimes M_2$ be the integrable module of [[lem-tensor-products-of-integrable-weight-modules-are-integrable]].

Then $(L_1\otimes_{A_0}L_2,\,B_1\otimes B_2)$ is a crystal basis of $M_1\otimes M_2$, and its crystal is the tensor product crystal $B_1\otimes B_2$ of [[def-tensor-product-of-crystals]]: for all $b_1\in B_1$, $b_2\in B_2$ and $i\in I$,

$$\tilde f_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=\begin{cases}\tilde f_ib_1\otimes b_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)>\varepsilon_i(b_2),\\ b_1\otimes\tilde f_ib_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)\le\varepsilon_i(b_2),\end{cases}\qquad \tilde e_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=\begin{cases}\tilde e_ib_1\otimes b_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)\ge\varepsilon_i(b_2),\\ b_1\otimes\tilde e_ib_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)<\varepsilon_i(b_2),\end{cases}$$

with value $0$ as soon as the selected factor maps to $0$. In particular $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ map $B_1\otimes B_2$ into $(B_1\otimes B_2)\cup\{0\}$, and for all $b,b'\in B_1\otimes B_2$ one has $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$, so the partial-inverse axiom holds. The equality case $\varphi_i(b_1)=\varepsilon_i(b_2)$ is resolved as in the definition: $\tilde f_i$ acts on the second factor and $\tilde e_i$ on the first.

No finite dimensionality, bounded support or uniform nilpotence is assumed, and no choice principle is used.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
Let $\mathbb{N} = \omega$ be the von Neumann naturals, with $0 = \varnothing$ and
$\sigma(n) = n \cup \{n\}$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), and let $\le$ and $<$ be
the order defined additively by $m \le n \iff \exists k \in \mathbb{N}\ (m + k = n)$
and $m < n \iff (m \le n$ and $m \ne n)$ ([[def-nat-order]]). Then $\mathbb{N}$ is
a **transitive set**: every element of a natural number is itself a natural
number. Moreover, for all $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$:

1. $m < n \iff m \in n$;
2. $m \le n \iff m \subseteq n$;
3. $n < \sigma(n)$, and $m < \sigma(n) \iff m \le n$;
4. $0 \le n$, and $0 \in n$ whenever $n \ne 0$.

Consequently $n = \{\, m \in \mathbb{N} : m < n \,\}$ for every $n$: a natural
number is exactly the set of the naturals below it.

**Why this is proved here.** [[def-nat-order]] defines the order additively and
records the identification with membership only as an orienting remark, without
proof. The countability arguments on this page use that identification as a
working fact, so it is established here, from the additive order and induction
alone. Nothing below uses ordinals or any later material.

actual_declared_use_sites.text: [F10] For naturals: $n<\sigma(n)$ for every $n$, and $n=\{m\in\mathbb{N}:m<n\}$ ([[lem-nat-order-is-membership]]).

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $X$ be a topological space, let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf of $k$-vector
spaces (or of abelian groups) on $X$
([[def-presheaf-on-topological-space]]), let $U\subseteq X$ be open and let
$s\in\mathcal F(U)$. The **support of $s$** is
$$\operatorname{Supp}(s):=\{\,x\in U: s_x\neq 0\,\}\subseteq U,$$
where $s_x\in\mathcal F_x$ denotes the germ of $s$ at $x$ in the stalk
$\mathcal F_x$ ([[def-stalk-of-presheaf]], [[def-germ-of-section]]). A section
$s\in\mathcal F(X)$ is **compactly supported** when its support is a compact
subspace of $X$ ([[def-compact-space]]). For a subspace $Z\subseteq X$ and a
presheaf $\mathcal G$ on $Z$, the support of $t\in\mathcal G(Z)$ is defined by
the same condition using the stalks of $\mathcal G$. The support is not assumed
closed in $X$ nor compact.

When $\mathcal F$ is a **sheaf** of $k$-vector spaces the following three
consistency facts hold; they are immediate consequences of the definitions
above and are recorded here because every later compact-support statement uses
them.

1. $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$ is closed in $U$. Indeed, if $x\notin
   \operatorname{Supp}(s)$ then $s_x=0$ in the stalk; equality of germs means
   that $s$ and the zero section agree on some open neighbourhood $W\subseteq U$
   of $x$ ([[def-germ-of-section]]), so $s$ vanishes on the open neighbourhood
   $W$ of $x$, and $U\setminus\operatorname{Supp}(s)$ is therefore open in $U$.
2. $\operatorname{Supp}(s)=\varnothing$ if and only if $s=0$. If every germ of
   $s$ is zero then $s=0$ by the locality axiom of a sheaf applied to the cover
   of $U$ by its open subsets ([[lem-section-zero-if-all-germs-zero]]); the
   converse is immediate, since the zero section has zero germ at every point.
3. $\operatorname{Supp}(s|_V)=\operatorname{Supp}(s)\cap V$ for every open
   $V\subseteq U$. Restriction is compatible with the germ maps, so
   $(s|_V)_x=s_x$ for every $x\in V$ ([[def-germ-of-section]]).

Since $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$ is closed in $U$ by fact 1, a section whose
support is contained in some compact subset of $X$ is compactly supported: a
closed subset of a compact space is compact. Fact 1 is closedness in $U$ only,
and nothing here asserts that the support is closed in $X$ or that $U$ is
closed. No choice principle is used anywhere: germs, stalks, supports and
restrictions are elementary.

actual_declared_use_sites.text: 1.5 Composition of proper-support direct images. The support definition gives $(gf)_!=g_!f_!$: a section whose support is proper over $Z$ has support proper over $Y$ because the inverse image of a compact $L\subseteq Y$ is a closed subset of the inverse image of the compact $g(L)$ by [F4], and conversely a support locally proper over $Y$ with proper image over $Z$ has compact preimages of compacta in $Z$. The support of $f_!s$ is $f(\operatorname{Supp}s)$ by the fibre-stalk identity [F1] and local properness, so the two descriptions are inverse. Direct images of globally $c$-soft sheaves by $f_!$ are $c$-soft: a section over a compact base set is represented on a neighbourhood by [F6], its total support over that compact set is compact by properness of the representing support, and enclosing it in a relatively compact $W$, the support-controlled $c$-soft extension of [F3] supported in $W$ pushes forward and extends the original section over the compact set. Thus $f_!$ sends injectives to $g_!$-acyclic sheaves, and applying the two ordinary support functors to an injective resolution gives the canonical derived composition $R(gf)_!=Rg_!Rf_!$; the same comparison proves associativity for triples, the section support bijection being literally associative. required_interface.text:
Let $K\subseteq X$ be a compact subset ([[def-compact-space]]) of a locally
compact Hausdorff space ([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]),
let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on $X$
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]]) and let $i:K\hookrightarrow X$ be the
inclusion. Then the canonical map
$$\varinjlim_{U\supseteq K,\ U\ \text{open}}\mathcal F(U)\longrightarrow\Gamma(K,i^{-1}\mathcal F)=(i^{-1}\mathcal F)(K)$$
is an isomorphism of $k$-vector spaces. Moreover, for pairwise disjoint compact
subsets $K_1,\dots,K_m\subseteq X$ and sections $s_j\in\mathcal F(U_j)$ over open
neighbourhoods $U_j$ of the respective $K_j$, there are an open neighbourhood $U$
of $K_1\cup\dots\cup K_m$ and a section $s\in\mathcal F(U)$, together with, for
every $j$, an open neighbourhood $W_j\subseteq U_j$ of $K_j$ with
$s|_{W_j}=s_j|_{W_j}$; in particular the zero section can be prescribed on any
compact set disjoint from the given one. The isomorphism is $k$-linear, and no
choice principle is used: every selection in the proof is made from finitely
many nonempty sets.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Fix an integer $n\ge0$ and work over $\mathbb C$. Let $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ be
partitions of $n$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]), and let
$S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$ be the tensor product of their complex
Specht modules, a finite-dimensional complex $S_n$-module
([[def-tensor-product-of-complex-representations]],
[[def-column-antisymmetrizer-polytabloid-and-specht-module]]). The
**Kronecker coefficient** $g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ of a third partition
$\nu\vdash n$ is the multiplicity of $S^\nu$ in this tensor product:

$$g(\lambda,\mu,\nu):=\frac{\dim_{\mathbb C}\bigl(S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu\bigr)_{(S^\nu)}}{\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\nu},$$

where $\bigl(S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu\bigr)_{(S^\nu)}$ is the isotypic
component of type $S^\nu$
([[def-isotypic-component-of-a-completely-reducible-representation]]).

**Well-definedness.** The module $S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$ is
finite-dimensional, and $\operatorname{char}\mathbb C=0$ does not divide the
order of the finite group $S_n$, so complex Maschke's theorem gives complete
reducibility
([[thm-maschkes-theorem-for-finite-groups-over-fields-whose-characteristic-does-not-divide-the-group-order]],
[[cor-finite-dimensional-representations-are-completely-reducible-when-char-k-does-not-divide-group-order]],
[[def-completely-reducible-representation]]). The complex Specht modules
$S^\nu$, $\nu\vdash n$, are a complete list of pairwise inequivalent
irreducible $S_n$-modules
([[thm-complex-specht-modules-are-irreducible]],
[[thm-complex-irreducibles-of-symmetric-groups-are-specht-modules]],
[[cor-distinct-specht-modules-are-inequivalent]]). Consequently a decomposition
into irreducibles has the form
$S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu\cong\bigoplus_{\nu\vdash n}m_\nu S^\nu$
with nonnegative integer multiplicities $m_\nu$, and the isotypic component of
type $S^\nu$ is the direct sum of exactly the $m_\nu$ copies of $S^\nu$
appearing in any such decomposition; in particular
$\dim_{\mathbb C}(S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu)_{(S^\nu)}=m_\nu\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\nu$
and $\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\nu>0$ because $S^\nu$ is irreducible. Hence
$g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)=m_\nu$ is a nonnegative integer, independent of the chosen
decomposition, and $g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ is by definition the multiplicity of
$S^\nu$ in $S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$.

**The internal product.** For partitions $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ call
$$(\lambda,\mu)\longmapsto S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$$
the **internal (Kronecker) product** of the $S_n$-representations $S^\lambda$
and $S^\mu$. Unlike the outer induction product
$\operatorname{Ind}_{S_a\times S_b}^{S_{a+b}}(S^\alpha\boxtimes S^\beta)$ of
[[thm-outer-littlewood-richardson-rule]], which takes a pair of modules of
degrees $a$ and $b$ to a module of degree $a+b$, the internal product keeps the
rank: both inputs and the output are $S_n$-modules of the same degree $n$. The
two operations are different constructions on different data; the outer product
is mentioned here only for contrast and is not used in this definition.

No form of the Axiom of Choice is used: the tensor product, Maschke's theorem,
the Specht classification and the isotypic decomposition are finite-dimensional
complex representation theory of a finite group.

actual_declared_use_sites.text:
For all partitions $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ one has the finite nonnegative
expansion
$$\bar g^\gamma_{\alpha,\beta} =\sum_{\mu,\lambda,\eta,\rho,\theta,\pi} c^\gamma_{\mu,\theta,\pi}\,c^\alpha_{\rho,\lambda,\theta}\, c^\beta_{\rho,\eta,\pi}\,g^\mu_{\lambda,\eta},$$
the sum over all six-tuples of partitions (only finitely many summands are
nonzero), where the $c$'s are the threefold Schur coefficients
([[def-iterated-schur-coefficients]]) and the $g$'s are the ordinary Kronecker
coefficients ([[def-kronecker-coefficient-and-internal-tensor-product]]).

[F4] The Schur basis is orthonormal ([[thm-schur-functions-form-an-orthonormal-integral-basis]]), the coefficients $c$ and $g$ are nonnegative integers, and $c^\lambda_{\mu
u}=0$ unless $\mu\subseteq\lambda$ and $|\lambda|=|\mu|+|
u|$, while $g^\lambda_{\mu
u}=0$ unless $|\lambda|=|\mu|=|
u|$ ([[def-littlewood-richardson-tableau-and-coefficient]], [[thm-littlewood-richardson-schur-product-expansion]], [[def-kronecker-coefficient-and-internal-tensor-product]]).

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X,Y$ be locally compact Hausdorff spaces
([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]). Write
$\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]])
viewed as modules over the constant ring sheaf $k_X$, and form derived
categories in those sheaves ([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]).
For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$, set $f^*=f^{-1}$
([[def-inverse-image-presheaf-and-sheaf]]) and define $f_!F$ on an open
$V\subseteq Y$ to consist of the sections of $F$ on $f^{-1}(V)$ whose closed
support ([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]],
[[def-compactly-supported-global-sections]]) maps properly to $V$, properness
being that of [[def-proper-continuous-map]] together with its stability lemma
[[lem-proper-continuous-map-stability]]. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]),
$Rf_*$ and $Rf_!$ are computed on bounded-below $k$-linear injective
replacements. Tensor means the signed total tensor over $k$
([[def-sheaf-tensor-product]]) and internal derived Hom is the injective
construction of
[[lem-bounded-analytic-field-sheaves-have-derived-tensor-hom-and-pullback-pushforward-adjunctions]]
([[def-sheaf-hom]]).

Suppose the uniform all-fibre-open cohomological dimension bound of
[[lem-finite-fibre-dimension-gives-bounded-fibrewise-soft-resolutions]] holds,
and choose its finite resolution $k_X\to K$; for an open $U\subseteq X$ put
$K_U=j_{U!}j_U^*K$ ([[def-extension-by-zero-abelian-sheaf]],
[[def-c-soft-sheaf]]). For a bounded-below injective complex $I$ on $Y$,
define the exceptional inverse-image candidate to be the sheaf complex with
open sections $\operatorname{Hom}_Y^\bullet(f_!K_U,I)$.
[[thm-compactly-supported-derived-pushforward-has-exceptional-inverse-image-adjoint]]
proves that this candidate is a sheaf complex and is independent of the chosen
resolution. Set $\omega_X=a_X^!k$ and $D_XA=R\mathcal Hom(A,\omega_X)$ when the
terminal map satisfies the same finite-dimensional hypotheses. Constructible
restriction is a separate geometric theorem; none of these definitions asserts
a generic six-functor axiom.

The prescriptions are those of Verdier's exposé: $f^*$ is the exact inverse
image, $f_!$ is the sheaf of sections whose closed support is proper over the
base — a presheaf by the local nature of properness, whose sheaf property on
bounded-below injective inputs is proved by the exceptional-adjoint theorem
recorded in `justified_by` — $Rf_*$ is derived from the direct image
[[def-direct-image-sheaf]] on bounded-below injective replacements, and the
terms of the chosen finite resolution are $c$-soft and hence acyclic for
compact support ([[lem-c-soft-field-sheaves-are-compact-support-acyclic]]).
The ordinary-operations lemma also supplies the flasque acyclicity
([[def-flasque-sheaf]]) used to compare resolutions. AC is used only for
injective replacements; the proper-support sections, extension by zero and the
exceptional candidate itself are choice-free constructions. Cohomological
shifts obey $H^i(A[r])=H^{i+r}(A)$ in the convention of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

The all-sheaf compact-support bound on every open in a finite deleted-boundary fibre model is [[lem-finite-polyhedral-covering-dimension-bounds-all-sheaf-cohomology]].

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $P=|K|$ be the realization of a finite abstract
simplicial complex $K$ of dimension $d$ (a finite compact polyhedron of
dimension $d$), and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $P$
([[def-geometric-realization-of-an-abstract-simplicial-complex]],
[[def-locally-finite-and-finite-dimensional-simplicial-complex]],
[[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]]); every clause applies to sheaves of
$k$-vector spaces. Then:

1. $H^q(P,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $q>d$
   ([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]);
2. for every open subspace $U\subseteq P$ and every sheaf $\mathcal E$ of
   abelian groups on $U$, one has $H^q_c(U,\mathcal E)=0$ for every $q>d$
   ([[def-compactly-supported-global-sections]]);
3. more generally, the same conclusions hold for every compact Hausdorff space
   in which every open cover admits a finite open refinement of order at most
   $d+1$ --- that is, a finite refinement such that every point lies in at most
   $d+1$ of its members --- and for every open subspace of such a space.

These bounds concern arbitrary sheaves, not merely cellular, constructible or
coherent ones. If $L\subseteq K$ is a subcomplex, then $|L|$ is closed in $P$,
the complement $P\setminus|L|$ is open, and every open subspace of
$P\setminus|L|$ is an open subspace of $P$; this is the fibre model on which
the bound is applied.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld-Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), with skew derivations
$e_i',e_i''$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]),
and let $(\ ,\ )$ be a bilinear form on $U_q^-$.

(i) **Existence and symmetry.** A bilinear form with $(1,1)=1$ and
$(F_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'(Q))$ for all $i,P,Q$ exists on $U_q^-$; every normalized
homogeneous form satisfying these conditions is symmetric; and by the
uniqueness of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]
there is exactly one such form. No separate right-adjunction formula for
$(P,QF_i)$ is asserted: in the rank-one subalgebra a formula
$(P,QF_i)=c\,(e_i''P,Q)$ with constant $c$ is false, as the explicit values in
(iv) show.

(ii) **Orthogonality.** $(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu])=0$ whenever $\nu\ne\mu$.

(iii) **Nondegeneracy.** For every $0\ne x\in U_q^-$ there is $y\in U_q^-$ with
$(x,y)\ne0$; equivalently, the restriction of the form to each
finite-dimensional graded piece $U_q^-[-\nu]$ is nondegenerate.

(iv) **Integrality on the word lattice.** Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]) and let $W\subseteq U_A^-$ be the
$A$-span of the monomials $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_k}$ ($k\ge0$). Then
$W\subseteq U_A^-$ (because $F_i^k=[k]_i!F_i^{(k)}$ and $[k]_i!\in A$), and
$(W,W)\subseteq A$. On the larger divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ the form is
*not* $A$-valued: in the rank-one subalgebra generated by a single $F_i$ one
has, for all $a,b\ge0$,
$$(F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)})=\delta_{ab}\frac{q_i^{-a(a-1)/2}}{[a]_i!}=\delta_{ab}\frac{1}{[a]_{q_i^2}!},$$

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_k)$ be a partition with $|\alpha|=\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_k$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]), and let $n\ge0$ be
an integer. Whenever

$$n\;\ge\;|\alpha|+\alpha_1,$$

define the **first-row padding** of $\alpha$ to size $n$ to be
$$\alpha[n]:=\bigl(n-|\alpha|,\ \alpha_1,\ \alpha_2,\ \dots,\ \alpha_k\bigr).$$

The threshold is exact.

**Above the threshold.** Suppose $n\ge|\alpha|+\alpha_1$. Then
$n-|\alpha|\ge\alpha_1\ge0$, so every entry of the displayed sequence is a
nonnegative integer, the entries sum to $(n-|\alpha|)+|\alpha|=n$, and the
sequence is weakly decreasing because $n-|\alpha|\ge\alpha_1$ and $\alpha$ is
weakly decreasing ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).
If $\alpha$ is nonempty then $\alpha_1\ge1$, hence $n-|\alpha|\ge1$ and the
displayed sequence is a partition of $n$ with positive parts. If
$\alpha=\varnothing$ then the displayed sequence is $(n)$; this is a partition
of $n$ for every $n\ge1$, while for $n=0$ one takes $\varnothing[0]:=\varnothing$,
the unique partition of $0$. Thus the padding is defined and is a partition of
$n$ on the whole displayed range.

**Below the threshold.** If $\alpha$ is nonempty and $n<|\alpha|+\alpha_1$,
then $n-|\alpha|<\alpha_1$; if also $n\ge|\alpha|$ the leading entry is
nonnegative but smaller than the second entry $\alpha_1$, and if $n<|\alpha|$
it is negative. In both cases the displayed sequence is not a partition, so
$\alpha[n]$ is left undefined. The threshold $|\alpha|+\alpha_1$ is therefore
the exact size at which the padded family begins: at
$n=|\alpha|+\alpha_1$ the padding equals $(\alpha_1,\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\dots)$,
which is a partition with a repeated first part when $\alpha$ is nonempty.

**Neutrality of the notation.** This definition records a family of partitions;
it asserts no constancy of any quantity along the family and no stability
property. The same notation is used by the FI-module and
representation-stability developments, where the padding threshold reappears as
the generation degree of the family under consideration.

required_interface.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces and let $k$ be a field. Inverse image of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[def-inverse-image-presheaf-and-sheaf]]) is exact and $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, where $Rf_*$ is computed on bounded-below $k$-linear injective replacements ([[lem-bounded-below-complexes-admit-injective-replacements]], [[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]]). For bounded complexes $A,B$ ([[def-bounded-bounded-below-and-bounded-above-complex]]) the derived tensor over $k$ is their signed total tensor ([[def-sheaf-tensor-product]]), and for bounded $A$ and bounded-below $B$ the derived internal Hom $R\mathcal Hom(A,B)$ is computed by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(A,I_B)$ in a $k$-linear bounded-below injective model $B\to I_B$ ([[def-sheaf-hom]], [[def-derived-hom-in-the-bounded-setting]]). Flasque $k$-sheaves ([[def-flasque-sheaf]]) are acyclic for sections on every open set ([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). The tensor-Hom adjunction and the dg associativity, evaluation and symmetry identities are natural. No bounded-constructibility claim for the internal Hom is made here; that requires the local geometric supplier of the later constructible items.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
For every commutative ring $R$ and $q\in R^\times$:

1. $\theta(T_i):=(q-1)-T_i=-qT_i^{-1}$ extends uniquely to an involutive
$R$-algebra automorphism $\theta$ of $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$, with
$\theta(T_w)=(-q)^{\ell(w)}T_{w^{-1}}^{-1}$; $\theta$ commutes with the star
anti-involution $*$ and is compatible with every base change.

2. For a right $H$-module $M$, the pullback $M^\theta$ (same underlying
$R$-module, action $m\cdot h:=m\theta(h)$) is a right $H$-module; $(-)^\theta$
is exact, preserves submodules, quotients, finite composition multiplicities and
simplicity, and $(M^\theta)^\theta=M$.

3. The star-contragredient $M^\circ:=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)$ with
$(f\cdot h)(m):=f(mh^*)$ is a right $H$-module; for finite free $M$ it is finite
free of the same rank, $(-)^\circ$ commutes with base change, and
$(M^\theta)^\circ=(M^\circ)^\theta$.

4. For every partition $\lambda\vdash n$, if $w_0(S_\lambda)$ is the longest
element of the row subgroup, then
$$\theta(x_\lambda)=q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}y_\lambda,\qquad \theta(y_\lambda)=q^{-\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}x_\lambda.$$
In particular $\theta(x_\lambda)$ and $y_\lambda$ differ by the unit
$q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}$, and this unit factor must be carried through every
form comparison. At $q=1$, $\theta$ is the pullback along the sign automorphism
$w\mapsto\operatorname{sgn}(w)w$ of $R[S_n]$.

No choice principle is used.
