Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^\times$ and $\lambda\vdash n$, and write $\mu=\lambda'$, $L=\ell(w_\lambda)$ and $N=\ell(w_0(S_{\lambda'}))$. Let $P(\lambda)=z_\lambda H$ with its DJ form $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$, the cell module $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ with its Murphy form $G_{\lambda'}$, and the sign automorphism $\theta$ be as in [[def-dj-bridge-row-column-permutation-modules-and-polytabloids]], [[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]] and [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]], and let $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta$ be the $\theta$-twisted cell module of [[lem-dj-bridge-theta-transport-of-the-cellular-structure]]. Then:

1. There is a base-change compatible isomorphism of right $H$-modules $$\Phi_\lambda\colon P(\lambda)\longrightarrow C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta,\qquad \Phi_\lambda(z_\lambda)=m_0,\quad \Phi_\lambda(z_\lambda h)=m_0\theta(h)\ \ (h\in H),$$ where $m_0$ is the class of $x_{\lambda'}$ in $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ and the right side is computed with the ordinary action on $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ and read in the twist; in particular $\Phi_\lambda(e_t)=m_0\theta(T_{d_{\lambda'}(t)})$ for $t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda')$. For a class $m\in C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ and any lift $\widetilde m\in M(\lambda')$, the inverse is $\Phi_\lambda^{-1}(m)=q^{-N}x_\lambda T_{w_\lambda}\theta(\widetilde m)$, independently of the chosen lift.

2. With $G_{\lambda'}^\theta$ the transported form of [[lem-dj-bridge-theta-transport-of-the-cellular-structure]] and $u_\lambda(q):=q^{\ell(w_0(S_{\lambda'}))-\ell(w_\lambda)}\in A^\times$, $$G_{\lambda'}^\theta(\Phi_\lambda x,\Phi_\lambda y)=u_\lambda(q)\,\beta_{P(\lambda)}(x,y)\qquad(x,y\in P(\lambda)),$$ over every commutative $R$ with $q\in R^\times$. No unnamed scalar and no potentially vanishing scalar occurs: $u_\lambda$ is the explicit unit $q^{N-L}$ in the fixed normalizations of this page.

3. Consequently $\Phi_\lambda$ maps the radical of $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$ onto the radical of $G_{\lambda'}^\theta$, the induced map between the quotients is an isomorphism, with the corresponding cell-form quotients $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}\cong(D^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^\theta$, including the zero-quotient case. Over a field, when the quotients are nonzero they are the simple heads; when the forms are identically zero, the displayed quotients are zero and no assertion about the actual module heads is made. Over a PID with a chosen prime, the unit-scaled form identity preserves all divisibility submodules and their reductions. One also obtains $P(\lambda')\cong P(\lambda)^{\circ,\theta}$ with the exact position of the dual and the twist, separating same-shape duality from conjugate-sign transport. No choice principle is used.

Let $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_k)$ be a partition with $|\alpha|=\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_k$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]), and let $n\ge0$ be
an integer. Whenever

$$n\;\ge\;|\alpha|+\alpha_1,$$

define the **first-row padding** of $\alpha$ to size $n$ to be
$$\alpha[n]:=\bigl(n-|\alpha|,\ \alpha_1,\ \alpha_2,\ \dots,\ \alpha_k\bigr).$$

The threshold is exact.

**Above the threshold.** Suppose $n\ge|\alpha|+\alpha_1$. Then
$n-|\alpha|\ge\alpha_1\ge0$, so every entry of the displayed sequence is a
nonnegative integer, the entries sum to $(n-|\alpha|)+|\alpha|=n$, and the
sequence is weakly decreasing because $n-|\alpha|\ge\alpha_1$ and $\alpha$ is
weakly decreasing ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).
If $\alpha$ is nonempty then $\alpha_1\ge1$, hence $n-|\alpha|\ge1$ and the
displayed sequence is a partition of $n$ with positive parts. If
$\alpha=\varnothing$ then the displayed sequence is $(n)$; this is a partition
of $n$ for every $n\ge1$, while for $n=0$ one takes $\varnothing[0]:=\varnothing$,
the unique partition of $0$. Thus the padding is defined and is a partition of
$n$ on the whole displayed range.

**Below the threshold.** If $\alpha$ is nonempty and $n<|\alpha|+\alpha_1$,
then $n-|\alpha|<\alpha_1$; if also $n\ge|\alpha|$ the leading entry is
nonnegative but smaller than the second entry $\alpha_1$, and if $n<|\alpha|$
it is negative. In both cases the displayed sequence is not a partition, so
$\alpha[n]$ is left undefined. The threshold $|\alpha|+\alpha_1$ is therefore
the exact size at which the padded family begins: at
$n=|\alpha|+\alpha_1$ the padding equals $(\alpha_1,\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\dots)$,
which is a partition with a repeated first part when $\alpha$ is nonempty.

**Neutrality of the notation.** This definition records a family of partitions;
it asserts no constancy of any quantity along the family and no stability
property. The same notation is used by the FI-module and
representation-stability developments, where the padding threshold reappears as
the generation degree of the family under consideration.

Use the standard graded cyclotomic quotient of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], and keep the conventions
fixed there: the cyclotomic relation is imposed on the FIRST strand and
cyclotomic induction appends strands on the RIGHT. Fix $\beta\in Q_+$ and a
color $i$; put
$$A:=R^\Lambda(\beta),\qquad B:=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i),\qquad e:=e(\beta,i),$$
where $e(\beta,i)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu i)\in R(\beta+\alpha_i)$ is the
idempotent of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]
supported on the sequences ending in $i$.

**The right-append corner homomorphism.** Right append defines a
$k$-algebra homomorphism
$$\iota_i:A\longrightarrow eBe,\qquad 1_A\longmapsto e,\quad e(\nu)\longmapsto e(\nu i),\quad x_a\longmapsto x_a,\quad \tau_a\longmapsto\tau_a ,$$
sending each old dot or crossing to the same-named generator at the same
position in the first $|\beta|$ strands of $R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$ and
each old idempotent to the longer idempotent obtained by appending $i$. It is
a graded homomorphism of degree zero: each generic relation (1)-(7) of
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] is preserved
under right append, and the first-strand cyclotomic generator of $A$ maps to
the first-strand cyclotomic generator of $B$, so the cyclotomic relation is
preserved and $\iota_i$ is well defined on the quotient. The unit is sent to
the corner unit $e$, not to a global unit of $B$; it is **not** asserted that
$\iota_i$ is injective, and $e$ is allowed to be zero.

**The functors.** On graded left modules define
$$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M):=Be\otimes_A M,\qquad E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N):=eN,$$
the tensor over the graded balanced tensor product of
[[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]] and the idempotent
restriction of the graded $B$-module $N$
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]). Both are additive
$k$-linear functors between the graded module categories, they preserve
degree-zero maps, and they extend to direct sums over the root degrees
$\beta\in Q_+$.

**Adjunction, weights and shifts.** Evaluation at $e$ identifies
$\operatorname{HOM}_B(Be,N)$ with $eN$ by the degree-zero tensor--Hom
adjunction, giving $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ with its
actual grading. The functor $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ increases ROOT degree by
$\alpha_i$, taking modules at root $\beta$ to modules at root
$\beta+\alpha_i$, and decreases the module weight $\Lambda-\beta$ by
$\alpha_i$; restriction does the reverse. Both composites are endofunctors at
a fixed root degree. Grading shifts satisfy
$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M\{r\})\cong F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M)\{r\}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N\{r\})\cong E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N)\{r\}$, using the
internal shifts of [[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]].

**Ungraded monic deformations.** For a general monic
specialization $a_j(u)$ the quotient $R^\Lambda_a(\beta)$ of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] carries no grading, and
the same formulas define the ungraded functors $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$; no graded statement is asserted on that branch.

**Status of further structure.** Exactness, preservation of projectives and a
shifted second adjunction are theorems below, not part of this definition; in
particular no unshifted right adjunction $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv
F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ is asserted here, and the explicit shift of the second
adjunction is supplied by the coherent-biadjunction lemma of this page. This
definition uses no choice.

required_interface.text:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $z\in A$ be a unit. Fix an integer
$n\ge0$.

**The nondegenerate affine presentation.** The algebra
$H_n^{\mathrm{aff}}(A;z)$ is the $A$-algebra presented by commuting units
$X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$
([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]],
[[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]) subject to
$$T_r^2=(z-1)T_r+z,\qquad T_rT_{r+1}T_r=T_{r+1}T_rT_{r+1},\qquad T_rT_s=T_sT_r\quad(|r-s|>1),$$
$$T_rX_rT_r=zX_{r+1},\qquad T_rX_s=X_sT_r\quad(s\notin\{r,r+1\}),$$
the last two relations being the Bernstein relation and the distant mixed
commutation, and with $T_r$ invertible as a consequence of its quadratic
relation. For $n=0$ the algebra is $A$.

**The degenerate affine presentation.** The algebra
$H_n^{\deg}(A)$ is the $A$-algebra presented by commuting generators
$x_1,\dots,x_n$ and symmetric-group generators $s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}$ subject to
the Coxeter relations $s_r^2=1$, $s_rs_{r+1}s_r=s_{r+1}s_rs_{r+1}$,
$s_rs_t=s_ts_r$ for $|r-t|>1$ together with the mixed relations
$$s_rx_r=x_{r+1}s_r-1,\qquad s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1,\qquad s_rx_t=x_ts_r\quad(t\notin\{r,r+1\}).$$

**Auxiliary cyclotomic quotients.** For a monic polynomial
$f(u)=u^{\ell}+a_{\ell-1}u^{\ell-1}+\dots+a_0$ in $A[u]$ of degree $\ell$
impose the single relation $f(X_1)=0$ (respectively $f(x_1)=0$) on the FIRST
polynomial generator and call the resulting quotient the **monic cyclotomic
quotient**; when $\ell=0$, so that $f=1$, the quotient at positive rank is the
zero algebra, while rank zero remains $A$. In the nondegenerate case the
constant term $a_0$ is required to be a unit. The first-strand convention
imposed here (cyclotomic relation on $X_1$, and later induction appending on
the right) is the one used on this page.

**The charged cyclic specialization.** Let $A=F$ be a field, let
$z=q_H\in F^{\times}$ have finite quantum characteristic $e\ge2$
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), and let
$I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ be the cyclic **label set** of residues, with a
dominant cyclic type-A weight $(\lambda_i)_{i\in I}$, $\lambda_i\ge0$, and
$\ell=\sum_i\lambda_i$
([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). If $q_H\ne1$ use the
nondegenerate presentation and put $c_i:=q_H^{\,i}$; if $q_H=1$ (which forces
$\operatorname{char}F=e$) use the degenerate presentation and put
$c_i:=i\cdot1_F$. Impose
$$f(z_1)=\prod_{i\in I}(z_1-c_i)^{\lambda_i}$$
on the first generator ($z_1=X_1$ in the nondegenerate branch and $z_1=x_1$ in
the degenerate branch) and write $H_d^\Lambda$ for the resulting **charged
cyclotomic quotient** of rank $d$. This charged finite-$e$ branch is the scope
of the present page; the arbitrary-base affine and monic definitions above
supply its universal PBW and trace proof inputs. The definition itself asserts
no basis, no spectrum, no primitive block decomposition and no
Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism. The grading variable $v$ of the KLR side is
independent of $q_H$.

**Well-definedness notes.** The nondegenerate parameters $c_i=q_H^i$ are
distinct because $q_H$ has multiplicative order exactly $e$; the degenerate
parameters $c_i=i\cdot1_F$ are distinct because $\operatorname{char}F=e$ makes
$i\cdot1_F\ne j\cdot1_F$ for $0\le i<j<e$. In the nondegenerate branch no
embedding of the label set $\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ into $F$ is claimed or used:
$i$ is only a label for the value $q_H^i$. All these definitions are given by
generators, relations and a two-sided quotient ideal and use no choice
principle.

Over any commutative base ring $A$ with invertible nondegenerate parameter,
use the defining relations of
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]], writing

the quotient by $f(X_1)=0$ is spanned by
$$X_1^{a_1}\cdots X_d^{a_d}T_w,\qquad 0\le a_r<\ell,\ w\in S_d,$$
and the degenerate quotient by $f(x_1)=0$ is spanned by
$$x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_d^{a_d}w,\qquad 0\le a_r<\ell,\ w\in S_d .$$

$\ell^dd!$. This applies to $f(t)=\prod_{i\in I}(t-q_H^i)^{\lambda_i}$ and
$f(t)=\prod_{i\in I}(t-i)^{\lambda_i}$ in the two finite-quantum-characteristic
branches, with $\ell=\sum_i\lambda_i$. No independence and no separate relation
$f(X_r)=0$ or $f(x_r)=0$ for $r>1$ is asserted. If $\ell=0$ and $d>0$, the
imposed relation $1=0$ gives the zero algebra with empty spanning family; for
$d=0$ the algebra is $A$ with the singleton empty monomial.

Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $z\in A$ be a unit. Fix an integer
$n\ge0$.

**The nondegenerate affine presentation.** The algebra
$H_n^{\mathrm{aff}}(A;z)$ is the $A$-algebra presented by commuting units
$X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$
([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]],

$$T_rX_rT_r=zX_{r+1},\qquad T_rX_s=X_sT_r\quad(s\notin\{r,r+1\}),$$
the last two relations being the Bernstein relation and the distant mixed
commutation, and with $T_r$ invertible as a consequence of its quadratic
relation. For $n=0$ the algebra is $A$.

**The degenerate affine presentation.** The algebra
$H_n^{\deg}(A)$ is the $A$-algebra presented by commuting generators
$x_1,\dots,x_n$ and symmetric-group generators $s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}$ subject to
the Coxeter relations $s_r^2=1$, $s_rs_{r+1}s_r=s_{r+1}s_rs_{r+1}$,
$s_rs_t=s_ts_r$ for $|r-t|>1$ together with the mixed relations
$$s_rx_r=x_{r+1}s_r-1,\qquad s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1,\qquad s_rx_t=x_ts_r\quad(t\notin\{r,r+1\}).$$

polynomial generator and call the resulting quotient the **monic cyclotomic
quotient**; when $\ell=0$, so that $f=1$, the quotient at positive rank is the
zero algebra, while rank zero remains $A$. In the nondegenerate case the
constant term $a_0$ is required to be a unit. The first-strand convention

the right) is the one used on this page.

the degenerate branch) and write $H_d^\Lambda$ for the resulting **charged
cyclotomic quotient** of rank $d$. This charged finite-$e$ branch is the scope
of the present page; the arbitrary-base affine and monic definitions above
supply its universal PBW and trace proof inputs. The definition itself asserts
no basis, no spectrum, no primitive block decomposition and no
Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism. The grading variable $v$ of the KLR side is
independent of $q_H$.

distinct because $q_H$ has multiplicative order exactly $e$; the degenerate
parameters $c_i=i\cdot1_F$ are distinct because $\operatorname{char}F=e$ makes

generated by the following elements:

- $x_ix_j-x_jx_i$ for all $1\le i,j\le d$;
- $s_i^2-1$, $s_is_{i+1}s_i-s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1}$, and $s_is_j-s_js_i$ for
  $|i-j|>1$, for $1\le i,j\le d-1$;
- $s_ix_j-x_js_i$ for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$, $s_ix_{i+1}-x_is_i-1$, and
  $x_{i+1}s_i-s_ix_i-1$, for $1\le i\le d-1$ and $1\le j\le d$.

independent of the chosen word once the basis theorem below is proved. For
$a\in\mathbb C$, the notation $H_d/(x_1-a)$ means the quotient by the two-sided
ideal generated by $x_1-a$.

The verification below establishes exactly the structure of $H_d$ used
throughout this page: the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad r_1,\dots,r_d\ge0,\ w\in S_d,$$
form a $\mathbb C$-basis, so that
$H_d\cong\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C[S_d]$ as a vector
space with polynomial and group-algebra subalgebras
([[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]], [[def-group-ring]]);
$H_0=\mathbb C$ and $H_1=\mathbb C[x_1]$; for every $a$ there is a unique
algebra isomorphism
$$H_d/(x_1-a)\cong\mathbb C[S_d],\qquad x_j\longmapsto a+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j);$$
and total polynomial degree is an algebra filtration whose associated graded is
the semidirect product $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$ in which
$s_i$ acts by swapping $x_i$ and $x_{i+1}$. The cross relation is
inhomogeneous, so it does not turn $H_d$ into a graded algebra with
$\deg x_i=1$ and $\deg s_i=0$.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $z\in A$ be a unit. Fix an integer
$n\ge0$.

**The nondegenerate affine presentation.** The algebra
$H_n^{\mathrm{aff}}(A;z)$ is the $A$-algebra presented by commuting units
$X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$
([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]],
[[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]) subject to
$$T_r^2=(z-1)T_r+z,\qquad T_rT_{r+1}T_r=T_{r+1}T_rT_{r+1},\qquad T_rT_s=T_sT_r\quad(|r-s|>1),$$
$$T_rX_rT_r=zX_{r+1},\qquad T_rX_s=X_sT_r\quad(s\notin\{r,r+1\}),$$
the last two relations being the Bernstein relation and the distant mixed
commutation, and with $T_r$ invertible as a consequence of its quadratic
relation. For $n=0$ the algebra is $A$.

**The degenerate affine presentation.** The algebra
$H_n^{\deg}(A)$ is the $A$-algebra presented by commuting generators
$x_1,\dots,x_n$ and symmetric-group generators $s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}$ subject to
the Coxeter relations $s_r^2=1$, $s_rs_{r+1}s_r=s_{r+1}s_rs_{r+1}$,
$s_rs_t=s_ts_r$ for $|r-t|>1$ together with the mixed relations
$$s_rx_r=x_{r+1}s_r-1,\qquad s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1,\qquad s_rx_t=x_ts_r\quad(t\notin\{r,r+1\}).$$

**Auxiliary cyclotomic quotients.** For a monic polynomial
$f(u)=u^{\ell}+a_{\ell-1}u^{\ell-1}+\dots+a_0$ in $A[u]$ of degree $\ell$
impose the single relation $f(X_1)=0$ (respectively $f(x_1)=0$) on the FIRST
polynomial generator and call the resulting quotient the **monic cyclotomic
quotient**; when $\ell=0$, so that $f=1$, the quotient at positive rank is the
zero algebra, while rank zero remains $A$. In the nondegenerate case the
constant term $a_0$ is required to be a unit. The first-strand convention
imposed here (cyclotomic relation on $X_1$, and later induction appending on
the right) is the one used on this page.

**The charged cyclic specialization.** Let $A=F$ be a field, let
$z=q_H\in F^{\times}$ have finite quantum characteristic $e\ge2$
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), and let
$I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ be the cyclic **label set** of residues, with a
dominant cyclic type-A weight $(\lambda_i)_{i\in I}$, $\lambda_i\ge0$, and
$\ell=\sum_i\lambda_i$
([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). If $q_H\ne1$ use the
nondegenerate presentation and put $c_i:=q_H^{\,i}$; if $q_H=1$ (which forces
$\operatorname{char}F=e$) use the degenerate presentation and put
$c_i:=i\cdot1_F$. Impose
$$f(z_1)=\prod_{i\in I}(z_1-c_i)^{\lambda_i}$$
on the first generator ($z_1=X_1$ in the nondegenerate branch and $z_1=x_1$ in
the degenerate branch) and write $H_d^\Lambda$ for the resulting **charged
cyclotomic quotient** of rank $d$. This charged finite-$e$ branch is the scope
of the present page; the arbitrary-base affine and monic definitions above
supply its universal PBW and trace proof inputs. The definition itself asserts
no basis, no spectrum, no primitive block decomposition and no
Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism. The grading variable $v$ of the KLR side is
independent of $q_H$.

**Well-definedness notes.** The nondegenerate parameters $c_i=q_H^i$ are
distinct because $q_H$ has multiplicative order exactly $e$; the degenerate
parameters $c_i=i\cdot1_F$ are distinct because $\operatorname{char}F=e$ makes
$i\cdot1_F\ne j\cdot1_F$ for $0\le i<j<e$. In the nondegenerate branch no
embedding of the label set $\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ into $F$ is claimed or used:
$i$ is only a label for the value $q_H^i$. All these definitions are given by
generators, relations and a two-sided quotient ideal and use no choice
principle.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra and let $\mu$ be a highest weight. The action of
$U(\mathfrak g)$ on the Verma module $M(\mu)$ induces an algebra isomorphism
$$U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \bigl(\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}M(\mu)\bigr)^{\operatorname{ad}\mathfrak g\text{-finite}},$$
where the target is the locally finite part of the endomorphism algebra for
the adjoint action $x\mapsto[x,-]$. In particular
$\operatorname{Ann}M(\mu)=U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu$. Moreover, for every
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $E$,
$$\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E\otimes M(\mu))=\dim E_0,$$
and the action identifies each finite adjoint isotypic multiplicity with that
dimension.

([[def-frobenius-characteristic-map]],
[[def-graded-ordinary-representation-ring-of-symmetric-groups]]). By
[[thm-frobenius-characteristic-is-an-isometric-graded-ring-isomorphism]] it is a
degree-preserving $\mathbb Z$-module isomorphism onto the stable symmetric
function ring $\Lambda=\bigoplus_{m\ge0}\Lambda^m$, so its restriction
$\operatorname{ch}:R(S_m)\to\Lambda^m$ is an isomorphism for every $m\ge0$.

For $f\in\Lambda^m$ and $g\in\Lambda^n$ define
$$f*g:=\begin{cases}\operatorname{ch}\bigl(\operatorname{ch}^{-1}(f)\cdot\operatorname{ch}^{-1}(g)\bigr),&m=n,\\[2pt]0,&m\ne n,\end{cases}$$
where $\cdot$ is the pointwise (internal tensor) product of class functions on
$S_m$; extend $*$ bilinearly to all of $\Lambda$. Call $*$ the
**internal (Kronecker) product** of symmetric functions.

**Well-definedness.** For $m=n$ the class functions $\operatorname{ch}^{-1}(f)$
and $\operatorname{ch}^{-1}(g)$ lie in $R(S_m)$, the integral span of the
irreducible characters of $S_m$
([[def-graded-ordinary-representation-ring-of-symmetric-groups]]). The
pointwise product of two honest characters of $S_m$ is again an honest
character, namely the character of the tensor product of the underlying
representations ([[thm-characters-of-direct-sums-tensor-products-and-duals]]),
and products of $\mathbb Z$-combinations of characters are computed
bilinearly; hence the pointwise product of two elements of $R(S_m)$ lies in
$R(S_m)$, and applying the isomorphism $\operatorname{ch}$ lands in $\Lambda^m$.
The product is therefore well defined and takes $\Lambda^m\times\Lambda^m$ to
$\Lambda^m$.

**Basic properties.** The product is bilinear by construction and inherits
commutativity and associativity from the pointwise product of class functions.
It preserves degrees, in the sense that $\Lambda^m*\Lambda^n\subseteq\Lambda^m$
for $m=n$ and is $0$ for $m\ne n$. On $\Lambda^n$ the unit is
$h_n=s_{(n)}=\operatorname{ch}(\text{trivial character of }S_n)$, because the
trivial character is the unit for pointwise multiplication on $R(S_n)$
([[thm-frobenius-characteristic-sends-specht-characters-to-schur-functions]]
identifies $\operatorname{ch}(\chi^{(n)})=s_{(n)}=h_n$). The graded direct sum
$\Lambda$ has **no global unit** for $*$: if $e\in\Lambda$ had finite degree
support and $n$ were a degree with $e_n=0$ while $\Lambda^n\ne0$, then
$(e*h_n)_n=e_n*h_n=0\ne h_n$, so $e*h_n\ne h_n$; a global unit would require
$e_n$ to be a unit of $(\Lambda^n,*)$ for every $n$. In particular the ordinary
product unit $1\in\Lambda^0$ is not a unit for $*$ on the positive degrees.

the Specht character dictionary $\operatorname{ch}(\chi^\lambda)=s_\lambda$
([[thm-frobenius-characteristic-sends-specht-characters-to-schur-functions]])
give
$$s_\lambda*s_\mu=\operatorname{ch}\bigl(\chi^\lambda\cdot\chi^\mu\bigr)=\operatorname{ch}\Bigl(\sum_{\nu\vdash n}g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)\chi^\nu\Bigr)=\sum_{\nu\vdash n}g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)\,s_\nu,$$
because $\chi^\lambda\chi^\mu$ is the character of
$S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$ and its decomposition has multiplicities
$g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$
([[def-kronecker-coefficient-and-internal-tensor-product]]).

choice-free Frobenius characteristic isomorphism and finite-dimensional
representation theory of finite groups.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Fix an integer $n\ge0$ and work over $\mathbb C$. Let $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ be
partitions of $n$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]), and let
$S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$ be the tensor product of their complex
Specht modules, a finite-dimensional complex $S_n$-module
([[def-tensor-product-of-complex-representations]],
[[def-column-antisymmetrizer-polytabloid-and-specht-module]]). The
**Kronecker coefficient** $g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ of a third partition
$\nu\vdash n$ is the multiplicity of $S^\nu$ in this tensor product:

$$g(\lambda,\mu,\nu):=\frac{\dim_{\mathbb C}\bigl(S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu\bigr)_{(S^\nu)}}{\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\nu},$$

where $\bigl(S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu\bigr)_{(S^\nu)}$ is the isotypic
component of type $S^\nu$
([[def-isotypic-component-of-a-completely-reducible-representation]]).

**Well-definedness.** The module $S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$ is
finite-dimensional, and $\operatorname{char}\mathbb C=0$ does not divide the
order of the finite group $S_n$, so complex Maschke's theorem gives complete
reducibility
([[thm-maschkes-theorem-for-finite-groups-over-fields-whose-characteristic-does-not-divide-the-group-order]],
[[cor-finite-dimensional-representations-are-completely-reducible-when-char-k-does-not-divide-group-order]],
[[def-completely-reducible-representation]]). The complex Specht modules
$S^\nu$, $\nu\vdash n$, are a complete list of pairwise inequivalent
irreducible $S_n$-modules
([[thm-complex-specht-modules-are-irreducible]],
[[thm-complex-irreducibles-of-symmetric-groups-are-specht-modules]],
[[cor-distinct-specht-modules-are-inequivalent]]). Consequently a decomposition
into irreducibles has the form
$S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu\cong\bigoplus_{\nu\vdash n}m_\nu S^\nu$
with nonnegative integer multiplicities $m_\nu$, and the isotypic component of
type $S^\nu$ is the direct sum of exactly the $m_\nu$ copies of $S^\nu$
appearing in any such decomposition; in particular
$\dim_{\mathbb C}(S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu)_{(S^\nu)}=m_\nu\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\nu$
and $\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\nu>0$ because $S^\nu$ is irreducible. Hence
$g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)=m_\nu$ is a nonnegative integer, independent of the chosen
decomposition, and $g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ is by definition the multiplicity of
$S^\nu$ in $S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$.

**The internal product.** For partitions $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ call
$$(\lambda,\mu)\longmapsto S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$$
the **internal (Kronecker) product** of the $S_n$-representations $S^\lambda$
and $S^\mu$. Unlike the outer induction product
$\operatorname{Ind}_{S_a\times S_b}^{S_{a+b}}(S^\alpha\boxtimes S^\beta)$ of
[[thm-outer-littlewood-richardson-rule]], which takes a pair of modules of
degrees $a$ and $b$ to a module of degree $a+b$, the internal product keeps the
rank: both inputs and the output are $S_n$-modules of the same degree $n$. The
two operations are different constructions on different data; the outer product
is mentioned here only for contrast and is not used in this definition.

No form of the Axiom of Choice is used: the tensor product, Maschke's theorem,
the Specht classification and the isotypic decomposition are finite-dimensional
complex representation theory of a finite group.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and that $I$ is bounded
below, so $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are finite; the upper end of
$I$ may remain unbounded. Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n(\mathbb C)$ and let
the standard parabolic $\mathfrak p$ have Levi
$\mathfrak{gl}_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{n_l}$
([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]).
For a tableau $A$ let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ be its ordinary highest-weight
reading: read columns from left to right and each column from top to bottom,
so its entries are strictly decreasing. This is also the normally ordered column reading of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]. Put
$$\lambda_A=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(a_j+j-1)\,\varepsilon_j .$$
Strict columns make $\lambda_A$ Levi-dominant, so that the simple highest weight
module $L(A)$ of [[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]
and the induced generalized standard
$M(A)=M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda_A)$ of
[[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]] belong to the genuine
parabolic category $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ of
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]].

Use the published **half-sum convention**
$\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$; then
$$\lambda_{A,j}+\rho_j=a_j+\frac{n-1}{2},$$
so the $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ Harish-Chandra shifted-coordinate multiset of the
block is the tableau-entry multiset plus the common scalar $(n-1)/2$, and this
multiset together with the displayed scalar $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ centre labels the
central character ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]). The Fock
weight $\sum_j\delta_{a_j}=\Lambda-\alpha$ of the Fock item belongs to the
different $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ weight lattice and indexes that entry multiset;
it is **not** a literal $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ highest weight.

For an entry multiset $\alpha$ the corresponding **finite parabolic central
block** $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ has labels
$\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$, generalized standards $M(A)$, simples $L(A)$,
projective covers $P(A)$ and costandards $\nabla(A)$, with the BGG reciprocity,
restricted duality and highest-weight structure inherited from
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]; by
[[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]] it is a single
linkage block. Its simple and standard classes form bases of its Grothendieck
group, and its numerical multiplicities include repeated-entry singular central
characters. The direct sum over the admitted entry multisets is
$\mathcal O^\Lambda$. **Opposite blocks** use the reversed Levi order and the
reverse-column reading, with the correspondingly reversed label order
([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
published category-$\mathcal O$ theory. Let
$\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ be the standard
parabolic of
[[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]], with
reductive parabolic Levi $\mathfrak l_J$, nilradical $\mathfrak u_J$ and Weyl
group $W_J$; the ambient category is $\mathcal O$ of [[def-bgg-category-o]]
with standard objects the Verma modules [[def-verma-module]].

**(1) Dominance for the Levi.** A weight $\lambda$ is **$\mathfrak p$-dominant**
if $\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ for all
$\alpha\in\Phi_J^+$ (this is dominance for the Levi root system; in particular
$\lambda$ is integral for $\Phi_J$; see
[[def-integral-dominant-and-strictly-dominant-weights]] for the ambient
notion).

**(2) Generalized Verma modules.** For a $\mathfrak p$-dominant $\lambda$ let
$E(\lambda)$ be the finite-dimensional simple $\mathfrak p$-module obtained
from the finite-dimensional simple $\mathfrak l_J$-module of highest weight
$\lambda$
([[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]])
by letting $\mathfrak u_J$ act by zero. Define the **generalized Verma module**

$$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak p)}E(\lambda).$$

**(3) The parabolic category.** The **parabolic category** $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
is the full subcategory of $\mathcal O$ whose objects are the finitely
generated $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-modules on which
$U(\mathfrak p)$ acts locally finitely, that is, on which every vector lies
in a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-submodule; equivalently, every vector
lies in a finite-dimensional
$\mathfrak l_J$-submodule and is annihilated by a power of $\mathfrak u_J$
(local finiteness for the nilpotent $\mathfrak u_J$).

The following structural facts are part of the definition; the arguments are
given in the Remarks.

**(4) Generalized Vermas lie in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.** For each
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$, $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is an
object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ with highest weight $\lambda$, and the
natural surjection $M(\lambda)\twoheadrightarrow M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$
exhibits $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ as the largest quotient of the Verma
module $M(\lambda)$ that lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.

**(5) Simples.** The simple objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ are exactly
the simple highest-weight modules $L(\lambda)$ with $\lambda$
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral
([[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]).

**(6) Serre property.** $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is closed under subobjects,
quotients and extensions in $\mathcal O$; in particular it is an abelian
subcategory of $\mathcal O$ stable under finite direct sums.

**(7) Costandard objects.** For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ put
$\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=D M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, the restricted
dual of [[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]].
These are the **costandard objects** of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$; each is
naturally a submodule of the ordinary dual Verma $D M(\lambda)$. They need not
be quotients of ordinary dual Vermas.

Only the Levi-integrable simple criterion, Serre property, largest generalized-Verma quotient and the explicit integral charge/height convention are consumed. required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its skew derivations $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), fix $i\in I$, and write $f_i^{(n)}=F_i^n/[n]_i!$ for the divided powers ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]). Then:

(i) $e_i'$ is locally nilpotent on $U_q^-$, and the endomorphism
$$P_i:=\sum_{m\ge0}(-1)^mq_i^{-m(m-1)/2}F_i^{(m)}e_i'^{\,m}\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^-)$$
is well defined (each sum is finite on each element) and is the projection onto $\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$ along $f_iU_q^-$. In particular $e_i'P_i=0$, $P_iF_i=0$, $P_i^2=P_i$, $P_iu=u$ for $u\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$, and
$$U_q^-=\operatorname{Ker}e_i'\oplus f_iU_q^-.$$

(ii) Every $u\in U_q^-$ has a unique $i$-string decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i',\qquad u_n=0\ \text{for }n\gg0,$$
and the components are given by $u_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_ie_i'^{\,n}u$.

(iii) The **Kashiwara operators on the negative half**, defined on the string decomposition by
$$\tilde e_iu:=\sum_{n\ge1}f_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_iu:=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n+1)}u_n,$$
are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear endomorphisms of $U_q^-$ with $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\operatorname{id}_{U_q^-}$; $\tilde e_iu=0$ if and only if $u\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$; $\tilde f_i$ is injective and $\tilde f_i(1)=F_i$. Both operators preserve the root grading and shift its degree by $\mp\alpha_i$, that is $\tilde e_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu+\alpha_i]$ and $\tilde f_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu-\alpha_i]$.

No choice principle is used. Here $e_i'^{\,n}$ denotes the ordinary $n$-fold power of the derivation, not its divided power. The same projector and every string coefficient preserve the $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), as proved by the integral skew-string supplier; this does not assert that lattice's freeness.

actual_declared_use_sites.text: [F2] Unique string decomposition ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]): every $u\in U_q^-$ has a unique finite decomposition $u=\sum_lF_i^{(l)}u_l$ with $u_l\in\ker e_i'$; for $u\in F_i^nU_q^-$ one has $u_l=0$ for $l<n$, and conversely.

required_interface.text:
For every commutative ring $R$ and $q\in R^\times$:

1. $\theta(T_i):=(q-1)-T_i=-qT_i^{-1}$ extends uniquely to an involutive
$R$-algebra automorphism $\theta$ of $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$, with
$\theta(T_w)=(-q)^{\ell(w)}T_{w^{-1}}^{-1}$; $\theta$ commutes with the star
anti-involution $*$ and is compatible with every base change.

2. For a right $H$-module $M$, the pullback $M^\theta$ (same underlying
$R$-module, action $m\cdot h:=m\theta(h)$) is a right $H$-module; $(-)^\theta$
is exact, preserves submodules, quotients, finite composition multiplicities and
simplicity, and $(M^\theta)^\theta=M$.

3. The star-contragredient $M^\circ:=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)$ with
$(f\cdot h)(m):=f(mh^*)$ is a right $H$-module; for finite free $M$ it is finite
free of the same rank, $(-)^\circ$ commutes with base change, and
$(M^\theta)^\circ=(M^\circ)^\theta$.

4. For every partition $\lambda\vdash n$, if $w_0(S_\lambda)$ is the longest
element of the row subgroup, then
$$\theta(x_\lambda)=q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}y_\lambda,\qquad \theta(y_\lambda)=q^{-\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}x_\lambda.$$
In particular $\theta(x_\lambda)$ and $y_\lambda$ differ by the unit
$q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}$, and this unit factor must be carried through every
form comparison. At $q=1$, $\theta$ is the pullback along the sign automorphism
$w\mapsto\operatorname{sgn}(w)w$ of $R[S_n]$.

No choice principle is used.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^\times$ and $\lambda\vdash n$, and let $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ with its basis $\{m_t\}$, $P(\lambda)=z_\lambda H$, the permutation form $\beta$ on $M(\lambda)$ and the DJ form on $P(\lambda)$ be as in [[def-dj-bridge-row-column-permutation-modules-and-polytabloids]], [[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]] and [[lem-dj-bridge-integral-murphy-and-polytabloid-straightening]]. Then:

1. Setting $B_\lambda(m_s,p):=\beta(x_\lambda T_{d_\lambda(s)},p)$ for $s\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)$ and $p\in P(\lambda)$ defines an explicit $R$-bilinear pairing $B_\lambda\colon C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)\times P(\lambda)\to R$ that is $H$-balanced, $B_\lambda(mh,p)=B_\lambda(m,ph^*)$, and whose adjoint $c\mapsto B_\lambda(c,-)$ is an isomorphism of right $H$-modules $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)\to P(\lambda)^\circ$ onto the star-contragredient module of [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]. No nondegeneracy of the DJ form $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$ is required.

2. Equivalently, the kernel of the quotient map $M(\lambda)\to C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ is the orthogonal complement $P(\lambda)^\perp=\{a\in M(\lambda):\beta(a,p)=0\text{ for all }p\in P(\lambda)\}$, namely $M(\lambda)\cap I^{\rhd\lambda}$; the pairing matrices in the bases $\{m_s\}$ and $\{e_t\}$ have entries $B_\lambda(m_s,e_t)=q^{\ell(d_\lambda(s))}a_{d_\lambda(s),t}$ with $e_t=\sum_d a_{d,t}b_d$, and determinant a unit of $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$. Their inverses are finite tableau formulas given by the adjugate divided by this unit.

3. All statements are compatible with every base change $A\to R$, $v\mapsto q$; the construction uses no generic semisimplicity, no nondegeneracy of $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$ and no choice principle.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring with $1$ and $A$ a unital $R$-algebra
([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) that is free as an $R$-module on a
finite set $C=\{c^{\lambda}_{st}:\lambda\in\Lambda,\ s,t\in T(\lambda)\}$,
where $(\Lambda,\unrhd)$ is a finite poset ([[def-partial-order]]; its strict
order is written $\rhd$) and each $T(\lambda)$ is a finite set. For
$\lambda\in\Lambda$ let $A^{\rhd\lambda}$ be the $R$-submodule of $A$ spanned
by all $c^{\mu}_{uv}$ with $\mu\rhd\lambda$.

Then $(C,\Lambda)$ is a **cellular basis** of $A$, and $A$ is a **cellular
algebra**, if:

(i) the $R$-linear map $i:A\to A$ with $i(c^{\lambda}_{st})=c^{\lambda}_{ts}$
for all $\lambda,s,t$ is an algebra anti-automorphism of $A$, i.e. $i(ab)=i(b)i(a)$
and $i(1)=1$ (equivalently $i$ is an isomorphism of $A$ with the opposite
algebra; the displayed formula forces $i^2=\mathrm{id}$); and

(ii) for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$, every $t\in T(\lambda)$ and every $a\in A$
there exist $r_v\in R$ ($v\in T(\lambda)$) with
$$c^{\lambda}_{st}\,a\equiv\sum_{v\in T(\lambda)}r_v\,c^{\lambda}_{sv}\pmod{A^{\rhd\lambda}}.$$

**Cell modules.** For $\lambda\in\Lambda$ let $C^{\lambda}$ be the free
$R$-module with basis $\{c^{\lambda}_t:=c^{\lambda}_{tt}:t\in T(\lambda)\}$;
condition (ii) makes $C^{\lambda}$ a right $A$-module by
$c^{\lambda}_t a:=\sum_v r_vc^{\lambda}_v$ when
$c^{\lambda}_{tt}a\equiv\sum_v r_vc^{\lambda}_{tv}\pmod{A^{\rhd\lambda}}$, and
it makes $C^{\lambda}$ a left $A$-module via $i$, the left action being
$a\cdot c^{\lambda}_t:=c^{\lambda}_t\,i(a)$. Both actions are well defined on
the freely spanning basis elements by (ii): the coefficients $r_v$ are unique
because $C$ is an $R$-basis of $A$ and the quotient by $A^{\rhd\lambda}$ kills
exactly the basis elements indexed by strictly larger labels, while applying
the anti-automorphism (i) to (ii) gives the same triangularity for left
multiplication. The module $C^{\lambda}$ is the **(right) cell module** of
$\lambda$, and
$$A^{\unrhd\lambda}/A^{\rhd\lambda}\cong C^{\lambda}\otimes_R C^{\lambda}$$
via $c^{\lambda}_{st}+A^{\rhd\lambda}\mapsto c^{\lambda}_s\otimes c^{\lambda}_t$,
where $A^{\unrhd\lambda}$ is spanned by all $c^{\mu}_{uv}$ with
$\mu\unrhd\lambda$. A cellular algebra may have several cellular bases.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
Let $F$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital cellular $F$-algebra with
cellular basis $(C,\Lambda)$ over the finite poset $\Lambda$
([[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]). For $\lambda\in\Lambda$
put $D^{\lambda}:=C^{\lambda}/\mathrm{rad}\,C^{\lambda}$, where
$\mathrm{rad}\,C^{\lambda}$ is the radical of the cell form
([[lem-cell-form-is-associative-and-its-radical-is-a-submodule]]). Then:

1. if $D^{\lambda}\ne0$ then $D^{\lambda}$ is an absolutely irreducible
   (absolutely simple) $A$-module: it is simple over $F$ and remains simple
   after every extension of scalars to a larger field;
2. $\{D^{\lambda}:\lambda\in\Lambda,\ D^{\lambda}\ne0\}$ is a complete set of
   pairwise non-isomorphic simple $A$-modules ([[def-simple-module]],
   [[thm-jordan-holder-theorem-for-modules]]);
3. $D^{\lambda}\ne0$ if and only if the cell form
   $\langle\ ,\ \rangle_\lambda$ is not identically zero, if and only if
   $\mathrm{rad}\,C^{\lambda}\ne C^{\lambda}$; and, when these equivalent
   conditions hold, $\mathrm{rad}\,C^{\lambda}$ is the unique maximal proper
   submodule and the Jacobson radical of $C^{\lambda}$, so $D^{\lambda}$ is its
   simple head. If the form is identically zero, the cell-form quotient
   $D^{\lambda}$ is zero; no assertion about the Jacobson radical or the actual
   head of $C^{\lambda}$ is made.

No semisimplicity of $A$ is assumed; the theorem is the Graham-Lehrer
classification and applies in particular to $A=H_{F,q}(S_n)$ for every field
$F$ and every $q\in F^{\times}$.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Fix the pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, its box-labelled natural module $V=\mathbb C^N$,
an arbitrary origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$.
Assume AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the imported Skryabin and Vust inputs.
For $X\in\mathfrak p$ define the column-trace character
$$\kappa_c(X)=\sum_{b=1}^l c_b\operatorname{tr}(X_{bb}),$$
where $X_{bb}$ is its $b$th column-Levi diagonal block. Write
$\eta_c(X)=X+\kappa_c(X)1$ for the resulting automorphism of $U(\mathfrak p)$,
so $\eta_c(e_{a,b})=e_{a,b}+\delta_{a,b}c_{\operatorname{col}(a)}$.
Let $\mathbb C_c$ be the corresponding one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module
and set $a_b=c_b+q_b-n$ and $\Lambda=\sum_{b=1}^l\Lambda_{a_b}$, with a
separate integer chain for each complex coset as in
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]].

The **truncated (deformed) tensor space** $E_c=V_c^{\otimes d}$ is
$E=V^{\otimes d}$ with the left $U(\mathfrak p)$-action obtained by composing
the ordinary total tensor representation $\rho_d$ with $\eta_c$.
Equivalently it is $\mathbb C_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, with one character
factor; the origin twist is applied once to the total action. For $d\ge1$
its right $H_d(\Lambda)$-action is determined by place permutations $s_i$ and
$$x_1\mapsto\Bigl(e+\sum_{j=1}^N(c_{\operatorname{col}(j)}+q_{\operatorname{col}(j)}-n)e_{j,j}\Bigr)\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}-\sum_{k=2}^d\sum_{\operatorname{col}(i)<\operatorname{col}(j)}e_{i,j}\otimes1^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes e_{j,i}\otimes1^{\otimes(d-k)},$$
with $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$. Here the generator-fixing anti-involution of
the Hecke algebra converts the displayed operators into a right action.
For $d=0$ there are no $x_j,s_i$, $H_0(\Lambda)=\mathbb C$, and $E_c=\mathbb C_c$.

Grade the box basis by $\deg v_a=l-\operatorname{col}(a)$, use the total
tensor grading and its induced endomorphism filtration, and use the fixed
loop chart $\zeta\colon\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)\to U(\mathfrak g^e)$ of
[[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]]:
$\zeta(\operatorname{gr}_rT_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$, $(i,j,r)\in K$.
The coefficient index remains the actual unshifted $T=FDE$ index of
[[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]].
The restricted character on the fixed centralizer basis is
$$\kappa_c(e_{i,j;r})=\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c),\qquad \sigma_i(c)=\sum_{b=1}^{p_i}c_b.$$
Consequently the **full graded left representation** in this fixed chart is
$$\varphi_{d,c}(X)=\sum_{t=1}^d X^{(t)}+\kappa_c(X)\operatorname{id}_E\qquad(X\in\mathfrak g^e),$$
where $X^{(t)}$ acts in tensor position $t$. In particular its complete
mode-symbol dictionary is
$$\operatorname{gr}_r\Phi_{d,c}(T_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^r\left(\sum_{t=1}^d e_{i,j;r}^{(t)}+\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c)\operatorname{id}_E\right),$$
where $\Phi_{d,c}$ is the restricted $W(\lambda)$-action. On the right,
$\operatorname{gr}_1x_j=e^{(j)}$ and $\operatorname{gr}_0s_i$ is the place
permutation. Thus the graded bimodule is the character-twisted Vust module
$\mathbb C_{\kappa_c|\mathfrak g^e}\otimes E$, with the ordinary truncated
polynomial/permutation action. It need not be the untwisted Vust module in
the fixed chart. Nevertheless its unital left image algebra and its
commutant are exactly the untwisted Vust image algebra and commutant, as
proved below.

The displayed right operators commute with $W(\lambda)$; full
$\mathfrak p$-commutation is not asserted. They make $E_c$ a filtered
$(W(\lambda),H_d(\Lambda))$-bimodule. The actual balanced Skryabin map gives
a coherent isomorphism
$\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to E_c$ of
$(W(\lambda),H_d)$-bimodules. For every complex origin, every pyramid and
every $d$, the two filtered image algebras are mutual centralizers, and their
associated graded image algebras are the unital Vust image algebras. No
admissibility or stable-range restriction enters this centralizer assertion.

If the pyramid is empty, $N=l=0$, use $V=0$ and $W=U(\mathfrak g^e)=\mathbb C$.
For $d=0$ all structures are scalar; for $d>0$, $E=0$ and the empty
cyclotomic product is $1$, giving the zero quotient and zero endomorphism
algebra. All formulas and centralizer identities then have these evident
empty interpretations.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
For every $n\ge0$ and $\lambda\vdash n$ the complex Specht module $S^\lambda$
carries a nondegenerate symmetric $S_n$-invariant bilinear form
$$b(x,y)=\sum_T x_Ty_T$$
given by the coefficientwise product in the tabloid basis, so
$v\mapsto b(v,-)$ is an isomorphism of $\mathbb C S_n$-modules
$S^\lambda\to(S^\lambda)^*$; equivalently $S^\lambda$ is self-dual.
Consequently $\chi^\lambda(g^{-1})=\chi^\lambda(g)$ for every $g\in S_n$, that
is, every irreducible character of $S_n$ is real-valued.

$W(\lambda)$-module by restriction, the natural map
$$\mu_{M,X}\colon M\circledast X\to M\otimes X,\qquad (\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes m)\otimes x\mapsto um\otimes x,$$

Let $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_k)$ be a partition with $|\alpha|=\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_k$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]), and let $n\ge0$ be
an integer. Whenever

$$n\;\ge\;|\alpha|+\alpha_1,$$

define the **first-row padding** of $\alpha$ to size $n$ to be
$$\alpha[n]:=\bigl(n-|\alpha|,\ \alpha_1,\ \alpha_2,\ \dots,\ \alpha_k\bigr).$$

The threshold is exact.

**Above the threshold.** Suppose $n\ge|\alpha|+\alpha_1$. Then
$n-|\alpha|\ge\alpha_1\ge0$, so every entry of the displayed sequence is a
nonnegative integer, the entries sum to $(n-|\alpha|)+|\alpha|=n$, and the
sequence is weakly decreasing because $n-|\alpha|\ge\alpha_1$ and $\alpha$ is
weakly decreasing ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).
If $\alpha$ is nonempty then $\alpha_1\ge1$, hence $n-|\alpha|\ge1$ and the
displayed sequence is a partition of $n$ with positive parts. If
$\alpha=\varnothing$ then the displayed sequence is $(n)$; this is a partition
of $n$ for every $n\ge1$, while for $n=0$ one takes $\varnothing[0]:=\varnothing$,
the unique partition of $0$. Thus the padding is defined and is a partition of
$n$ on the whole displayed range.

**Below the threshold.** If $\alpha$ is nonempty and $n<|\alpha|+\alpha_1$,
then $n-|\alpha|<\alpha_1$; if also $n\ge|\alpha|$ the leading entry is
nonnegative but smaller than the second entry $\alpha_1$, and if $n<|\alpha|$
it is negative. In both cases the displayed sequence is not a partition, so
$\alpha[n]$ is left undefined. The threshold $|\alpha|+\alpha_1$ is therefore
the exact size at which the padded family begins: at
$n=|\alpha|+\alpha_1$ the padding equals $(\alpha_1,\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\dots)$,
which is a partition with a repeated first part when $\alpha$ is nonempty.

**Neutrality of the notation.** This definition records a family of partitions;
it asserts no constancy of any quantity along the family and no stability
property. The same notation is used by the FI-module and
representation-stability developments, where the padding threshold reappears as
the generation degree of the family under consideration.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge0$ and $\ell\ge1$, and let $z,U_1,\dots,U_\ell$
be units of $R$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). The **arbitrary-level
cyclotomic Hecke algebra** $H_n=H_n(R;z;U_1,\dots,U_\ell)$ is the $R$-algebra
presented by invertible commuting elements $X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ subject to the relations
$$(T_i-z)(T_i+1)=0,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(|i-j|>1),$$
$$T_iX_iT_i=zX_{i+1},\qquad X_jT_i=T_iX_j\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}),\qquad \prod_{a=1}^{\ell}(X_1-U_a)=0 .$$
For $n=0$ set $H_0=R$. The **grading variable** of this page is $v$, not the
unit $z$: the two are identified only where a statement says so explicitly.

**Multipartitions and Murphy data.** An $\ell$-**multipartition** of $n$ is an
ordered tuple $\lambda=(\lambda^{(1)},\dots,\lambda^{(\ell)})$ of partitions
with $\sum_{b}|\lambda^{(b)}|=n$ ([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]).
Multipartitions are partially ordered by dominance, $\lambda\unrhd\mu$ meaning
that $\sum_{b\le k}|\lambda^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\lambda^{(k)}_j\ge
\sum_{b\le k}|\mu^{(b)}|+\sum_{j\le m}\mu^{(k)}_j$ for all $k,m$. Fill the
diagram $t^\lambda$ with $1,\dots,n$ in component order, then row order, then
column order. Put $a_k:=\sum_{b<k}|\lambda^{(b)}|$,
$u_\lambda:=\prod_{k=1}^{\ell}\prod_{j\le a_k}(X_j-U_k)$,
$x_\lambda:=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$, and $m_\lambda:=x_\lambda u_\lambda$,
where $S_\lambda$ is the row subgroup: the subgroup of $S_n$ stabilizing the
rows of $t^\lambda$
([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]],
[[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Write $M_\lambda:=m_\lambda H_n$ for
the right $H_n$-submodule generated by $m_\lambda$
([[def-left-and-right-modules]]). The **presentation involution** $*$ of $H_n$
fixes every $X_j$ and every $T_i$ and reverses products. For standard
tableaux $s,t$ of shape $\lambda$ put $m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^{*}m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$,
where $d(s)$ is the permutation determined by $t^\lambda d(s)=s$.
Denote by $H^{>\lambda}$ the span of the higher Murphy shapes once their
basis and cell law is established by
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]], and by
$S_\lambda$ the right cell (**Specht**) module with basis $m_t$ and the
action given by that cell law; its cellular form defines
$D_\lambda:=S_\lambda/\operatorname{rad}S_\lambda$, which may vanish.

**Types.** The types used below are **exactly** all $\ell$-multipartitions of
$n$, including tuples with empty components — not all multicompositions. A
**semistandard tableau** $S$ has entries the labels $(i,k)$ (row $i$ in
component $k$) ordered by component first and then by row, weakly increasing
along rows, strictly increasing down columns, and a label of component $a$
may occur only in physical component $b\le a$
([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]]); the **type** of $S$ is the
multipartition counting each label with the multiplicity of the corresponding
row. For standard $s$ let $\mu(s)$ be the tableau obtained from $s$ by
replacing each entry by its row-and-component in $t^{\mu}$. Put
$$m_{(S,t)}:=\sum_{s:\,\mu(s)=S}m_{st},\qquad m_{(S,T)}:=\sum_{s,t:\,\mu(s)=S,\ \nu(t)=T}m_{st}.$$
Let
$$M:=\bigoplus_{\lambda\ \text{multipartition of}\ n}M_\lambda,\qquad C_n:=\operatorname{End}_{H_n}(M),$$
with ordinary composition ([[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]]). For
$S,T$ of shape $\lambda$ and types $\mu,\nu$, the map $\varphi_{ST}$ — once
justified by [[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]] —
sends $m_\alpha h$ to $\delta_{\alpha,\nu}m_{(S,T)}h$. Its right cell module
$\Delta_\lambda$ has basis $v_T$ over the semistandard $T$ of multipartition
types, with contravariant cell form and quotient $L_\lambda$. Let $T^\lambda$
be the unique tableau of shape and type $\lambda$, and let $e_\lambda$ be the
identity projection onto $M_\lambda$. Put $\omega:=(\varnothing,\dots,\varnothing,(1^n))$
and $e:=e_\omega$; then $m_\omega=1$, so $M_\omega=H_n$, and $H_n$ is an
actual direct summand of $M$. The weight projections used by the Jantzen
theory below are the $e_\nu$ with $\nu$ a multipartition. Write
$K_{(\lambda,\nu)}:=\#\operatorname{SStd}_\nu(\lambda)$ for the number of
semistandard tableaux of shape $\lambda$ and type $\nu$.

**Boundary of the definition.** All asserted module, form and map laws are
discharged by the linked local suppliers
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]],
[[lem-cyclotomic-semistandard-sums-give-schur-endomorphism-basis]] and
[[thm-cyclotomic-schur-standards-and-schur-functor-control-block-linkage]];
the definition itself claims no proof of them and no primitive
residue-content classification. No choice principle is used: only finite
bases, finite subgroup and coset decompositions, finite filtrations and
explicit polynomial identities occur.

For an ordered multipartition $\boldsymbol\mu$ of $d$, let
$S_\xi(\boldsymbol\mu)$ be the intrinsic Murphy cell Specht of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]],
converted from right to left through the generator-fixing star
anti-involution. Let $S_{\deg}(\boldsymbol\mu)$ be the actual affine-induced
Specht of [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]],
with factors $\mathrm{ev}_{m_j}^*S^{\mu^{(j)}}$ in that component order.
Then
$$[\mathcal E_d S_\xi(\boldsymbol\mu)]=[S_{\deg}(\boldsymbol\mu)]\quad\text{in }G_0(H_d^{\deg}).$$
This is equality of classes, not an asserted isomorphism of the Specht
modules. It does not identify an untwisted ordinary same-shape simple with a
transported crystal simple.

[F2] The arbitrary-level Murphy basis is finite free and its commuting $X_r$
act on the cell basis with dominance-triangular diagonal
$U_jz^{c-r}$ at node $(r,c,j)$
([[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]],
[[lem-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-murphy-jm-action-is-content-triangular]]).
This is a universal parameter identity, not an invocation of a finite-$e$
label theorem at $e=0$.

required_interface.text:
Work over the field $\mathbb C$ and fix an integer $d\ge 0$
([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], [[def-commutative-ring]]). Let
$\mathcal F_d$ be the free associative unital $\mathbb C$-algebra on the
$d+(d-1)$ symbols $x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ (for $d=0$ there is only
the unit; for $d=1$ only $x_1$), with its word basis and universal property
([[lem-hh-free-associative-ring-and-relations-descent]]), and let
$I_d\mathrel{\trianglelefteq}\mathcal F_d$ be the two-sided ideal
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]])
generated by the following elements:

- $x_ix_j-x_jx_i$ for all $1\le i,j\le d$;
- $s_i^2-1$, $s_is_{i+1}s_i-s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1}$, and $s_is_j-s_js_i$ for
  $|i-j|>1$, for $1\le i,j\le d-1$;
- $s_ix_j-x_js_i$ for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$, $s_ix_{i+1}-x_is_i-1$, and
  $x_{i+1}s_i-s_ix_i-1$, for $1\le i\le d-1$ and $1\le j\le d$.

The **degenerate affine Hecke algebra** is the quotient $\mathbb C$-algebra
$$H_d:=\mathcal F_d/I_d$$
with unit element written $1$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]). We keep the symbols
$x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ for their images, and for $w\in S_d$ we write
$w$ for the image in $H_d$ of any word in the $s_i$ representing $w$; this is
independent of the chosen word once the basis theorem below is proved. For
$a\in\mathbb C$, the notation $H_d/(x_1-a)$ means the quotient by the two-sided

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Work with the type-$A$ coordinate lattice and the dictionary of
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]];
weights are written in the coordinates $\delta_a=\varepsilon_a$.

Fix a set $I$ of consecutive residues (for the finite box model
$I=\{k_0,\dots,k_0+N-2\}$ and $I^+=I\cup(I+1)=\{k_0,\dots,k_0+N-1\}$; $I$ may be
unbounded below or above), a positive **level** $l$, and
$$\Lambda=\Lambda_{m_1}+\cdots+\Lambda_{m_l}\in P^+,\qquad m_1\ge m_2\ge\cdots\ge m_l,$$
where $m_j\in I^+$ and, if $I$ has lower endpoint $k$, $\Lambda_m=\sum_{k\le a\le m}\delta_a$. When $I$ is unbounded below, $\Lambda_m$ is the ground semi-infinite fundamental weight with the finite-coordinate-difference interpretation below. For $I$ bounded below put
$n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ boxes in column $j$ and $n=\sum_j n_j$; for $I$ unbounded
below use semi-infinite columns with a common finite tail below, as explained
after the weight definition.

The **higher-level wedge-tensor Fock module** is
$$F(\Lambda):=V(\Lambda_{m_1})\otimes V(\Lambda_{m_2})\otimes\cdots\otimes V(\Lambda_{m_l}),$$
the tensor product of the fundamental modules of the dictionary item. When $I$
is bounded below, $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ is the fundamental integrable highest
weight module of highest weight $\Lambda_{m_j}$ in the library algebra. When
$I$ is unbounded below, $V(\Lambda_{m_j})$ is the semi-infinite wedge
$\Lambda^{m_j+\infty}V$ with $V$ the natural module for the locally finite
type-$A$ algebra on $I$; its basis is the set of normally ordered wedges
$v_{i_1}\wedge v_{i_2}\wedge\cdots$ with $i_1>i_2>\cdots$ and the tail
$i_k=m_j+1-k$ for all sufficiently large $k$.

A **$\Lambda$-tableau** $A$ fills the diagram of $\Lambda$ — the columns
$1,\dots,l$ of heights $n_j$, with rows indexed by $I^+$ — with entries in
$I^+$; it is **column-strict** if in each column the entries strictly increase
from bottom to top and all but finitely many entries of row $i$ equal $i$, and
**standard** if in addition the entries weakly increase from left to right in
each row. Write $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, respectively $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$,
for the sets of column-strict, respectively standard $\Lambda$-tableaux, and
$A_\Lambda$ for the **ground-state tableau** with row $i$ filled entirely
with $i$.

For $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ the **column monomial** is
$$M_A:=\left(v_{A(m_1,1)}\wedge v_{A(m_1-1,1)}\wedge\cdots\right)\otimes\cdots\otimes\left(v_{A(m_l,l)}\wedge v_{A(m_l-1,l)}\wedge\cdots\right),$$
with each wedge normally ordered (the entries strictly decrease from top to
bottom inside a column), and
$$\mathrm{wt}_j(A)=\sum_{m_j\ge i\in I^+}\delta_{A(i,j)},\qquad \mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_l(A),\qquad \mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha=\{A:\mathrm{wt}(A)=\Lambda-\alpha\}$$
for $\alpha\in Q^+$. When a column is semi-infinite, the displayed sum means
its ground fundamental weight $\Lambda_{m_j}$ plus the finite sum of the
coordinate differences $\delta_{A(i,j)}-\delta_i$ over the finitely many
positions where $A$ differs from the ground state, evaluated on each
finite-support coroot or torus input; no divergent infinite coordinate sum is
asserted.

The **Bruhat order** on $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ is defined by $A\le B$ iff
$\mathrm{wt}(A)=\mathrm{wt}(B)$ and
$\mathrm{wt}_1(A)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(A)\ge\mathrm{wt}_1(B)+\cdots+\mathrm{wt}_j(B)$
in the dominance order of [[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]] for every
$j<l$; then $A<B$ whenever $B$ is obtained from $A$ by swapping entries $a<b$
in columns $i<j$. The column reading of a tableau (list the columns from left
to right, each column read top to bottom) gives the passage to partitions and
to the Young-diagram conventions of
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]] and
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]; the removable- and
addable-node notation of [[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]
is used for the box moves of a tableau.

The vector $v_\Lambda:=M_{A_\Lambda}$ is called the **vacuum vector**. Weight
bookkeeping, the uniqueness of the monomial of weight $\Lambda$ and the
bijectivity of the column reading are verified below; the column-monomial theorem records the full integral tensor-basis statement. The well-definedness verification here constructs each fundamental factor explicitly without treating a citation to integrability as a wedge-basis theorem.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $z\in A$ be a unit. Fix an integer
$n\ge0$.

**The nondegenerate affine presentation.** The algebra
$H_n^{\mathrm{aff}}(A;z)$ is the $A$-algebra presented by commuting units
$X_1,\dots,X_n$ and generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$
([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]],
[[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]) subject to
$$T_r^2=(z-1)T_r+z,\qquad T_rT_{r+1}T_r=T_{r+1}T_rT_{r+1},\qquad T_rT_s=T_sT_r\quad(|r-s|>1),$$
$$T_rX_rT_r=zX_{r+1},\qquad T_rX_s=X_sT_r\quad(s\notin\{r,r+1\}),$$
the last two relations being the Bernstein relation and the distant mixed
commutation, and with $T_r$ invertible as a consequence of its quadratic
relation. For $n=0$ the algebra is $A$.

**The degenerate affine presentation.** The algebra
$H_n^{\deg}(A)$ is the $A$-algebra presented by commuting generators
$x_1,\dots,x_n$ and symmetric-group generators $s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}$ subject to
the Coxeter relations $s_r^2=1$, $s_rs_{r+1}s_r=s_{r+1}s_rs_{r+1}$,
$s_rs_t=s_ts_r$ for $|r-t|>1$ together with the mixed relations
$$s_rx_r=x_{r+1}s_r-1,\qquad s_rx_{r+1}=x_rs_r+1,\qquad s_rx_t=x_ts_r\quad(t\notin\{r,r+1\}).$$

**Auxiliary cyclotomic quotients.** For a monic polynomial
$f(u)=u^{\ell}+a_{\ell-1}u^{\ell-1}+\dots+a_0$ in $A[u]$ of degree $\ell$
impose the single relation $f(X_1)=0$ (respectively $f(x_1)=0$) on the FIRST
polynomial generator and call the resulting quotient the **monic cyclotomic
quotient**; when $\ell=0$, so that $f=1$, the quotient at positive rank is the
zero algebra, while rank zero remains $A$. In the nondegenerate case the
constant term $a_0$ is required to be a unit. The first-strand convention
imposed here (cyclotomic relation on $X_1$, and later induction appending on
the right) is the one used on this page.

**The charged cyclic specialization.** Let $A=F$ be a field, let
$z=q_H\in F^{\times}$ have finite quantum characteristic $e\ge2$
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), and let
$I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ be the cyclic **label set** of residues, with a
dominant cyclic type-A weight $(\lambda_i)_{i\in I}$, $\lambda_i\ge0$, and
$\ell=\sum_i\lambda_i$
([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). If $q_H\ne1$ use the
nondegenerate presentation and put $c_i:=q_H^{\,i}$; if $q_H=1$ (which forces
$\operatorname{char}F=e$) use the degenerate presentation and put
$c_i:=i\cdot1_F$. Impose
$$f(z_1)=\prod_{i\in I}(z_1-c_i)^{\lambda_i}$$
on the first generator ($z_1=X_1$ in the nondegenerate branch and $z_1=x_1$ in
the degenerate branch) and write $H_d^\Lambda$ for the resulting **charged
cyclotomic quotient** of rank $d$. This charged finite-$e$ branch is the scope
of the present page; the arbitrary-base affine and monic definitions above
supply its universal PBW and trace proof inputs. The definition itself asserts
no basis, no spectrum, no primitive block decomposition and no
Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism. The grading variable $v$ of the KLR side is
independent of $q_H$.

**Well-definedness notes.** The nondegenerate parameters $c_i=q_H^i$ are
distinct because $q_H$ has multiplicative order exactly $e$; the degenerate
parameters $c_i=i\cdot1_F$ are distinct because $\operatorname{char}F=e$ makes
$i\cdot1_F\ne j\cdot1_F$ for $0\le i<j<e$. In the nondegenerate branch no
embedding of the label set $\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ into $F$ is claimed or used:
$i$ is only a label for the value $q_H^i$. All these definitions are given by
generators, relations and a two-sided quotient ideal and use no choice
principle.

Write $H_d^{\deg}$ for the first-strand quotient
$\prod_j(x_1-m_j)=0$ and $H_d^\xi$ for
$\prod_j(X_1-\xi^{m_j})=0$ in
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]]. The
proved support and two local inverse dictionaries give a coherent tower
isomorphism
$$\Theta_d=\phi_d^\xi(\phi_d^{\deg})^{-1}:H_d^{\deg}\longrightarrow H_d^\xi,$$
with $\Theta_d(e_{\deg}(\nu))=e_\xi(\nu)$ for every integer word $\nu$,
where the eigenvalues are $\nu_r$ and $\xi^{\nu_r}$, respectively. Pullback
$\mathcal E_d=\Theta_d^*$ is an exact equivalence preserving all residue
induction/restriction bimodules and their compositions.

Let $k$ have characteristic zero, let $\xi\in k^\times$ have infinite
multiplicative order, and fix a finite integral multicharge
$m_1,\ldots,m_\ell$. Write $S=\{m_j:1\le j\le\ell\}$.
Use the arbitrary-base presentations of
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]] to define
$H_d^{\deg}$ by $\prod_j(x_1-m_j)=0$ and $H_d^{\xi}$ by
$\prod_j(X_1-\xi^{m_j})=0$.
For $d>0$, every nonzero joint generalized weight in the regular module has
labels $\nu\in\mathbb Z^d$, with eigenvalues $\nu_r$ respectively
$\xi^{\nu_r}$, and
$$\min_{s\in S}|\nu_r-s|\le d-1.$$
Thus both algebras have finite joint spectral decompositions defined over $k$.

Use the directed line $i\to i+1$ on $\mathbb Z$, with $d_i=1$,
$Q_{i,i+1}(u,v)=v-u$, $Q_{i+1,i}(u,v)=u-v$ and $Q_{ij}=1$ for
$|i-j|>1$. Define the rank-$d$ cyclotomic KLR algebra as the direct sum of its
finite-content presentations, with first-strand exponents
$\lambda_i=\#\{j:m_j=i\}$. Every nonzero word idempotent satisfies the same
bound, so this rank algebra is a finite sum of finite-dimensional graded
content algebras. Any interval containing
$[\min S-d+1,\max S+d-1]$ gives exactly the same rank-$d$ algebra;
enlarging it introduces only zero word idempotents. Rank zero is $k$.
At level zero every positive rank is zero. This lemma supplies support and
finite windows; it asserts no Hecke--KLR isomorphism or basis correspondence.

Work over a field $k$ of characteristic zero, with $q\in k^\times$ of infinite multiplicative order, integer colors, and the arrows $a\to a+1$. On any finite permutation-stable set of color words, complete the dot ring at the zero dots. The completed local affine Hecke presentation at spectral words $(q^{i_1},\ldots,q^{i_d})$ and the completed type-$A_\infty$ KLR presentation have mutually inverse changes of generators below. This is a local statement; it does not assert cyclotomic support, a tower comparison, or a Specht dictionary.

Write $x=q^a(1-u)$, $z=q^b(1-v)$ and set
$$P_{ab}(u,v)=\begin{cases}1&a=b,\\(1-q)/(1-x/z)&a\ne b,\end{cases}$$
$$Q_{ab}(u,v)=\begin{cases}1-q+qv-u&a=b,\\-q^a/(x-z)&a=b+1,\\(x-qz)/(x-z)&a\ne b,\ a\ne b+1.\end{cases}$$
These are explicit, invertible, rank-independent power series over $k$; in particular the result applies over $\mathbb C$. Use $y_r=1-q^{-i_r}X_r$ on $e(i)$ and the source convention $\psi_r=-\tau_r$, where $\tau$ is the native crossing. The changes of generators are
$$\psi_re(i)=(T_r+P_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1}))Q_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1})^{-1}e(i),$$
$$X_re(i)=q^{i_r}(1-y_r)e(i),\qquad T_re(i)=(\psi_rQ_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1})-P_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1}))e(i).$$
The quadratic polynomial is $K_{aa}=0$, $K_{a,a+1}(u,v)=v-u$, $K_{a+1,a}(u,v)=u-v$, and $K_{ab}=1$ otherwise. The exact equal-color dot moves are $\psi_ru-v\psi_r=-1$ and $\psi_rv-u\psi_r=1$, the same convention as the degenerate dictionary. The braid order is $\psi_1\psi_2\psi_1-\psi_2\psi_1\psi_2$; on $(a,b,a)$ its value is $[K_{ab}(u,v)-K_{ab}(w,v)]/(w-u)$, hence respectively $+1,-1,0$ for forward, backward, nonadjacent colors.

$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$. Use the current category-O namespace:
$N(A):=M(A)$ is the generalized standard, $K(A):=\nabla(A)$ the costandard,
$L(A)$ the category-O simple and $P(A)$ its projective cover, as in
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].
The source17 symbol $K(A)$ denotes our $L(A)$, not our costandard $K(A)$.
Write $\mathsf L(A):=\mathrm{Wh}(L(A))$ for the finite-W image of the
category-O simple; for $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ this is the source finite-W simple
appearing in the Whittaker/Morita contract of
[[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]].
In particular the $W_d$-Hom below takes a finite-W module as its second
argument. Let $\mathrm{Std}$ be the standard labels. Then:

1. For every label $A$, the Schur image of the standard object $N(A)$ is the
   intrinsic affine-induced Specht module
   $$S(A)=H_d\otimes_{H_{d_1,\dots,d_l}}\Bigl(\bigotimes_j \mathrm{ev}^*_{a_j}S^{\mu^{(j)}}\Bigr),\qquad a_j=c_j+q_j-n,$$
   where $\mu^{(j)}$ is the partition of $d_j$ read from the nonnegative
   ground differences in the $j$-th column of $A$ and the factors are induced
   along the affine Young subalgebra $H_{d_1,\dots,d_l}=H_{d_1}\otimes\cdots
   \otimes H_{d_l}$. Its affine action factors through the cyclotomic image $B_d$, so the same module is obtained by replacing $H_d$ in this tensor product by $H_d(\mathbf a)$.
2. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ the module
   $D(A)=\pi(L(A))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},\mathsf L(A))$ is
   simple, the modules $D(A)$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, form a complete set of
   pairwise non-isomorphic simples of the Hecke image $B_d$, and
   $\pi(L(A))=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}$.
3. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, $\pi(P(A))$ is the projective cover $Y(A)$ of
   $D(A)$, and $\pi^*\pi(P(A))\cong P(A)$; ambient off-standard projectives
   still have their genuine images, and no projective-preservation assertion
   is made for them.
4. Images of tiltings carry the opposite-parabolic standard/Specht flag
   coefficients, and $\pi$ is fully faithful on tiltings.
5. For $A\in\mathrm{Col}$ and $B\in\mathrm{Std}$,

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Fix an integer $n\ge0$ and work over $\mathbb C$. Let $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ be
partitions of $n$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]), and let
$S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$ be the tensor product of their complex
Specht modules, a finite-dimensional complex $S_n$-module
([[def-tensor-product-of-complex-representations]],
[[def-column-antisymmetrizer-polytabloid-and-specht-module]]). The
**Kronecker coefficient** $g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ of a third partition
$\nu\vdash n$ is the multiplicity of $S^\nu$ in this tensor product:

$$g(\lambda,\mu,\nu):=\frac{\dim_{\mathbb C}\bigl(S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu\bigr)_{(S^\nu)}}{\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\nu},$$

where $\bigl(S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu\bigr)_{(S^\nu)}$ is the isotypic
component of type $S^\nu$
([[def-isotypic-component-of-a-completely-reducible-representation]]).

**Well-definedness.** The module $S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$ is
finite-dimensional, and $\operatorname{char}\mathbb C=0$ does not divide the
order of the finite group $S_n$, so complex Maschke's theorem gives complete
reducibility
([[thm-maschkes-theorem-for-finite-groups-over-fields-whose-characteristic-does-not-divide-the-group-order]],
[[cor-finite-dimensional-representations-are-completely-reducible-when-char-k-does-not-divide-group-order]],
[[def-completely-reducible-representation]]). The complex Specht modules
$S^\nu$, $\nu\vdash n$, are a complete list of pairwise inequivalent
irreducible $S_n$-modules
([[thm-complex-specht-modules-are-irreducible]],
[[thm-complex-irreducibles-of-symmetric-groups-are-specht-modules]],
[[cor-distinct-specht-modules-are-inequivalent]]). Consequently a decomposition
into irreducibles has the form
$S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu\cong\bigoplus_{\nu\vdash n}m_\nu S^\nu$
with nonnegative integer multiplicities $m_\nu$, and the isotypic component of
type $S^\nu$ is the direct sum of exactly the $m_\nu$ copies of $S^\nu$
appearing in any such decomposition; in particular
$\dim_{\mathbb C}(S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu)_{(S^\nu)}=m_\nu\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\nu$
and $\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\nu>0$ because $S^\nu$ is irreducible. Hence
$g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)=m_\nu$ is a nonnegative integer, independent of the chosen
decomposition, and $g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ is by definition the multiplicity of
$S^\nu$ in $S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$.

**The internal product.** For partitions $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ call
$$(\lambda,\mu)\longmapsto S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$$
the **internal (Kronecker) product** of the $S_n$-representations $S^\lambda$
and $S^\mu$. Unlike the outer induction product
$\operatorname{Ind}_{S_a\times S_b}^{S_{a+b}}(S^\alpha\boxtimes S^\beta)$ of
[[thm-outer-littlewood-richardson-rule]], which takes a pair of modules of
degrees $a$ and $b$ to a module of degree $a+b$, the internal product keeps the
rank: both inputs and the output are $S_n$-modules of the same degree $n$. The
two operations are different constructions on different data; the outer product
is mentioned here only for contrast and is not used in this definition.

No form of the Axiom of Choice is used: the tensor product, Maschke's theorem,
the Specht classification and the isotypic decomposition are finite-dimensional
complex representation theory of a finite group.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and that $I$ is bounded
below, so $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are finite; the upper end of
$I$ may remain unbounded. Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n(\mathbb C)$ and let
the standard parabolic $\mathfrak p$ have Levi
$\mathfrak{gl}_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{n_l}$
([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]).
For a tableau $A$ let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ be its ordinary highest-weight
reading: read columns from left to right and each column from top to bottom,
so its entries are strictly decreasing. This is also the normally ordered column reading of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]. Put
$$\lambda_A=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(a_j+j-1)\,\varepsilon_j .$$
Strict columns make $\lambda_A$ Levi-dominant, so that the simple highest weight
module $L(A)$ of [[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]
and the induced generalized standard
$M(A)=M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda_A)$ of
[[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]] belong to the genuine
parabolic category $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ of
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]].

Use the published **half-sum convention**
$\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$; then
$$\lambda_{A,j}+\rho_j=a_j+\frac{n-1}{2},$$
so the $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ Harish-Chandra shifted-coordinate multiset of the
block is the tableau-entry multiset plus the common scalar $(n-1)/2$, and this
multiset together with the displayed scalar $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ centre labels the
central character ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]). The Fock
weight $\sum_j\delta_{a_j}=\Lambda-\alpha$ of the Fock item belongs to the
different $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ weight lattice and indexes that entry multiset;
it is **not** a literal $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ highest weight.

For an entry multiset $\alpha$ the corresponding **finite parabolic central
block** $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ has labels
$\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$, generalized standards $M(A)$, simples $L(A)$,
projective covers $P(A)$ and costandards $\nabla(A)$, with the BGG reciprocity,
restricted duality and highest-weight structure inherited from
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]; by
[[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]] it is a single
linkage block. Its simple and standard classes form bases of its Grothendieck
group, and its numerical multiplicities include repeated-entry singular central
characters. The direct sum over the admitted entry multisets is
$\mathcal O^\Lambda$. **Opposite blocks** use the reversed Levi order and the
reverse-column reading, with the correspondingly reversed label order
([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]).
