required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $m\ge1$. A **chart** on a topological space $X$ is a homeomorphism
$\varphi:U\to\varphi(U)$ from an open set $U\subseteq X$ onto an open subset of
$\mathbb C^m$ with its usual topology ([[def-homeomorphism-and-open-maps]]);
two charts $\varphi,\psi$ are **holomorphically compatible** when the
transition maps $\psi\circ\varphi^{-1}$ and $\varphi\circ\psi^{-1}$ are
holomorphic on the open sets where they are defined
([[def-holomorphic-function-in-several-complex-variables]]). A **holomorphic
atlas** is a family of pairwise compatible charts whose domains cover $X$. A
**complex manifold of dimension $m$** is a nonempty Hausdorff
([[def-hausdorff-space]]) second-countable ([[def-second-countable-space]])
topological space carrying a holomorphic atlas; the same maximal-atlas argument
as for [[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]] applies verbatim with
$\mathbb C^m$ in place of $\mathbb C$: the union of a holomorphic atlas with all
charts compatible with it is again a holomorphic atlas, so one passes to the
unique maximal atlas and calls its members holomorphic charts. Each chart is a
homeomorphism onto an open subset of $\mathbb C^m\cong\mathbb R^{2m}$, so $X$ is
a topological manifold without boundary of real dimension $2m$
([[def-topological-manifold-without-boundary]]), and for connected $X$ the case
$m=1$ recovers Riemann surfaces ([[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]]).

A **holomorphic map** $f:X\to Y$ between complex manifolds is a continuous map
whose expression in every pair of holomorphic charts is holomorphic
([[def-holomorphic-map-and-complex-jacobian]]); equivalently, composition with
$f$ preserves holomorphic functions.

**Induced smooth structure and complex structure.** Holomorphic functions on
open subsets of $\mathbb C^m$ are smooth
([[cor-holomorphic-functions-in-several-variables-are-smooth]]), so every
holomorphic atlas is a smooth atlas ([[def-smooth-atlas]]) and $X$ is a smooth
manifold of real dimension $2m$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]) whose smooth charts
include the holomorphic ones. In holomorphic coordinates
$z_k=x_k+iy_k$ the **complex structure** is the endomorphism field $J$ of the
tangent bundle determined by $J\partial_{x_k}=\partial_{y_k}$ and
$J\partial_{y_k}=-\partial_{x_k}$; it satisfies $J^2=-\mathrm{id}$ and is
independent of the holomorphic chart, because a holomorphic transition map has
complex-linear differential ([[def-holomorphic-map-and-complex-jacobian]],
[[thm-chain-rule-for-holomorphic-maps-in-several-variables]]) and complex-linear
maps intertwine the two coordinate definitions of multiplication by $i$. A
**Hermitian metric** on $X$ is a Riemannian metric $g$
([[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]]) satisfying
$g(Jv,Jw)=g(v,w)$ for all tangent vectors $v,w$; its Riemannian volume density
is written $\mu_g$ ([[def-riemannian-volume-density]]). The complex structure
makes each tangent space a complex vector space, so the tangent bundle is a
smooth complex vector bundle in the sense of
[[def-complex-linear-and-compatible-bundle-connections]].

**Holomorphic vector bundles and Hermitian bundle metrics.** A **holomorphic
vector bundle of rank $r$** on $X$ is a smooth complex vector bundle
$\pi:E\to X$ of rank $r$
([[def-smooth-vector-bundle-rank-fibre-and-trivial-bundle]],
[[def-complex-linear-and-compatible-bundle-connections]]) together with an open
cover $(V_\alpha)$ of $X$ and smooth local trivializations
$\theta_\alpha:E|_{V_\alpha}\to V_\alpha\times\mathbb C^r$ whose transition
matrices $g_{\alpha\beta}:V_\alpha\cap V_\beta\to\mathrm{GL}_r(\mathbb C)$,
defined by $\theta_\alpha\theta_\beta^{-1}(p,v)=(p,g_{\alpha\beta}(p)v)$, are
holomorphic. A **holomorphic frame** over an open set $V$ is such a
trivialization. Changing holomorphic frame multiplies a local section by a
holomorphic matrix, hence a smooth local section is **holomorphic** exactly when
its representatives in holomorphic frames are holomorphic functions. A
**Hermitian metric** $h$ on $E$ is a smooth bundle metric
([[def-smooth-bundle-metric]]) whose fibre pairings are positive definite
Hermitian forms, linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the
second; the condition is frame-independent because the gauge freedom is
conjugation by a pointwise invertible matrix. Smooth sections are
$\Gamma(E)$ ([[def-smooth-section-local-section-and-support]]).

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $M$ be a Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary of
dimension $n\ge2$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]), let $\mu$ be a smooth positive
density on $M$ ([[def-density-bundle-and-smooth-density]]), and let $E\to M$ be
a finite-rank smooth vector bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-bundle-rank-fibre-and-trivial-bundle]]) over
$\mathbb K=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ carrying a smooth bundle metric
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ ([[def-smooth-bundle-metric]]), Euclidean in the
real case and Hermitian, linear in the first variable, in the complex case; in
the complex case the fibres are complex vector spaces through a smooth complex
structure on $E$
([[def-complex-linear-and-compatible-bundle-connections]]). Write $\Gamma(E)$
for the smooth sections ([[def-smooth-section-local-section-and-support]]).

A $\mathbb K$-linear map $P:\Gamma(E)\to\Gamma(E)$ is a **linear differential
operator of order at most two** on $E$ when, on every chart domain $\Omega$ of
$M$ with coordinates $x=(x^1,\ldots,x^n)$ and in every local frame of $E$ over
$\Omega$ in which a section is written $s\leftrightarrow u=(u^1,\ldots,u^r)$
and its image as $Ps\leftrightarrow((Ps)_1,\ldots,(Ps)_r)$,
$$(Ps)_\lambda=-\sum_{i,j=1}^na^{ij}_{\lambda\mu}(x)\,\partial_i\partial_ju^\mu(x)+\sum_{j=1}^nb^j_{\lambda\mu}(x)\,\partial_ju^\mu(x)+c_{\lambda\mu}(x)u^\mu(x),\qquad1\le\lambda\le r,$$
with smooth coefficient functions on $\Omega$ and summation over the repeated
index $\mu$ (and over $i,j$). Such an operator is **Laplace type** when in
addition, in every such chart and frame, its second-order coefficients are
scalar multiples of the identity, $a^{ij}_{\lambda\mu}=a^{ij}\delta_{\lambda\mu}$,
with $a^{ij}$ smooth real functions for which the matrix $(a^{ij}(x))$ is
symmetric and positive definite at every $x\in\Omega$. Its **principal symbol**
is the smooth section $\sigma_2(P)$ of $\mathrm{Sym}^2T^*M$
([[def-smooth-tensor-field]]) given on such a chart by
$\sigma_2(P)(x,\xi)=a^{ij}(x)\xi_i\xi_j$ for $\xi\in T_x^*M$; equivalently
$\sigma_2(P)(x,\xi)=a_x(\xi,\xi)\,\mathrm{id}_{E_x}$ for a smooth field of
positive-definite quadratic forms $a_x$ on $T_x^*M$, so that
$\sigma_2(P)(x,\xi)>0$ whenever $\xi\ne0$.

$P$ is **formally symmetric** for $(\mu,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ when
$$\int_M\langle Ps,t\rangle\,d\mu=\int_M\langle s,Pt\rangle\,d\mu$$
for all compactly supported smooth sections $s,t\in\Gamma_c(E)$
([[def-integral-of-a-compactly-supported-smooth-density]]).

**Well-definedness.** The definition is local. On a fixed chart and frame the
displayed assignment is a $\mathbb K$-linear map on components with smooth
coefficients, and the chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]])
computes the transition to another chart and frame on the overlap: the
second-order coefficients transform by the symmetric tensor rule
$a'^{kl}=a^{ij}\frac{\partial x'^k}{\partial x^i}\frac{\partial x'^l}{\partial x^j}$
together with conjugation by the frame-change matrix, while the terms produced
by the second derivatives of the coordinate change are absorbed into the
first-order coefficients. Hence a single operator that admits a local
expression on one cover admits a local expression on every chart and frame, and
the two hypotheses placed on the leading coefficient are invariant: scalar-ness
is preserved by frame conjugation and by the coordinate rule for a field of
symmetric matrices, and symmetric positive definiteness is preserved by both.
The principal symbol is therefore independent of the chart and frame, since two
local expressions of the same operator differ by an operator of order at most
one; it is smooth in $(x,\xi)$ because the $a^{ij}$ are smooth, and it is
positive on nonzero covectors exactly when $(a^{ij})$ is positive definite.
Formal symmetry is an identity between integrals of compactly supported smooth
sections and therefore depends only on the operator, the density and the
metric.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
Let $M$ be a Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary,
$\mu$ a smooth positive density on $M$, and $E,F\to M$ finite-rank smooth vector
bundles over $\mathbb K=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ with smooth bundle metrics,
Hermitian (first-variable-linear) in the complex case, with the conventions of
[[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]]. Let
$P:\Gamma(E)\to\Gamma(F)$ be a linear differential operator of order at most two
(the target-$F$ version of the local description in
[[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]]).

Then there is a unique linear differential operator $P^\star:\Gamma(F)\to\Gamma(E)$
of order at most two such that
$$\int_M\langle Pu,v\rangle_F\,d\mu=\int_M\langle u,P^\star v\rangle_E\,d\mu$$
for all compactly supported smooth sections $u\in\Gamma_c(E)$ and
$v\in\Gamma_c(F)$; it is the **formal adjoint** of $P$. It is given locally as
follows: in a chart with coordinates $x$, with density coefficient $\gamma>0$
defined by $\mu=\gamma\,|dx^1\cdots dx^n|$
([[def-density-bundle-and-smooth-density]]), with frames of $E$ and $F$
orthonormal for the metrics (equivalently unitary in the complex case; such
frames exist locally by applying Gram–Schmidt to any local frame,
[[thm-gram-schmidt-orthonormalisation]]), and with local coefficients
$Pu=\sum_{|\alpha|\le2}a_\alpha D^\alpha u$,
$$P^\star v=\sum_{|\alpha|\le2}(-1)^{|\alpha|}\gamma^{-1}D^\alpha\bigl(\gamma\,a_\alpha^*v\bigr),$$
where $a_\alpha^*$ is the fibre adjoint. Consequently:
1. if the leading coefficients of $P$ of order $\delta\in\{0,1,2\}$ are the
   matrices $a_\alpha$, $|\alpha|=\delta$, then those of $P^\star$ are
   $(-1)^\delta a_\alpha^*$, computed in the same orthonormal frames; in
   particular the formal adjoint of a Laplace-type operator is again Laplace
   type and its principal symbol is unchanged,
   $\sigma_2(P^\star)=\sigma_2(P)$;
2. $(P^\star)^\star=P$;
3. if $E=F$, then $P$ is formally symmetric in the sense of
   [[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]] exactly when
   $P=P^\star$.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and that $I$ is bounded
below, so $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are finite; the upper end of
$I$ may remain unbounded. Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n(\mathbb C)$ and let
the standard parabolic $\mathfrak p$ have Levi
$\mathfrak{gl}_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{n_l}$
([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]).
For a tableau $A$ let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ be its ordinary highest-weight
reading: read columns from left to right and each column from top to bottom,
so its entries are strictly decreasing. This is also the normally ordered column reading of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]. Put
$$\lambda_A=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(a_j+j-1)\,\varepsilon_j .$$
Strict columns make $\lambda_A$ Levi-dominant, so that the simple highest weight
module $L(A)$ of [[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]
and the induced generalized standard
$M(A)=M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda_A)$ of
[[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]] belong to the genuine
parabolic category $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ of
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]].

Use the published **half-sum convention**
$\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$; then
$$\lambda_{A,j}+\rho_j=a_j+\frac{n-1}{2},$$
so the $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ Harish-Chandra shifted-coordinate multiset of the
block is the tableau-entry multiset plus the common scalar $(n-1)/2$, and this
multiset together with the displayed scalar $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ centre labels the
central character ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]). The Fock
weight $\sum_j\delta_{a_j}=\Lambda-\alpha$ of the Fock item belongs to the
different $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ weight lattice and indexes that entry multiset;
it is **not** a literal $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ highest weight.

For an entry multiset $\alpha$ the corresponding **finite parabolic central
block** $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ has labels
$\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$, generalized standards $M(A)$, simples $L(A)$,
projective covers $P(A)$ and costandards $\nabla(A)$, with the BGG reciprocity,
restricted duality and highest-weight structure inherited from
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]; by
[[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]] it is a single
linkage block. Its simple and standard classes form bases of its Grothendieck
group, and its numerical multiplicities include repeated-entry singular central
characters. The direct sum over the admitted entry multisets is
$\mathcal O^\Lambda$. **Opposite blocks** use the reversed Levi order and the
reverse-column reading, with the correspondingly reversed label order
([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]).

required_interface.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The exact residue
functors of
[[def-residue-translation-functors-on-the-sum-of-parabolic-o-blocks]] on the
genuine finite-$n$ parabolic blocks have multiplicity-free
generalized-standard flags given by the valid single-entry moves $i\to i+1$ and
$i+1\to i$.

(1) Their $K_0$ operators are the full integrable $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ Fock
Chevalley action, satisfying the integral Chevalley/Serre relations on the
standard basis.

(2) For each simple $L(A)$, a residue translate vanishes exactly when the
corresponding crystal edge is absent; otherwise it is a self-dual
indecomposable with simple equal head and socle $L(\tilde f_iA)$, respectively
$L(\tilde e_iA)$.

(3) The full tensor Fock module is represented by all standard classes; the
ground-state class, with
$M(A_\Lambda)=L(A_\Lambda)=P(A_\Lambda)$, generates only its multiplicity-one
highest constituent.

No action on labels alone proves the $K_0$ relations or the head/socle
statement.

actual_declared_use_sites.text: 1.2 **The actual surviving-head calculation.** Fix $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and let $M=f_i^{\mathcal O}L(A)$, or $M=e_i^{\mathcal O}L(A)$. The local residue theorem [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]] says $M=0$ exactly when the corresponding crystal edge is absent; otherwise its head is the simple $L(C)$ at that edge, and it is self-dual. The ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ is closed under the two crystal operators by [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], so $C$ is standard. The actual detector/corner Hom comparison of [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]] applies to maps from a Std-head object to a Std-socle object. Applying it to $M$ and $L(B)$ for each standard $B$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}_H(\pi M,D(B))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M,L(B))$, of dimension $\delta_{CB}$. Since the $D(B)$ are the complete distinct Hecke simples, this computes the head of $\pi M$ as the single simple $D(C)$ and proves $\pi M\ne0$. The natural intertwining of [[thm-category-o-translation-intertwines-residue-induction-and-restriction]] identifies $\pi M$ with the appropriate Hecke translate of $D(A)$, and its natural duality comparison makes that translate self-dual. Its socle is therefore also $D(C)$. A direct sum of two nonzero finite-length modules has at least two nonzero simple head summands, so a module with simple head is indecomposable. If the edge is absent the translate is zero by the same natural isomorphism. This proves (iii) in both directions by a Hom calculation; no arbitrary head or socle preservation by an exact quotient is assumed. [F2, given, construct, algebra]

2.2 **The Chevalley operators (ii).** The residue operators on $G_0$ are the Chevalley operators by [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]], and the corresponding statement on $K_0$ for projective classes is [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-projective-k-zero-is-the-highest-weight-module]]; on the category-O side both statements are the integrable Fock action of [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]] transferred by the actual natural residue comparisons. This proves (ii). [step 1.1, step 1.2, given, algebra]

a projective $W$-module. The composite of $V$ with the Morita equivalence is
the Serre quotient killing exactly the off-standard simples.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $\operatorname{ch}:R_S\to\Lambda$ be the Frobenius characteristic restricted
to the graded ordinary representation ring of the symmetric groups
([[def-frobenius-characteristic-map]],
[[def-graded-ordinary-representation-ring-of-symmetric-groups]]). By
[[thm-frobenius-characteristic-is-an-isometric-graded-ring-isomorphism]] it is a
degree-preserving $\mathbb Z$-module isomorphism onto the stable symmetric
function ring $\Lambda=\bigoplus_{m\ge0}\Lambda^m$, so its restriction
$\operatorname{ch}:R(S_m)\to\Lambda^m$ is an isomorphism for every $m\ge0$.

For $f\in\Lambda^m$ and $g\in\Lambda^n$ define
$$f*g:=\begin{cases}\operatorname{ch}\bigl(\operatorname{ch}^{-1}(f)\cdot\operatorname{ch}^{-1}(g)\bigr),&m=n,\\[2pt]0,&m\ne n,\end{cases}$$
where $\cdot$ is the pointwise (internal tensor) product of class functions on
$S_m$; extend $*$ bilinearly to all of $\Lambda$. Call $*$ the
**internal (Kronecker) product** of symmetric functions.

**Well-definedness.** For $m=n$ the class functions $\operatorname{ch}^{-1}(f)$
and $\operatorname{ch}^{-1}(g)$ lie in $R(S_m)$, the integral span of the
irreducible characters of $S_m$
([[def-graded-ordinary-representation-ring-of-symmetric-groups]]). The
pointwise product of two honest characters of $S_m$ is again an honest
character, namely the character of the tensor product of the underlying
representations ([[thm-characters-of-direct-sums-tensor-products-and-duals]]),
and products of $\mathbb Z$-combinations of characters are computed
bilinearly; hence the pointwise product of two elements of $R(S_m)$ lies in
$R(S_m)$, and applying the isomorphism $\operatorname{ch}$ lands in $\Lambda^m$.
The product is therefore well defined and takes $\Lambda^m\times\Lambda^m$ to
$\Lambda^m$.

**Basic properties.** The product is bilinear by construction and inherits
commutativity and associativity from the pointwise product of class functions.
It preserves degrees, in the sense that $\Lambda^m*\Lambda^n\subseteq\Lambda^m$
for $m=n$ and is $0$ for $m\ne n$. On $\Lambda^n$ the unit is
$h_n=s_{(n)}=\operatorname{ch}(\text{trivial character of }S_n)$, because the
trivial character is the unit for pointwise multiplication on $R(S_n)$
([[thm-frobenius-characteristic-sends-specht-characters-to-schur-functions]]
identifies $\operatorname{ch}(\chi^{(n)})=s_{(n)}=h_n$). The graded direct sum
$\Lambda$ has **no global unit** for $*$: if $e\in\Lambda$ had finite degree
support and $n$ were a degree with $e_n=0$ while $\Lambda^n\ne0$, then
$(e*h_n)_n=e_n*h_n=0\ne h_n$, so $e*h_n\ne h_n$; a global unit would require
$e_n$ to be a unit of $(\Lambda^n,*)$ for every $n$. In particular the ordinary
product unit $1\in\Lambda^0$ is not a unit for $*$ on the positive degrees.

**Schur expansion.** For partitions $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$, the definition and
the Specht character dictionary $\operatorname{ch}(\chi^\lambda)=s_\lambda$
([[thm-frobenius-characteristic-sends-specht-characters-to-schur-functions]])
give
$$s_\lambda*s_\mu=\operatorname{ch}\bigl(\chi^\lambda\cdot\chi^\mu\bigr)=\operatorname{ch}\Bigl(\sum_{\nu\vdash n}g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)\chi^\nu\Bigr)=\sum_{\nu\vdash n}g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)\,s_\nu,$$
because $\chi^\lambda\chi^\mu$ is the character of
$S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$ and its decomposition has multiplicities
$g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$
([[def-kronecker-coefficient-and-internal-tensor-product]]).

No form of the Axiom of Choice is used: the transport goes through the
choice-free Frobenius characteristic isomorphism and finite-dimensional
representation theory of finite groups.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Fix an integer $n\ge0$ and work over $\mathbb C$. Let $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ be
partitions of $n$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]), and let
$S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$ be the tensor product of their complex
Specht modules, a finite-dimensional complex $S_n$-module
([[def-tensor-product-of-complex-representations]],
[[def-column-antisymmetrizer-polytabloid-and-specht-module]]). The
**Kronecker coefficient** $g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ of a third partition
$\nu\vdash n$ is the multiplicity of $S^\nu$ in this tensor product:

$$g(\lambda,\mu,\nu):=\frac{\dim_{\mathbb C}\bigl(S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu\bigr)_{(S^\nu)}}{\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\nu},$$

where $\bigl(S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu\bigr)_{(S^\nu)}$ is the isotypic
component of type $S^\nu$
([[def-isotypic-component-of-a-completely-reducible-representation]]).

**Well-definedness.** The module $S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$ is
finite-dimensional, and $\operatorname{char}\mathbb C=0$ does not divide the
order of the finite group $S_n$, so complex Maschke's theorem gives complete
reducibility
([[thm-maschkes-theorem-for-finite-groups-over-fields-whose-characteristic-does-not-divide-the-group-order]],
[[cor-finite-dimensional-representations-are-completely-reducible-when-char-k-does-not-divide-group-order]],
[[def-completely-reducible-representation]]). The complex Specht modules
$S^\nu$, $\nu\vdash n$, are a complete list of pairwise inequivalent
irreducible $S_n$-modules
([[thm-complex-specht-modules-are-irreducible]],
[[thm-complex-irreducibles-of-symmetric-groups-are-specht-modules]],
[[cor-distinct-specht-modules-are-inequivalent]]). Consequently a decomposition
into irreducibles has the form
$S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu\cong\bigoplus_{\nu\vdash n}m_\nu S^\nu$
with nonnegative integer multiplicities $m_\nu$, and the isotypic component of
type $S^\nu$ is the direct sum of exactly the $m_\nu$ copies of $S^\nu$
appearing in any such decomposition; in particular
$\dim_{\mathbb C}(S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu)_{(S^\nu)}=m_\nu\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\nu$
and $\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\nu>0$ because $S^\nu$ is irreducible. Hence
$g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)=m_\nu$ is a nonnegative integer, independent of the chosen
decomposition, and $g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ is by definition the multiplicity of
$S^\nu$ in $S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$.

**The internal product.** For partitions $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ call
$$(\lambda,\mu)\longmapsto S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$$
the **internal (Kronecker) product** of the $S_n$-representations $S^\lambda$
and $S^\mu$. Unlike the outer induction product
$\operatorname{Ind}_{S_a\times S_b}^{S_{a+b}}(S^\alpha\boxtimes S^\beta)$ of
[[thm-outer-littlewood-richardson-rule]], which takes a pair of modules of
degrees $a$ and $b$ to a module of degree $a+b$, the internal product keeps the
rank: both inputs and the output are $S_n$-modules of the same degree $n$. The
two operations are different constructions on different data; the outer product
is mentioned here only for contrast and is not used in this definition.

No form of the Axiom of Choice is used: the tensor product, Maschke's theorem,
the Specht classification and the isotypic decomposition are finite-dimensional
complex representation theory of a finite group.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The **linear
contravariant anti-involution** $\sigma$ of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is defined on
generators by

$$\sigma(q)=q,\qquad\sigma(K_h)=K_h,\qquad\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1},\qquad\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i,$$

extended as an anti-algebra map, $\sigma(xy)=\sigma(y)\sigma(x)$. It is
$\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, preserves the torus (it does not invert it), and is an
involution (Verification, step 1.1). It is distinct from the semilinear
contravariant anti-involution $\tau$ with $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$,
$\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].

Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
so $\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$ for all $i$, and let $(M,v_\lambda)$ be a
**normalized highest weight module**: $M$ is a $P$-graded type-one quantum
weight module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) with
$v_\lambda\in M_\lambda$, $E_iv_\lambda=0$ for all $i$, and $M=U_q(\mathfrak g)v_\lambda$.
(The normalized simple highest weight module $L(\lambda)$ is the companion
construction later on this page; the present definition applies to any
normalized highest weight module, in particular to the Verma module and to its
simple quotient.)

A **contravariant form** on $(M,v_\lambda)$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon M\times M\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(i) $B$ is symmetric: $B(u,v)=B(v,u)$ for all $u,v\in M$;

(ii) $B$ is **homogeneous** for the label grading: $B(M_\mu,M_\tau)=0$
whenever the two labels have different toral characters, that is, whenever
$\langle\mu,h\rangle\ne\langle\tau,h\rangle$ for some $h\in P^{\vee}$;

(iii) $B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$ (the normalization);

(iv) $B$ is $\sigma$-invariant: $B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$ for all
$x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)$ and all $u,v\in M$.

Because $\sigma$ is $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear and fixes the torus, condition (iv)
is equivalent to the adjunction displays

$$B(K_hu,v)=B(u,K_hv),\qquad B(E_iu,v)=B(u,q_iF_iK_i^{-1}v),\qquad B(F_iu,v)=B(u,q_i^{-1}K_iE_iv),$$

for all $u,v\in M$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$ (Verification, step 2.1).

For $\lambda$ dominant and $L(\lambda)$ the normalized simple highest weight
module, such a form exists, is unique, and is nondegenerate on $L(\lambda)$;
moreover distinct label-weight spaces with distinct characters are orthogonal
by (ii). Uniqueness is proved here (Verification, step 4.1), as is the
orthogonality; consequently, when the pairing separates $P$, the distinct
label-weight spaces of $L(\lambda)$ are orthogonal and the restriction of $B$
to each finite-dimensional label-weight space is nondegenerate (Verification,
step 5.1). The
existence, the identification of the radical on the Verma module and the
descent to $L(\lambda)$ are proved in the local Cartan-projection lemma
`lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form`, which
is the declared justification of this definition. That lemma is proved on this
page, and its statement is the supplier of the existence and nondegeneracy
clauses above; establishing those clauses is its content rather than a claim of
this definition.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
For the same standard homogeneous general-field/general-Cartan parameters as
the integral projective theorem, the tensor pairing
$T(P,M)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes M)$ is weightwise perfect and
$A$-bilinear, with normalized cover/simple dual bases. Its associated map
$$\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}:G_0(R^\Lambda)\longrightarrow V_A(\Lambda)^\vee=\bigoplus_\beta\operatorname{Hom}_A (V_A(\Lambda)_{\Lambda-\beta},A),\qquad \Psi_{\mathrm{can}}(M)(\phi(P))=T(P,M)$$
is an isomorphism to the RESTRICTED weight dual, identified inside
$V(\Lambda)$ using the highest-weight contravariant form. It intertwines the
CANONICAL module action having the same normalization as projective $K_0$, and
sends normalized simple classes to the form-dual projective basis. The KK
module action is also sound, but its intertwiner is
$\Psi_{\mathrm{KK}}|_\beta=q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}
\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}|_\beta$. Thus an unrescaled KK identification is not
asserted to send simples to the upper global basis. The Hom pairing is instead
first-bar-sesquilinear, $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$; this does not alter the bilinear
tensor-dual identification.

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. For the standard homogeneous graded quotient over any field, with arbitrary real symmetrizable Cartan datum and admissible graded KLR parameters, there is a unique $U_A$-module isomorphism $\phi:K_0(\mathrm{Proj}\,R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)$ sending $1_\Lambda$ to $v_\Lambda$ and intertwining all normalized $E_i,F_i,K_i$ and divided powers. In particular $K_0$ is free over $A$. On the NEGATIVE half the vacuum map has exact kernel
$$\ker(U_A^-\to K_0(R^\Lambda))=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s>\lambda_i}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}.$$
This is the integral negative-half presentation; neither a full-$U_A$ quotient by only $F_i^{(\lambda_i+1)}$ nor invertibility of divided-power factorials is asserted.
For projectives, the tensor form $T(P,Q)=\mathrm{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes Q)$ transports to the highest-weight contravariant form normalized by $(v_\Lambda,v_\Lambda)=1$ and $\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$, $\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1}$, $\sigma(K_i)=K_i$. It is not the generic negative-half Lusztig form with a newly alleged radical.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
Let $A=R(\beta)$ and $B=A/J$ be the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient.
For an indecomposable finite graded projective generic cover $P(S)$,
$B\otimes_AP(S)$ is its same-head indecomposable $B$-cover if $JS=0$, and is
zero otherwise. Every graded simple/indecomposable projective $B$-orbit arises
this way, and distinct surviving heads do not merge. Finite projective Hom
duality commutes with this base change, and finite vector duality commutes with
inflation. Thus generic normalized $\#$-self-dual covers and $D_\psi$-self-dual
simples supply unique normalized $B$-covers/simples. For these labels
$h(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,S)$ and
$T(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_BS)$ are both $\delta_{P,S}$; $T$ is
bilinear and $h$ first-bar sesquilinear. Extension induces a surjection on
projective $K_0$. No Frobenius, geometric basis or cyclotomic crystal premise
is used.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
Let $F$ be a field, $q\in F^{\times}$, let
$e=e(F,q)\in\{2,3,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ be the quantum characteristic
([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]) and let
$H=H_{F,q}(S_n)$ for $n\ge0$. For $\lambda\vdash n$ let $S^{\lambda}$ be the
Hecke Specht module and $D^{\lambda}=S^{\lambda}/\mathrm{rad}\,S^{\lambda}$ its
cell-form quotient ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]). Then:

1. $D^{\lambda}\ne0$ if and only if $\lambda$ is $e$-regular
   ([[def-e-regular-and-e-restricted-partitions]]);
2. $\{D^{\lambda}:\lambda\vdash n\text{ is }e\text{-regular}\}$ is a complete
   set of pairwise non-isomorphic absolutely irreducible $H$-modules;
3. $H$ is split semisimple if and only if $e>n$ (including $e=\infty$); when
   $e\le n$ the algebra has nonzero radical.

This is the exact root-of-unity replacement for the ordinary Specht
classification. At $q=1$ in characteristic $p>0$ it specialises to the
classification of the simple $F[S_n]$-modules by $p$-regular partitions
([[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]]). No
semisimplicity is assumed and no choice principle is used.

actual_declared_use_sites.text:

absolutely simple exactly at the restricted labels, and these quotients exhaust
the ungraded simples over every stated field
([[thm-simple-type-a-hecke-modules-are-indexed-by-e-regular-partitions]]).
Every proper submodule of a nonzero-form cell lies in its form radical;
$[S(\mu):D_\lambda]\ne0$ forces $\lambda\unlhd\mu$, and
$[S(\lambda):D_\lambda]=1$
([[lem-finite-cellular-nonzero-form-heads-purity-and-shared-factor-linkage]]).
The left version is obtained through cellular star.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
For every commutative ring $R$, every $q\in R^\times$, and every partition
$\lambda\vdash n$ with row symmetrizer $m_\lambda=x_\lambda$, put
$m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^*m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$ for standard $\lambda$-tableaux $s,t$,
where $d(t)\in D_\lambda$ is the element with $t^\lambda\cdot d(t)=t$. Then:

1. $\{m_{st}:\lambda\vdash n,\ s,t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$ is an
$R$-basis of $H$ (the **Murphy basis**), and $m_{st}^*=m_{ts}$.

2. The $R$-spans $I^{\unrhd\lambda}$ of $\{m_{uv}:\mu\unrhd\lambda\}$ and
$I^{\rhd\lambda}$ of $\{m_{uv}:\mu\rhd\lambda\}$ are two-sided ideals of $H$
(dominance order), and $I^{\unrhd\lambda}/I^{\rhd\lambda}$ is free with basis
the classes of $\{m_{st}:s,t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$.

3. The **Murphy cell module**
$C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/(M(\lambda)\cap I^{\rhd\lambda})$ is free
with basis $\{m_t:=x_\lambda T_{d(t)}+I^{\rhd\lambda}:t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$
and satisfies the **cell law**: for $h\in H$ and standard $s,t$,
$$m_{st}h\equiv\sum_{v\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)}r_v\,m_{sv}\pmod{I^{\rhd\lambda}},\qquad r_v\in R,$$
with coefficients $r_v$ independent of $s$.

4. There is a unique $R$-bilinear **Murphy form** $G_\lambda$ on
$C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ with
$m_{us}m_{tv}\equiv G_\lambda(m_s,m_t)m_{uv}\pmod{I^{\rhd\lambda}}$; it is
symmetric, associative in the sense
$G_\lambda(m_sh,m_t)=G_\lambda(m_s,m_th^*)$, and its radical is a submodule of
$C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$.

5. The basis, the ideals, the cell law and the form are compatible with every
base change.

In particular $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ is finite free of rank
$f^\lambda=|\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)|$. No choice principle is used.

Let $F$ be any field, let $q\in F^\times$ have finite quantum characteristic
$e=e(F,q)\ge2$, let $\Lambda\in P^+$ be dominant and let $\alpha\in Q_+$ have
height $d$ with $e_\alpha\ne0$, in the conventions of
[[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]] and
[[def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks]]. Then the
homomorphisms $\rho\colon R^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_\alpha$ of
[[lem-hecke-intertwiners-produce-local-klr-generators]] and
$\sigma\colon H^\Lambda_\alpha\to R^\Lambda_\alpha$ of
[[lem-cyclotomic-klr-block-satisfies-the-hecke-relations]] are mutually
inverse $F$-algebra isomorphisms. Equivalently, $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ is
generated by the Khovanov–Lauda generators
$\{e(i)\}\cup\{y_r\}\cup\{\psi_r\}$ subject only to the relations
(1.6)–(1.15), and the isomorphism is normalized by
$\rho(e(i))=e(i)$ and
$$\rho(y_re(i))=(1-q^{-i_r}X_r)e(i)\quad(q\ne1),\qquad \rho(y_re(i))=(x_r-i_r)e(i)\quad(q=1).$$
The degenerate ($q=1$, $\operatorname{char}F=e$) and nondegenerate
($q\ne1$) cases are proved separately, and both hold in finite quantum
characteristic $e$.

1. (**Separation**) If $s,t$ are standard $\lambda$-tableaux with $[\operatorname{content}_s(k)]_q=[\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q$ for all $1\le k\le n$ then $s=t$. More precisely, if the q-content values agree for all $k\notin\{i,i+1\}$ for some $i$, then $s=t$ or $t=s(i\ i+1)$. 2. For every commutative ring $R$, every $q\in R^\times$, and every partition
$\lambda\vdash n$ with row symmetrizer $m_\lambda=x_\lambda$, put
$m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^*m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$ for standard $\lambda$-tableaux $s,t$,
where $d(t)\in D_\lambda$ is the element with $t^\lambda\cdot d(t)=t$. Then:

1. $\{m_{st}:\lambda\vdash n,\ s,t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$ is an
$R$-basis of $H$ (the **Murphy basis**), and $m_{st}^*=m_{ts}$.

2. The $R$-spans $I^{\unrhd\lambda}$ of $\{m_{uv}:\mu\unrhd\lambda\}$ and
$I^{\rhd\lambda}$ of $\{m_{uv}:\mu\rhd\lambda\}$ are two-sided ideals of $H$
(dominance order), and $I^{\unrhd\lambda}/I^{\rhd\lambda}$ is free with basis
the classes of $\{m_{st}:s,t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$.

3. The **Murphy cell module**
$C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/(M(\lambda)\cap I^{\rhd\lambda})$ is free
with basis $\{m_t:=x_\lambda T_{d(t)}+I^{\rhd\lambda}:t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$
and satisfies the **cell law**: for $h\in H$ and standard $s,t$,
$$m_{st}h\equiv\sum_{v\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)}r_v\,m_{sv}\pmod{I^{\rhd\lambda}},\qquad r_v\in R,$$
with coefficients $r_v$ independent of $s$.

4. There is a unique $R$-bilinear **Murphy form** $G_\lambda$ on
$C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ with
$m_{us}m_{tv}\equiv G_\lambda(m_s,m_t)m_{uv}\pmod{I^{\rhd\lambda}}$; it is
symmetric, associative in the sense
$G_\lambda(m_sh,m_t)=G_\lambda(m_s,m_th^*)$, and its radical is a submodule of
$C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$.

5. The basis, the ideals, the cell law and the form are compatible with every
base change.

In particular $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ is finite free of rank
$f^\lambda=|\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)|$. No choice principle is used.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^\times$ and $\lambda\vdash n$, and write $\mu=\lambda'$, $L=\ell(w_\lambda)$ and $N=\ell(w_0(S_{\lambda'}))$. Let $P(\lambda)=z_\lambda H$ with its DJ form $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$, the cell module $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ with its Murphy form $G_{\lambda'}$, and the sign automorphism $\theta$ be as in [[def-dj-bridge-row-column-permutation-modules-and-polytabloids]], [[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]] and [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]], and let $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta$ be the $\theta$-twisted cell module of [[lem-dj-bridge-theta-transport-of-the-cellular-structure]]. Then:

1. There is a base-change compatible isomorphism of right $H$-modules $$\Phi_\lambda\colon P(\lambda)\longrightarrow C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta,\qquad \Phi_\lambda(z_\lambda)=m_0,\quad \Phi_\lambda(z_\lambda h)=m_0\theta(h)\ \ (h\in H),$$ where $m_0$ is the class of $x_{\lambda'}$ in $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ and the right side is computed with the ordinary action on $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ and read in the twist; in particular $\Phi_\lambda(e_t)=m_0\theta(T_{d_{\lambda'}(t)})$ for $t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda')$. For a class $m\in C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ and any lift $\widetilde m\in M(\lambda')$, the inverse is $\Phi_\lambda^{-1}(m)=q^{-N}x_\lambda T_{w_\lambda}\theta(\widetilde m)$, independently of the chosen lift.

2. With $G_{\lambda'}^\theta$ the transported form of [[lem-dj-bridge-theta-transport-of-the-cellular-structure]] and $u_\lambda(q):=q^{\ell(w_0(S_{\lambda'}))-\ell(w_\lambda)}\in A^\times$, $$G_{\lambda'}^\theta(\Phi_\lambda x,\Phi_\lambda y)=u_\lambda(q)\,\beta_{P(\lambda)}(x,y)\qquad(x,y\in P(\lambda)),$$ over every commutative $R$ with $q\in R^\times$. No unnamed scalar and no potentially vanishing scalar occurs: $u_\lambda$ is the explicit unit $q^{N-L}$ in the fixed normalizations of this page.

3. Consequently $\Phi_\lambda$ maps the radical of $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$ onto the radical of $G_{\lambda'}^\theta$, the induced map between the quotients is an isomorphism, with the corresponding cell-form quotients $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}\cong(D^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^\theta$, including the zero-quotient case. Over a field, when the quotients are nonzero they are the simple heads; when the forms are identically zero, the displayed quotients are zero and no assertion about the actual module heads is made. Over a PID with a chosen prime, the unit-scaled form identity preserves all divisibility submodules and their reductions. One also obtains $P(\lambda')\cong P(\lambda)^{\circ,\theta}$ with the exact position of the dual and the twist, separating same-shape duality from conjugate-sign transport. No choice principle is used.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
Let $F$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital cellular $F$-algebra with
cellular basis $(C,\Lambda)$ over the finite poset $\Lambda$
([[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]). For $\lambda\in\Lambda$
put $D^{\lambda}:=C^{\lambda}/\mathrm{rad}\,C^{\lambda}$, where
$\mathrm{rad}\,C^{\lambda}$ is the radical of the cell form
([[lem-cell-form-is-associative-and-its-radical-is-a-submodule]]). Then:

1. if $D^{\lambda}\ne0$ then $D^{\lambda}$ is an absolutely irreducible
   (absolutely simple) $A$-module: it is simple over $F$ and remains simple
   after every extension of scalars to a larger field;
2. $\{D^{\lambda}:\lambda\in\Lambda,\ D^{\lambda}\ne0\}$ is a complete set of
   pairwise non-isomorphic simple $A$-modules ([[def-simple-module]],
   [[thm-jordan-holder-theorem-for-modules]]);
3. $D^{\lambda}\ne0$ if and only if the cell form
   $\langle\ ,\ \rangle_\lambda$ is not identically zero, if and only if
   $\mathrm{rad}\,C^{\lambda}\ne C^{\lambda}$; and, when these equivalent
   conditions hold, $\mathrm{rad}\,C^{\lambda}$ is the unique maximal proper
   submodule and the Jacobson radical of $C^{\lambda}$, so $D^{\lambda}$ is its
   simple head. If the form is identically zero, the cell-form quotient
   $D^{\lambda}$ is zero; no assertion about the Jacobson radical or the actual
   head of $C^{\lambda}$ is made.

No semisimplicity of $A$ is assumed; the theorem is the Graham-Lehrer
classification and applies in particular to $A=H_{F,q}(S_n)$ for every field
$F$ and every $q\in F^{\times}$.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, i.e. a classical
algebraic variety over $\mathbb C$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), regarded as
a topological space with its analytic topology
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]), and
let $k$ be a field. Write $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves
of $k$-vector spaces and $k$-linear morphisms
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is
an abelian category ([[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]), so its
bounded derived category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is defined with the
conventions of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]], under the
standing smallness hypothesis recorded there.

The category $D_c^b(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ consisting of the complexes $A$ satisfying:

1. $A$ is **cohomologically bounded**: $H^j(A)=0$ for $|j|$ sufficiently large;
   and
2. $A$ is **algebraically constructible**: there exists a finite smooth
   algebraic stratification with the frontier condition $\mathfrak S$ of $X$
   ([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]) such
   that for every stratum $S\in\mathfrak S$ and every integer $j$ the
   restriction $H^j(A)|_S$ is locally constant of finite rank
   ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]).

These are topological constructible sheaves, not coherent or quasi-coherent
sheaves. We use the shift convention of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]: $H^j(A[m])=H^{j+m}(A)$. A
groupoid local system is identified with a locally constant sheaf only through
an explicit local comparison, which is not made here.

Constructibility is a condition on the cohomology sheaves of a complex, and it
is quantified existentially over finite smooth algebraic frontier
stratifications: no stratification is fixed, and no existence or
common-refinement theorem for stratifications is asserted by this definition.
Shifting replaces $H^j$ by $H^{j+m}$, which preserves cohomological boundedness
and shifts a witnessing stratification nowhere, so the class is closed under
shifts and under isomorphisms in $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$. No choice
principle is used.

actual_declared_use_sites.text: [F6] Sheaves and derived global sections ([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]], [[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]], [[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]], [[lem-locally-contractible-metric-spaces-have-singular-constant-sheaf-cohomology]]). Sheaf cohomology is the right derived global-sections functor computed from a supplied functorial injective resolution datum, independent of the datum up to natural isomorphism; for a bounded-below complex of sheaves the same construction is applied to a filtered injective resolution and computes the hypercohomology. On a metric space with a neighbourhood basis of contractible open sets, constant-sheaf cohomology agrees with singular cohomology on every open subset.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_k)$ be a partition with $|\alpha|=\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_k$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]), and let $n\ge0$ be
an integer. Whenever

$$n\;\ge\;|\alpha|+\alpha_1,$$

define the **first-row padding** of $\alpha$ to size $n$ to be
$$\alpha[n]:=\bigl(n-|\alpha|,\ \alpha_1,\ \alpha_2,\ \dots,\ \alpha_k\bigr).$$

The threshold is exact.

**Above the threshold.** Suppose $n\ge|\alpha|+\alpha_1$. Then
$n-|\alpha|\ge\alpha_1\ge0$, so every entry of the displayed sequence is a
nonnegative integer, the entries sum to $(n-|\alpha|)+|\alpha|=n$, and the
sequence is weakly decreasing because $n-|\alpha|\ge\alpha_1$ and $\alpha$ is
weakly decreasing ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).
If $\alpha$ is nonempty then $\alpha_1\ge1$, hence $n-|\alpha|\ge1$ and the
displayed sequence is a partition of $n$ with positive parts. If
$\alpha=\varnothing$ then the displayed sequence is $(n)$; this is a partition
of $n$ for every $n\ge1$, while for $n=0$ one takes $\varnothing[0]:=\varnothing$,
the unique partition of $0$. Thus the padding is defined and is a partition of
$n$ on the whole displayed range.

**Below the threshold.** If $\alpha$ is nonempty and $n<|\alpha|+\alpha_1$,
then $n-|\alpha|<\alpha_1$; if also $n\ge|\alpha|$ the leading entry is
nonnegative but smaller than the second entry $\alpha_1$, and if $n<|\alpha|$
it is negative. In both cases the displayed sequence is not a partition, so
$\alpha[n]$ is left undefined. The threshold $|\alpha|+\alpha_1$ is therefore
the exact size at which the padded family begins: at
$n=|\alpha|+\alpha_1$ the padding equals $(\alpha_1,\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\dots)$,
which is a partition with a repeated first part when $\alpha$ is nonempty.

**Neutrality of the notation.** This definition records a family of partitions;
it asserts no constancy of any quantity along the family and no stability
property. The same notation is used by the FI-module and
representation-stability developments, where the padding threshold reappears as
the generation degree of the family under consideration.

an identity in the symmetric function ring, where $s_{\gamma[n]}$ is the
Jacobi–Trudi determinant attached to the integer sequence

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Fix an integer $n\ge0$ and work over $\mathbb C$. Let $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ be
partitions of $n$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]), and let
$S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$ be the tensor product of their complex
Specht modules, a finite-dimensional complex $S_n$-module
([[def-tensor-product-of-complex-representations]],
[[def-column-antisymmetrizer-polytabloid-and-specht-module]]). The
**Kronecker coefficient** $g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ of a third partition
$\nu\vdash n$ is the multiplicity of $S^\nu$ in this tensor product:

$$g(\lambda,\mu,\nu):=\frac{\dim_{\mathbb C}\bigl(S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu\bigr)_{(S^\nu)}}{\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\nu},$$

where $\bigl(S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu\bigr)_{(S^\nu)}$ is the isotypic
component of type $S^\nu$
([[def-isotypic-component-of-a-completely-reducible-representation]]).

**Well-definedness.** The module $S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$ is
finite-dimensional, and $\operatorname{char}\mathbb C=0$ does not divide the
order of the finite group $S_n$, so complex Maschke's theorem gives complete
reducibility
([[thm-maschkes-theorem-for-finite-groups-over-fields-whose-characteristic-does-not-divide-the-group-order]],
[[cor-finite-dimensional-representations-are-completely-reducible-when-char-k-does-not-divide-group-order]],
[[def-completely-reducible-representation]]). The complex Specht modules
$S^\nu$, $\nu\vdash n$, are a complete list of pairwise inequivalent
irreducible $S_n$-modules
([[thm-complex-specht-modules-are-irreducible]],
[[thm-complex-irreducibles-of-symmetric-groups-are-specht-modules]],
[[cor-distinct-specht-modules-are-inequivalent]]). Consequently a decomposition
into irreducibles has the form
$S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu\cong\bigoplus_{\nu\vdash n}m_\nu S^\nu$
with nonnegative integer multiplicities $m_\nu$, and the isotypic component of
type $S^\nu$ is the direct sum of exactly the $m_\nu$ copies of $S^\nu$
appearing in any such decomposition; in particular
$\dim_{\mathbb C}(S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu)_{(S^\nu)}=m_\nu\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\nu$
and $\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\nu>0$ because $S^\nu$ is irreducible. Hence
$g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)=m_\nu$ is a nonnegative integer, independent of the chosen
decomposition, and $g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ is by definition the multiplicity of
$S^\nu$ in $S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$.

**The internal product.** For partitions $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ call
$$(\lambda,\mu)\longmapsto S^\lambda\otimes_{\mathbb C}S^\mu$$
the **internal (Kronecker) product** of the $S_n$-representations $S^\lambda$
and $S^\mu$. Unlike the outer induction product
$\operatorname{Ind}_{S_a\times S_b}^{S_{a+b}}(S^\alpha\boxtimes S^\beta)$ of
[[thm-outer-littlewood-richardson-rule]], which takes a pair of modules of
degrees $a$ and $b$ to a module of degree $a+b$, the internal product keeps the
rank: both inputs and the output are $S_n$-modules of the same degree $n$. The
two operations are different constructions on different data; the outer product
is mentioned here only for contrast and is not used in this definition.

No form of the Axiom of Choice is used: the tensor product, Maschke's theorem,
the Specht classification and the isotypic decomposition are finite-dimensional
complex representation theory of a finite group.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$. A **consistent sequence** is a
sequence $(V_n,\varphi_n)_{n\ge0}$ in which each $V_n$ is a finite-dimensional
left $kS_n$-module and each $\varphi_n\colon V_n\to V_{n+1}$ is
$S_n$-equivariant, the target being regarded as an $S_n$-module by restriction
along the standard inclusion $S_n\hookrightarrow S_{n+1}$ that fixes $n$. An
FI-module $V$ over $k$ with finite-dimensional values
([[def-fi-category-and-fi-module]]) determines such a sequence by
$V_n:=V([n])$ and $\varphi_n:=f_*$ for the standard inclusions
$f\colon[n]\to[n+1]$; these maps are $S_n$-equivariant by functoriality and the
conjugation action, since $f\circ\sigma=\Phi_f(\sigma)\circ f$ with
$\Phi_f(\sigma)$ the extension of $\sigma$ by the fixed point $n$.

The sequence is **uniformly representation stable with stable range $n\ge N$**
when all three of the following hold.

1. **(I) Injectivity.** The map $\varphi_n\colon V_n\to V_{n+1}$ is injective for
   every $n\ge N$.
2. **(II) Surjectivity.** The $S_{n+1}$-span of the image $\varphi_n(V_n)$ is
   all of $V_{n+1}$ for every $n\ge N$.
3. **(III) Multiplicities.** For each partition $\lambda$ and each $n$ with
   $n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$, let $V(\lambda)_n$ be the irreducible $kS_n$-module
   indexed by the first-row padding $\lambda[n]=(n-|\lambda|,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots)$
   ([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]), namely the scalar extension
   $k\otimes_{\mathbb Q}S^{\lambda[n]}_{\mathbb Q}$ of the rational Specht model,
   which is the unique irreducible $kS_n$-module with that label
   ([[lem-specht-modules-classify-irreducibles-over-characteristic-zero-fields]];
   over $\mathbb C$ this is the published complex Specht classification
   [[thm-complex-specht-modules-are-irreducible]]). Decompose
   $V_n\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda}c_{\lambda,n}V(\lambda)_n$ with multiplicities
   $c_{\lambda,n}\ge0$, the sum over those $\lambda$ with
   $n\ge|\lambda|+\lambda_1$. Then for every fixed $\lambda$ the multiplicity
   $c_{\lambda,n}$ is independent of $n$ for all $n\ge N$.

The sequence is **uniformly representation stable** when it is so for some
$N\ge0$. All three conditions are part of the definition, and (II) is not a
consequence of (I) and (III): the sequence with $V_n=k^2$ carrying the trivial
$S_n$-action and $\varphi_n$ the inclusion of the first coordinate is injective
and has constant multiplicities $c_{\varnothing,n}=2$, but its images span only
a one-dimensional subspace of $V_{n+1}$. No choice principle is used.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and let $n\ge0$. For every partition
$\lambda\vdash n$ the field-valued Specht module $S^\lambda_F$ of
[[def-polytabloid-specht-module-over-an-arbitrary-field]] is nonzero and
irreducible, distinct partitions give non-isomorphic modules, and every
irreducible $FS_n$-module is isomorphic to exactly one of them. Consequently,
by Maschke's theorem, every finite-dimensional $FS_n$-module is a direct sum of
copies of the $S^\lambda_F$; thus the irreducible $FS_n$-modules are indexed by
the partitions of $n$ and the modules $\{S^\lambda_F:\lambda\vdash n\}$ form a
complete irredundant list.

This is the constituent convention used throughout the pair: over
$F=\mathbb C$ it specialises to the published complex classification, and over
a general characteristic-zero field $F$ it is proved by extending the rational
Specht models along $\mathbb Q\to F$, never by a scalar extension from
$\mathbb C$ to $F$.

required_interface.text:
For every commutative ring $R$, every $q\in R^\times$, and every partition
$\lambda\vdash n$ with row symmetrizer $m_\lambda=x_\lambda$, put
$m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^*m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$ for standard $\lambda$-tableaux $s,t$,
where $d(t)\in D_\lambda$ is the element with $t^\lambda\cdot d(t)=t$. Then:

1. $\{m_{st}:\lambda\vdash n,\ s,t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$ is an
$R$-basis of $H$ (the **Murphy basis**), and $m_{st}^*=m_{ts}$.

2. The $R$-spans $I^{\unrhd\lambda}$ of $\{m_{uv}:\mu\unrhd\lambda\}$ and
$I^{\rhd\lambda}$ of $\{m_{uv}:\mu\rhd\lambda\}$ are two-sided ideals of $H$
(dominance order), and $I^{\unrhd\lambda}/I^{\rhd\lambda}$ is free with basis
the classes of $\{m_{st}:s,t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$.

3. The **Murphy cell module**
$C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/(M(\lambda)\cap I^{\rhd\lambda})$ is free
with basis $\{m_t:=x_\lambda T_{d(t)}+I^{\rhd\lambda}:t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$
and satisfies the **cell law**: for $h\in H$ and standard $s,t$,
$$m_{st}h\equiv\sum_{v\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)}r_v\,m_{sv}\pmod{I^{\rhd\lambda}},\qquad r_v\in R,$$
with coefficients $r_v$ independent of $s$.

4. There is a unique $R$-bilinear **Murphy form** $G_\lambda$ on
$C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ with
$m_{us}m_{tv}\equiv G_\lambda(m_s,m_t)m_{uv}\pmod{I^{\rhd\lambda}}$; it is
symmetric, associative in the sense
$G_\lambda(m_sh,m_t)=G_\lambda(m_s,m_th^*)$, and its radical is a submodule of
$C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$.

5. The basis, the ideals, the cell law and the form are compatible with every
base change.

In particular $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ is finite free of rank
$f^\lambda=|\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)|$. No choice principle is used.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^\times$ and $\lambda\vdash n$, and let $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ with its basis $\{m_t\}$, $P(\lambda)=z_\lambda H$, the permutation form $\beta$ on $M(\lambda)$ and the DJ form on $P(\lambda)$ be as in [[def-dj-bridge-row-column-permutation-modules-and-polytabloids]], [[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]] and [[lem-dj-bridge-integral-murphy-and-polytabloid-straightening]]. Then:

1. Setting $B_\lambda(m_s,p):=\beta(x_\lambda T_{d_\lambda(s)},p)$ for $s\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)$ and $p\in P(\lambda)$ defines an explicit $R$-bilinear pairing $B_\lambda\colon C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)\times P(\lambda)\to R$ that is $H$-balanced, $B_\lambda(mh,p)=B_\lambda(m,ph^*)$, and whose adjoint $c\mapsto B_\lambda(c,-)$ is an isomorphism of right $H$-modules $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)\to P(\lambda)^\circ$ onto the star-contragredient module of [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]. No nondegeneracy of the DJ form $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$ is required.

2. Equivalently, the kernel of the quotient map $M(\lambda)\to C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ is the orthogonal complement $P(\lambda)^\perp=\{a\in M(\lambda):\beta(a,p)=0\text{ for all }p\in P(\lambda)\}$, namely $M(\lambda)\cap I^{\rhd\lambda}$; the pairing matrices in the bases $\{m_s\}$ and $\{e_t\}$ have entries $B_\lambda(m_s,e_t)=q^{\ell(d_\lambda(s))}a_{d_\lambda(s),t}$ with $e_t=\sum_d a_{d,t}b_d$, and determinant a unit of $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$. Their inverses are finite tableau formulas given by the adjugate divided by this unit.

3. All statements are compatible with every base change $A\to R$, $v\mapsto q$; the construction uses no generic semisimplicity, no nondegeneracy of $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$ and no choice principle.

actual_declared_use_sites.text: [F2] The central transposition class sum $T_m$ acts on the ordinary integral Specht lattice and every field specialization by the total content $z_\xi=\sum_{(r,c)\in[\xi]}(c-r)$ ([[lem-transposition-class-sum-acts-on-a-specht-module-by-total-content]]). At $m=0,1$, both the class sum and total content are zero directly. The actual same-shape perfect pairing identifies the Murphy cell $C_{\mathrm M}(\xi)$ with the star dual of the ordinary Specht module ([[thm-dj-bridge-murphy-cell-is-the-same-shape-specht-dual]]). Let $i\in I$, write $z=q_i$, and let $V(a)$, $V(b)$ be the simple rank-one modules of nonnegative integral highest weights $a,b$ for the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$, with divided bases $v_j=F_i^{(j)}v_0$ $(0\le j\le a)$ and $w_k=F_i^{(k)}w_0$ $(0\le k\le b)$ ([[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]]). Consider the tensor product with the coproduct $\Delta E_i=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$, $\Delta F_i=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$ ([[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]), its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]]) and the $\mathbb Z$-graded $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space $V(a)\otimes V(b)$ with the tensor lattice
$$L:=\bigoplus_{j=0}^{a}\bigoplus_{k=0}^{b}A_0\,(v_j\otimes w_k)$$
over the local ring $A_0$ ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]). Then:

(i) $L$ is a crystal lattice: it is a free $A_0$-module generating $V(a)\otimes V(b)$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, it respects the weight grading, and $\tilde e_iL\subseteq L$, $\tilde f_iL\subseteq L$.

(ii) Modulo $q$ one has, for all $0\le j\le a$, $0\le k\le b$,
$$\tilde f_i(v_j\otimes w_k)=\begin{cases}v_{j+1}\otimes w_k & \text{if } a-j>k,\\ v_j\otimes w_{k+1} & \text{if } a-j\le k,\end{cases}$$
and
$$\tilde e_i(v_j\otimes w_k)=\begin{cases}v_{j-1}\otimes w_k & \text{if } a-j\ge k,\\ v_j\otimes w_{k-1} & \text{if } a-j<k,\end{cases}$$
where terms leaving the divided-basis ranges are $0$. In particular $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$ for residues $b,b'$ of the product basis (the partial-inverse property).

(iii) The nonzero residue strings are the chains $(0,t),(1,t),\dots,(a-t,t),(a-t,t+1),\dots,(a-t,b)$, $0\le t\le\min(a,b)$, and they partition the rectangle $0\le j\le a$, $0\le k\le b$.

This is a finite, choice-free calculation, independent of the grand loop and of global integral freeness.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups acting algebraically on a separated finite-type complex
algebraic variety $X$, and let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero. For
bounded algebraically constructible $A,B$ in the equivariant category
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ of
[[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]:

1. every $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ is
   finite-dimensional over $k$ and vanishes for all sufficiently negative $m$;
2. for every field extension $k\to K$ of characteristic-zero fields, the
   canonical map
   $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)\otimes_kK\to\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A_K,B_K)$
   is an isomorphism, natural in $A$ and $B$ and compatible with shifts and
   with Yoneda composition;
3. coefficient extension commutes with the coherent six operations, normalized
   Verdier duality, perverse truncation and intermediate extension on these
   bounded constructible objects.

The total Ext space $\bigoplus_m\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)$ need not be
finite-dimensional, and simplicity is not asserted to be preserved under
coefficient extension.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$\mathfrak p=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
be as in [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]. Then:

**(1) (Simples.)** Within an integral block, $L(\lambda)\in\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
if and only if $\lambda$ is $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral; every simple
object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is of this form.

**(2) (Standards.)** For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the
generalized Verma $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$,
has finite length, has $L(\lambda)$ as its unique simple quotient (head), and
$[M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):L(\mu)]\neq0$ forces $\mu\le\lambda$ in the
dominance order; $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the largest quotient of
$M(\lambda)$ lying in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.

**(3) (Enough projectives.)** The inclusion
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathcal O$ is exact and has a left adjoint
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ (the largest $\mathfrak p$-locally-finite quotient);
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ is right exact and sends projective objects of $\mathcal O$
to projective objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. Consequently, for every
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the object
$P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=L_{\mathfrak p}(P^{(\mathcal O)}(\lambda))$ is a
projective cover of $L(\lambda)$ in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, and
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ has enough projectives and injectives.

**(4) (Generalized-standard flags, BGG reciprocity and duality.)** Every
projective in a fixed integral block has a finite generalized Verma flag. Its
projective cover surjects to its labelled generalized standard with a kernel
filtered by higher-labelled generalized standards. The simple and
generalized-standard classes form bases of the finite block Grothendieck
group, and characters are injective on this group. For $\mathfrak p$-dominant
integral $\lambda,\mu$,
$$(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=[M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
the multiplicities being finite; moreover restricted duality restricts to an
exact contravariant involution of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ exchanging
$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ and $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda),\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=0$
for all $\lambda,\mu$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and that $I$ is bounded
below, so $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are finite; the upper end of
$I$ may remain unbounded. Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n(\mathbb C)$ and let
the standard parabolic $\mathfrak p$ have Levi
$\mathfrak{gl}_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{n_l}$
([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]).
For a tableau $A$ let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ be its ordinary highest-weight
reading: read columns from left to right and each column from top to bottom,
so its entries are strictly decreasing. This is also the normally ordered column reading of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]. Put
$$\lambda_A=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(a_j+j-1)\,\varepsilon_j .$$
Strict columns make $\lambda_A$ Levi-dominant, so that the simple highest weight
module $L(A)$ of [[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]
and the induced generalized standard
$M(A)=M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda_A)$ of
[[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]] belong to the genuine
parabolic category $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ of
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]].

Use the published **half-sum convention**
$\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$; then
$$\lambda_{A,j}+\rho_j=a_j+\frac{n-1}{2},$$
so the $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ Harish-Chandra shifted-coordinate multiset of the
block is the tableau-entry multiset plus the common scalar $(n-1)/2$, and this
multiset together with the displayed scalar $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ centre labels the
central character ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]). The Fock
weight $\sum_j\delta_{a_j}=\Lambda-\alpha$ of the Fock item belongs to the
different $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ weight lattice and indexes that entry multiset;
it is **not** a literal $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ highest weight.

For an entry multiset $\alpha$ the corresponding **finite parabolic central
block** $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ has labels
$\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$, generalized standards $M(A)$, simples $L(A)$,
projective covers $P(A)$ and costandards $\nabla(A)$, with the BGG reciprocity,
restricted duality and highest-weight structure inherited from
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]; by
[[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]] it is a single
linkage block. Its simple and standard classes form bases of its Grothendieck
group, and its numerical multiplicities include repeated-entry singular central
characters. The direct sum over the admitted entry multisets is
$\mathcal O^\Lambda$. **Opposite blocks** use the reversed Levi order and the
reverse-column reading, with the correspondingly reversed label order
([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]).

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be a field of
characteristic zero. On the equivariant constructible derived category
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ of
[[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]],
middle perversity is defined on smooth complex strata $S$ by the two
inequalities $H^q(i_S^*A)=0$ for $q>-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$ and
$H^q(i_S^!A)=0$ for $q<-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$, where $i_S$ is the inclusion of a
stratum. These inequalities give a bounded t-structure independent of
compatible refinement and gluing across algebraic open/closed decompositions,
and the equivariant structure is detected by restriction to $X$. Its heart is
abelian of finite length, and its simple objects are the intermediate
extensions $\operatorname{IC}_Z(L)=j_{!*}L[\dim_{\mathbb C}Z]$ of simple
finite-rank local systems $L$ on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports
$Z$, with equivariant data in the equivariant category. If $A,B$ lie in the
heart, then $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])=0$ for $m<0$. A simple object's
endomorphism ring is a division $k$-algebra, not asserted to equal $k$.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited. In the setting of
[[def-quiver-full-flag-incidence-varieties-and-geometric-klr-generators]], the convolution
algebra $\mathfrak A=\bigoplus_{\eta,\nu}\operatorname{Ext}_G(L_\eta,L_\nu)$ acts by
correspondence composition on the direct sum $P=\bigoplus_\nu P_\nu$ of shifted polynomial
summands $P_\nu=H_G^\bullet(X_\nu;k)[d_\nu]$, where the unit of $P_\nu$ has degree $-d_\nu$
and every $x_r$ has degree $2$, and this action is faithful; here
$H_G^\bullet(X_\nu;k)=k[x_1,\dots,x_m]$ with $m=\sum_i\beta_i$, the variables being the
classes $x_r=c_1^G(F^r/F^{r-1})$ of the preceding definition. Fix one reduced expression of
every $w\in S_m$ and let $\tau_we_\nu$ be the corresponding product of elementary crossings of
[[def-quiver-full-flag-incidence-varieties-and-geometric-klr-generators]]. Then the elements
$x_1^{c_1}\cdots x_m^{c_m}\tau_we_\nu$ with $c_r\ge0$ form a $k$-basis of $\mathfrak A$;
equivalently, the $\tau_we_\nu$ form a free basis of $\mathfrak A$ over the first-coordinate
polynomial corners $k[x_1,\dots,x_m]$, the polynomials acting by left multiplication. In
particular the dots and the elementary crossings generate $\mathfrak A$. Only relative-position
incidence strata are paved; nothing is asserted about arbitrary stable-flag fibers of
$\pi_\nu$.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
For every commutative ring $R$, every $q\in R^\times$, and every partition
$\lambda\vdash n$ with row symmetrizer $m_\lambda=x_\lambda$, put
$m_{st}:=T_{d(s)}^*m_\lambda T_{d(t)}$ for standard $\lambda$-tableaux $s,t$,
where $d(t)\in D_\lambda$ is the element with $t^\lambda\cdot d(t)=t$. Then:

1. $\{m_{st}:\lambda\vdash n,\ s,t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$ is an
$R$-basis of $H$ (the **Murphy basis**), and $m_{st}^*=m_{ts}$.

2. The $R$-spans $I^{\unrhd\lambda}$ of $\{m_{uv}:\mu\unrhd\lambda\}$ and
$I^{\rhd\lambda}$ of $\{m_{uv}:\mu\rhd\lambda\}$ are two-sided ideals of $H$
(dominance order), and $I^{\unrhd\lambda}/I^{\rhd\lambda}$ is free with basis
the classes of $\{m_{st}:s,t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$.

3. The **Murphy cell module**
$C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/(M(\lambda)\cap I^{\rhd\lambda})$ is free
with basis $\{m_t:=x_\lambda T_{d(t)}+I^{\rhd\lambda}:t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)\}$
and satisfies the **cell law**: for $h\in H$ and standard $s,t$,
$$m_{st}h\equiv\sum_{v\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)}r_v\,m_{sv}\pmod{I^{\rhd\lambda}},\qquad r_v\in R,$$
with coefficients $r_v$ independent of $s$.

4. There is a unique $R$-bilinear **Murphy form** $G_\lambda$ on
$C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ with
$m_{us}m_{tv}\equiv G_\lambda(m_s,m_t)m_{uv}\pmod{I^{\rhd\lambda}}$; it is
symmetric, associative in the sense
$G_\lambda(m_sh,m_t)=G_\lambda(m_s,m_th^*)$, and its radical is a submodule of
$C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$.

5. The basis, the ideals, the cell law and the form are compatible with every
base change.

In particular $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ is finite free of rank
$f^\lambda=|\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)|$. No choice principle is used.

For a row group $S_\alpha$, $x_\alpha^2=[\alpha]!_Qx_\alpha$ by length-additive parabolic cosets; $[\alpha]!_Q=\prod_j[\alpha_j]!_Q$ ([[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]]).

[[def-dj-bridge-row-column-permutation-modules-and-polytabloids]], for every
commutative ring $R$ and every $q\in R^\times$:

1. $M(\lambda)$ is free with basis $\{x_\lambda T_d:d\in D_\lambda\}$;

2. $x_\lambda T_w=q^{\ell(w)}x_\lambda$ and $T_wx_\lambda=q^{\ell(w)}x_\lambda$
for every $w\in S_\lambda$, and $x_\lambda^*=x_\lambda$;

3. if $d\in D_\lambda$, $t=t^\lambda\cdot d$ and $s=t\cdot s_i=t^\lambda\cdot d'$, then
$$x_\lambda T_dT_i=\begin{cases}q\,x_\lambda T_d,&s\text{ is not row standard},\\ x_\lambda T_{d'},&s\text{ is row standard and }\ell(d')>\ell(d),\\ q\,x_\lambda T_{d'}+(q-1)x_\lambda T_d,&s\text{ is row standard and }\ell(d')<\ell(d);\end{cases}$$

4. the basis and the action formulas are compatible with every base change
$R\to R'$ along a ring map sending $q$ to a unit.

No choice principle is used.

Let $M_1,M_2$ be integrable chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight modules with crystal bases $(L_1,B_1)$, $(L_2,B_2)$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]), and let $M_1\otimes M_2$ be the integrable module of [[lem-tensor-products-of-integrable-weight-modules-are-integrable]].

Then $(L_1\otimes_{A_0}L_2,\,B_1\otimes B_2)$ is a crystal basis of $M_1\otimes M_2$, and its crystal is the tensor product crystal $B_1\otimes B_2$ of [[def-tensor-product-of-crystals]]: for all $b_1\in B_1$, $b_2\in B_2$ and $i\in I$,

$$\tilde f_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=\begin{cases}\tilde f_ib_1\otimes b_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)>\varepsilon_i(b_2),\\ b_1\otimes\tilde f_ib_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)\le\varepsilon_i(b_2),\end{cases}\qquad \tilde e_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=\begin{cases}\tilde e_ib_1\otimes b_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)\ge\varepsilon_i(b_2),\\ b_1\otimes\tilde e_ib_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)<\varepsilon_i(b_2),\end{cases}$$

with value $0$ as soon as the selected factor maps to $0$. In particular $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ map $B_1\otimes B_2$ into $(B_1\otimes B_2)\cup\{0\}$, and for all $b,b'\in B_1\otimes B_2$ one has $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$, so the partial-inverse axiom holds. The equality case $\varphi_i(b_1)=\varepsilon_i(b_2)$ is resolved as in the definition: $\tilde f_i$ acts on the second factor and $\tilde e_i$ on the first.

No finite dimensionality, bounded support or uniform nilpotence is assumed, and no choice principle is used.

Let $\lambda\in P$ be a dominant integral label weight, put
$m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the quantum Verma
module with highest vector $v_\lambda$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]],

(i) The quotient $\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$
is nonzero, has finite-dimensional label weights and support
$\lambda-Q_+$, is integrable, and equals the canonical simple highest weight
module $L(\lambda)$, which is simple also as an ordinary (not assumed graded)
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module.

(ii) **Universality.** Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of
highest weight $\lambda$ with highest vector $v\ne0$ receives a
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $\tilde L(\lambda)\to V$ with
$\bar v_\lambda\mapsto v$, and this map is unique; every nonzero such $V$ is
isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$.

(iii) Its character equals the classical integrable highest weight character of
the explicitly regularized realization of the datum. No global
$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness and no crystal or global basis is used.

Let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$, let $L^-:=\psi(L)$ be the bar lattice, all as in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]] and [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]], and let $E_{\mathbb Z}:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ be the balanced intersection. Let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$.

By [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-triple-is-balanced]] the integral triple $(M_A,L,L^-)$ is balanced componentwise: for every root or label degree the canonical map $E_{\mathbb Z}\to(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is an isomorphism onto the free $\mathbb Z$-span $\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B}\mathbb Zb$ of the crystal classes of that degree. For $b\in\mathcal B$ define the **lower global lift** $G(b)$ to be the unique element of $E_{\mathbb Z}$ whose residue class in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$. The family $G(\mathcal B)$ is the **lower global basis** of $M_A$ (of $U_A^-$ or of $V_A(\lambda)$).

With these definitions, the theorem's extensions give the basis assertions: the $A$-span of $G(\mathcal B)$ is $M_A$, its $A_0$-span is $L$, its $A_\infty$-span is $L^-$, and its $\mathbb Z$-span is $E_{\mathbb Z}$, while after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ the residue classes of the $G(b)$ are the full rational crystal spaces; in particular $G(\mathcal B)$ is an $A$-basis of $M_A$. Each $G(b)$ is bar fixed, $G(0)$ is not defined, and no equality of $E_{\mathbb Z}$ with the whole Laurent module $M_A$ is implied; the identification of the integral residue subgroup with $\mathbb Z\mathcal B(\lambda)$ for highest modules is the corresponding part of the same theorem. The lifts are characterized by the simultaneous balanced intersection, not by an unproved unitriangular word-basis condition, and all definitions apply componentwise on finite root or label components and are extended by their direct sums.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The **linear
contravariant anti-involution** $\sigma$ of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is defined on
generators by

$$\sigma(q)=q,\qquad\sigma(K_h)=K_h,\qquad\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1},\qquad\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i,$$

extended as an anti-algebra map, $\sigma(xy)=\sigma(y)\sigma(x)$. It is
$\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, preserves the torus (it does not invert it), and is an
involution (Verification, step 1.1). It is distinct from the semilinear
contravariant anti-involution $\tau$ with $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$,
$\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].

Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
so $\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$ for all $i$, and let $(M,v_\lambda)$ be a
**normalized highest weight module**: $M$ is a $P$-graded type-one quantum
weight module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) with
$v_\lambda\in M_\lambda$, $E_iv_\lambda=0$ for all $i$, and $M=U_q(\mathfrak g)v_\lambda$.
(The normalized simple highest weight module $L(\lambda)$ is the companion
construction later on this page; the present definition applies to any
normalized highest weight module, in particular to the Verma module and to its
simple quotient.)

A **contravariant form** on $(M,v_\lambda)$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon M\times M\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(i) $B$ is symmetric: $B(u,v)=B(v,u)$ for all $u,v\in M$;

(ii) $B$ is **homogeneous** for the label grading: $B(M_\mu,M_\tau)=0$
whenever the two labels have different toral characters, that is, whenever
$\langle\mu,h\rangle\ne\langle\tau,h\rangle$ for some $h\in P^{\vee}$;

(iii) $B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$ (the normalization);

(iv) $B$ is $\sigma$-invariant: $B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$ for all
$x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)$ and all $u,v\in M$.

Because $\sigma$ is $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear and fixes the torus, condition (iv)
is equivalent to the adjunction displays

$$B(K_hu,v)=B(u,K_hv),\qquad B(E_iu,v)=B(u,q_iF_iK_i^{-1}v),\qquad B(F_iu,v)=B(u,q_i^{-1}K_iE_iv),$$

for all $u,v\in M$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$ (Verification, step 2.1).

For $\lambda$ dominant and $L(\lambda)$ the normalized simple highest weight
module, such a form exists, is unique, and is nondegenerate on $L(\lambda)$;
moreover distinct label-weight spaces with distinct characters are orthogonal
by (ii). Uniqueness is proved here (Verification, step 4.1), as is the
orthogonality; consequently, when the pairing separates $P$, the distinct
