required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.

(b) $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$.

(c) (Recursive spanning.) For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$,
$$\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad \mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}\Bigr)\setminus\{0\},$$
and the same formulas with $\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$. Each $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is generated over $A_0$ by finitely many monomials of total length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$, hence is a finitely generated $A_0$-module.

No basis property, scalar-extension spanning or crystal-lattice property of $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ or $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is asserted here; these are conclusions of the grand loop. The script letters avoid the collision with the simple module $L(\lambda)$. No choice principle is used. Each fixed component is torsionfree inside a field vector space and generated by finitely many words of its fixed height, so it is free over the DVR $A_0$; its full field-span is proved later. The field map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective, but exact equality on Kashiwara monomial generators is not asserted.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
**Assume the axiom of choice** ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $M$ be a chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight module that is integrable, has finite-dimensional label-weight spaces and weight set contained in a finite union of cones $\lambda-Q_+$ ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]), and let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of $M$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]).

(i) **Splitting along the top isotypic part.** Let $\lambda$ be a maximal weight of $M$, put $N_0:=U_q(\mathfrak g)M_\lambda$ and let $N_1$ be the sum of the remaining simple constituents, so that $M=N_0\oplus N_1$ and $N_0\cong V(\lambda)^{\oplus m}$ with $m=\dim M_\lambda$. Then $L=(L\cap N_0)\oplus(L\cap N_1)$, $B=\bigl(B\cap(L\cap N_0)/q(L\cap N_0)\bigr)\sqcup\bigl(B\cap(L\cap N_1)/q(L\cap N_1)\bigr)$, and both pairs are crystal bases of $N_0$ and $N_1$.

(ii) **Uniqueness.** There is a locally weight-finite indexed family $(\lambda_j)_{j\in J}$ in $P^+$ and an isomorphism of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-modules $\Phi:M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\bigoplus_{j\in J}V(\lambda_j)$ with $\Phi(L)=\bigoplus_j\mathcal L(\lambda_j)$ and $\Phi$ inducing a bijection $B\to\bigsqcup_j\mathcal B(\lambda_j)$ of crystals. The multiset $\{\lambda_j:j\in J\}$ is the multiset of highest weights of the simple integrable constituents of $M$: the number of $j$ with $\lambda_j=\lambda$ equals the multiplicity $[M:V(\lambda)]$.

(iii) **Components.** Through $\Phi$ the connected components of the crystal $B$ are exactly the canonical highest weight crystals $\mathcal B(\lambda_j)$; each component has a unique highest weight element $b$, of dominant weight $\lambda$, and equals the lowering-generated subcrystal $F(b)$ of [[def-highest-weight-element-and-connected-highest-weight-crystal]]. In particular the crystal graph of any crystal basis of $M$ is determined up to isomorphism by $M$, and no other highest weight elements occur.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared in [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and used to obtain the decomposition of $M$ into simple integrable highest weight modules from [[prop-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-modules-are-semisimple]], which selects a maximal independent family of simple submodules simultaneously. It also permits simultaneous choices of lifts of the finite residue bases in the possibly infinite family of top spaces. After those choices, each lattice and crystal argument is finite and choice-free. No incompatible-axiom branch is used, and no global $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness is assumed. The index set $J$ need not be finite in affine or indefinite type; local weight finiteness means only finitely many summands contribute to any fixed label-weight space.

For any finite sequence of based integrable modules in the finite-weight-space category $O_{\mathrm{int}}$, the field tensor bar $\Psi=\Theta(\text{composite factor bars})$, built from the normalized intertwiner $\Theta$ of [[thm-the-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiner-exists-and-is-unique]], is well defined, semilinear, $U$- and bar-compatible, involutive and independent of all parenthesizations; all root-height sums are vectorwise finite.

This field assertion holds for arbitrary based pairs and does not imply integral action. Its integral and based assertion holds for exactly the admissible cases proved by the integral-action supplier [[lem-quasi-r-divided-power-integrality-on-based-lattices]]: highest-first or first $C_{\mathrm{high}}$ with arbitrary based second; arbitrary based first with lowest or $C_{\mathrm{low}}$ second under finite action; all finite highest products and exact based subquotients and direct sums of their tensor constructions; ordered highest-prefix, based-middle, lowest-suffix products with explicit local support bounds; and arbitrary based pairs and products in finite Cartan type. For any other pair the same conclusion is conditional on an independently proved integral $\Theta$ action, not on field semisimplicity or lattice freeness.

In these cases: $\Psi$ preserves the divided-power integral tensor lattice; its action on raw tensor lower basis vectors is locally weight-transfer triangular with diagonal $1$; the actual tensor global vectors are its uniquely corrected bar-fixed lifts congruent to those raw tensor vectors modulo $q$, with corrections in $q\mathbb Z[q]$; they form a genuine $A$-basis and give the integral balanced tensor triple; the $q=0$ tensor lattice and crystal basis are supplied separately by the completed crystal tensor rule [[thm-crystal-basis-tensor-product-rule]], and the infinity chart is $\Psi(L_0^{\mathrm{tensor}})$, not an asserted bar containment in $L_0$, since semilinearity sends $q$ to $q^{-1}$. The raw tensor lower vectors are generally not bar fixed. Exact based integral and bar-compatible subquotient maps preserve the corrected global bases by balanced uniqueness. No assertion covers arbitrary two-sided-unbounded evaluation, semi-infinite limits, a universal-$R$ braiding, or general arbitrary-based integral action; the affine boundary in the supplier disproves the latter.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

$w_A$ be shortest with $a(A)w_A$ weakly increasing, and let $K$ be the Young
stabilizer of that sorted multiset. Then $w_A$ is shortest RIGHT modulo $K$,
$d(A)=w_A^{-1}$ is shortest LEFT, and
$$p_{A,B}(s)=s^{\ell(w_B)-\ell(w_A)}\sum_{z\in K}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_Az,\,w_B}(s^{-2}).$$
This is the **antispherical/sign** family for the entry stabilizer, in the left
convention after inversion, with Hecke variable $v=s$; the library quantum
parameter is instead $t=s^{-1}$. It has support $A\le B$ and diagonal $1$, and
$d$ is its inverse coefficient matrix through $p(-s)$. The **column Levi**
subgroup $J$ is generally different from $K$. The genuine parabolic block
composition matrix is
$$[M(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)=\sum_{C\sim_{\mathrm{col}}B}(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}P_{d(C)w_0,\,d(A)w_0}(1),$$
where $C$ runs over the column permutations of $B$. This uses singular ordinary
**spherical** coefficients for the entry stabilizer inside finite Levi
cancellation, so it covers mixed singular-ambient/parabolic-Levi blocks. It does
not identify a singular category with genuine parabolic $\mathcal O$ and does
not identify the two polynomial families by an opposite convention.

(1) The vectors $S_A:=\pi M_A$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a basis of

summand with basis the $L_A$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and

$$\pi M_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(s)\,D_A,$$

the assertions hold in the full direct limit. The relation of the source
$D_A$ to the library form-dual upper family
([[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]]) is the explicit weight

identification.

required_interface.heading: Statement
required_interface.text:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$\mathfrak p=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
be as in [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]. Then:

**(1) (Simples.)** Within an integral block, $L(\lambda)\in\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
if and only if $\lambda$ is $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral; every simple
object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is of this form.

**(2) (Standards.)** For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the
generalized Verma $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$,
has finite length, has $L(\lambda)$ as its unique simple quotient (head), and
$[M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):L(\mu)]\neq0$ forces $\mu\le\lambda$ in the
dominance order; $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the largest quotient of
$M(\lambda)$ lying in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.

**(3) (Enough projectives.)** The inclusion
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathcal O$ is exact and has a left adjoint
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ (the largest $\mathfrak p$-locally-finite quotient);
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ is right exact and sends projective objects of $\mathcal O$
to projective objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. Consequently, for every
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the object
$P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=L_{\mathfrak p}(P^{(\mathcal O)}(\lambda))$ is a
projective cover of $L(\lambda)$ in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, and
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ has enough projectives and injectives.

**(4) (Generalized-standard flags, BGG reciprocity and duality.)** Every
projective in a fixed integral block has a finite generalized Verma flag. Its
projective cover surjects to its labelled generalized standard with a kernel
filtered by higher-labelled generalized standards. The simple and
generalized-standard classes form bases of the finite block Grothendieck
group, and characters are injective on this group. For $\mathfrak p$-dominant
integral $\lambda,\mu$,
$$(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=[M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
the multiplicities being finite; moreover restricted duality restricts to an
exact contravariant involution of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ exchanging
$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ and $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda),\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=0$
for all $\lambda,\mu$.

Let $X$ be a topological space, let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf of $k$-vector
spaces (or of abelian groups) on $X$
([[def-presheaf-on-topological-space]]), let $U\subseteq X$ be open and let
$s\in\mathcal F(U)$. The **support of $s$** is
$$\operatorname{Supp}(s):=\{\,x\in U: s_x\neq 0\,\}\subseteq U,$$
where $s_x\in\mathcal F_x$ denotes the germ of $s$ at $x$ in the stalk
$\mathcal F_x$ ([[def-stalk-of-presheaf]], [[def-germ-of-section]]). A section
$s\in\mathcal F(X)$ is **compactly supported** when its support is a compact
subspace of $X$ ([[def-compact-space]]). For a subspace $Z\subseteq X$ and a
presheaf $\mathcal G$ on $Z$, the support of $t\in\mathcal G(Z)$ is defined by
the same condition using the stalks of $\mathcal G$. The support is not assumed
closed in $X$ nor compact.

When $\mathcal F$ is a **sheaf** of $k$-vector spaces the following three
consistency facts hold; they are immediate consequences of the definitions
above and are recorded here because every later compact-support statement uses
them.

1. $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$ is closed in $U$. Indeed, if $x\notin
   \operatorname{Supp}(s)$ then $s_x=0$ in the stalk; equality of germs means
   that $s$ and the zero section agree on some open neighbourhood $W\subseteq U$
   of $x$ ([[def-germ-of-section]]), so $s$ vanishes on the open neighbourhood
   $W$ of $x$, and $U\setminus\operatorname{Supp}(s)$ is therefore open in $U$.
2. $\operatorname{Supp}(s)=\varnothing$ if and only if $s=0$. If every germ of
   $s$ is zero then $s=0$ by the locality axiom of a sheaf applied to the cover
   of $U$ by its open subsets ([[lem-section-zero-if-all-germs-zero]]); the
   converse is immediate, since the zero section has zero germ at every point.
3. $\operatorname{Supp}(s|_V)=\operatorname{Supp}(s)\cap V$ for every open
   $V\subseteq U$. Restriction is compatible with the germ maps, so
   $(s|_V)_x=s_x$ for every $x\in V$ ([[def-germ-of-section]]).

Since $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$ is closed in $U$ by fact 1, a section whose
support is contained in some compact subset of $X$ is compactly supported: a
closed subset of a compact space is compact. Fact 1 is closedness in $U$ only,
and nothing here asserts that the support is closed in $X$ or that $U$ is
closed. No choice principle is used anywhere: germs, stalks, supports and
restrictions are elementary.

required_interface.heading: Definition
required_interface.text:
Fix a beta length $L\ge1$. For a partition $
u$ with at most $L$ columns (that is, $
u_1\le L$), put $$ eta_i(
u)=
u'_i+L-i\qquad(1\le i\le L).$$ Its beta numbers are strictly decreasing nonnegative integers. Conversely, from any strictly decreasing nonnegative sequence $b$ recover the unique partition with conjugate parts $
u'_i=b_i-L+i$, of degree $|
u|=\sum_i b_i-L(L-1)/2$ ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).

For arbitrary $b\in\mathbb Z^L$, first set all its alternating symbols to zero if it has repeated entries or a negative entry. Otherwise there is a unique sorting permutation $w$ taking it to decreasing order; let $
u$ be the recovered partition and let $\epsilon(b)=(-1)^{\ell(w)}$. Uniqueness of the sorting permutation is claimed only in this distinct-entry case. In the fixed degree-$r$ Grothendieck groups define $$[W^b]_{d,r}:= egin{cases}\epsilon(b)[W^
u],&|
u|=r	ext{ and } \ell(
u)\le d,\0,&	ext{otherwise},\end{cases} \qquad [S^b]_r:= egin{cases}\epsilon(b)[S_{\mathrm M}^
u],&|
u|=r,\ 0,&	ext{otherwise}.\end{cases}$$ The notation $[\Delta^b]$ is synonymous with $[W^b]_{d,r}$ when $d,r$ are fixed. The ordinary Dipper-James translation conjugates every partition label and pulls every compared module back by the same $	heta$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]], [[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]).

For a composition $\mu$ define the signed semistandard number directly by $$d_\mu(b):= egin{cases}\epsilon(b)|T_0(
u,\mu)|,&b	ext{ has distinct nonnegative entries and }|
u|=|\mu|,\0,&	ext{otherwise}. \end{cases}$$ Here the tableau alphabet is the length of $\mu$; a shape with too many rows automatically has no such tableau ([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]]). This function is alternating in the beta entries. It also obeys the branching identity $$d_\mu(b)=\sum_{\substack{C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,L\}\|C|=z}}  d_{ ar\mu}(b-\mathbf1_C),$$ where $z$ is the last nonzero part of $\mu$ and $ ar\mu$ deletes that part. The selected entries are **decreased by one**, not replaced by $-1$. For a decreasing beta sequence this is the deletion of the largest semistandard entries: they occupy a horizontal strip, at most one box in each selected column. Sorting extends the identity to distinct arbitrary sequences; if entries repeat, terms selecting just one of the equal entries cancel in pairs, while terms selecting both or neither vanish. Negative entries remain negative after decrementing. Thus the identity also holds in all zero-symbol cases. At $\mu=0$ its value is the sorting sign for a permutation of $(L-1,\ldots,0)$ and is zero otherwise, so the recursion terminates without another unproved extension rule.

In the formulas of this page take $L=r$ when $r>0$. A nonzero degree-$r$ partition has width at most $r$, so this length suffices; the Weyl cutoff $\ell(
u)\le d$ is retained even when $d<r$. A balanced displacement $+h\mathbf e_b-h\mathbf e_c$ preserves total degree. An unbalanced change is not silently treated as a class in the same fixed-degree group. The empty degree is handled by the empty beta sequence and unit symbol. No choice principle is used.

required_interface.text:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^\times$ and $\lambda\vdash n$, and write $\mu=\lambda'$, $L=\ell(w_\lambda)$ and $N=\ell(w_0(S_{\lambda'}))$. Let $P(\lambda)=z_\lambda H$ with its DJ form $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$, the cell module $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ with its Murphy form $G_{\lambda'}$, and the sign automorphism $\theta$ be as in [[def-dj-bridge-row-column-permutation-modules-and-polytabloids]], [[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]] and [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]], and let $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta$ be the $\theta$-twisted cell module of [[lem-dj-bridge-theta-transport-of-the-cellular-structure]]. Then:

1. There is a base-change compatible isomorphism of right $H$-modules $$\Phi_\lambda\colon P(\lambda)\longrightarrow C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta,\qquad \Phi_\lambda(z_\lambda)=m_0,\quad \Phi_\lambda(z_\lambda h)=m_0\theta(h)\ \ (h\in H),$$ where $m_0$ is the class of $x_{\lambda'}$ in $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ and the right side is computed with the ordinary action on $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ and read in the twist; in particular $\Phi_\lambda(e_t)=m_0\theta(T_{d_{\lambda'}(t)})$ for $t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda')$. For a class $m\in C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ and any lift $\widetilde m\in M(\lambda')$, the inverse is $\Phi_\lambda^{-1}(m)=q^{-N}x_\lambda T_{w_\lambda}\theta(\widetilde m)$, independently of the chosen lift.

2. With $G_{\lambda'}^\theta$ the transported form of [[lem-dj-bridge-theta-transport-of-the-cellular-structure]] and $u_\lambda(q):=q^{\ell(w_0(S_{\lambda'}))-\ell(w_\lambda)}\in A^\times$, $$G_{\lambda'}^\theta(\Phi_\lambda x,\Phi_\lambda y)=u_\lambda(q)\,\beta_{P(\lambda)}(x,y)\qquad(x,y\in P(\lambda)),$$ over every commutative $R$ with $q\in R^\times$. No unnamed scalar and no potentially vanishing scalar occurs: $u_\lambda$ is the explicit unit $q^{N-L}$ in the fixed normalizations of this page.

3. Consequently $\Phi_\lambda$ maps the radical of $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$ onto the radical of $G_{\lambda'}^\theta$, the induced map between the quotients is an isomorphism, with the corresponding cell-form quotients $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}\cong(D^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^\theta$, including the zero-quotient case. Over a field, when the quotients are nonzero they are the simple heads; when the forms are identically zero, the displayed quotients are zero and no assertion about the actual module heads is made. Over a PID with a chosen prime, the unit-scaled form identity preserves all divisibility submodules and their reductions. One also obtains $P(\lambda')\cong P(\lambda)^{\circ,\theta}$ with the exact position of the dual and the twist, separating same-shape duality from conjugate-sign transport. No choice principle is used.

There are exactly $e$ partitions $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_e$ of $n$ with $e$-core $\gamma$; list them in dominance order, $\lambda_1\rhd\lambda_2\rhd\cdots\rhd\lambda_e$. In the source's (Murphy) normalisation the Weyl modules and simple modules of this weight-one class satisfy $W^{\lambda_e}=L^{\lambda_e}$ and $$[W^{\lambda_k}]=[L^{\lambda_k}]+[L^{\lambda_{k+1}}]\qquad(1\le k<e),$$ so the decomposition matrix of the class is the $e\times e$ bidiagonal matrix with rows and columns $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_e$. Moreover exactly $\lambda_1$ is not $e$-restricted, while $\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_e$ are. Under the Schur functor ([[thm-schur-functor-sends-weyl-and-simple-modules-to-specht-and-hecke-simple-modules]]) the corresponding Murphy Specht classes are $$[S^{\lambda_1}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_2}_{\mathrm M}],\qquad [S^{\lambda_k}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_k}_{\mathrm M}]+[D^{\lambda_{k+1}}_{\mathrm M}]\ (2\le k<e),\qquad [S^{\lambda_e}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_e}_{\mathrm M}],$$ with $D^{\lambda_1}_{\mathrm M}=0$; conjugating partitions and applying the same $\theta$ pullback to both modules ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]], [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]) gives the corresponding decomposition matrix for the page's Dipper-James Specht modules in $e$-regular labels.

[F4] The exact Schur functor sends $W^{\lambda}$ to $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ and $L^{\lambda}$ to $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$, whose nonzero labels are precisely the restricted partitions. required_interface.heading: page summary
required_interface.text:
**Objective.** This page develops the Arakawa–Suzuki action of the degenerate
affine Hecke algebra on tensor functors and the higher-level Schur–Weyl duality
of Brundan–Kleshchev: the Casimir and place-permutation operators, the type-A
pyramid good grading and finite W-algebra, the Whittaker category and Skryabin
equivalence, the truncated (deformed) tensor space, the filtered double
centralizer, the Schur functor on parabolic category $\mathcal O$, the stable
range and its block-idempotent corner, and the Hecke residue functors with
their intertwining with category-$\mathcal O$ translation. Everything is
stated over $\mathbb C$ with the Axiom of Choice carried as an explicit
dependency, and the source normalizations differ from the library conventions
only where recorded in the individual items.

**The Hecke algebra and the Casimir action.**
[[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] fixes the degenerate affine Hecke
algebra $H_d$ with its bounded monomial basis and filtration, and
[[def-arakawa-suzuki-casimir-operators-on-tensor-functors]] defines the
natural operators $x_j=\Omega_{0j}+\sum_{k<j}P_{kj}$ and
$s_i=P_{i,i+1}$ on $M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, including the $\mathfrak{sl}_N$
normalization $y_j=x_j-z_M/N+(N-1)/2$ used by the source.
[[thm-the-casimir-and-place-permutation-operators-satisfy-degenerate-affine-hecke-relations]]
proves that these operators satisfy all Coxeter, commutation and affine cross
relations, so that every $\mathfrak g$-module carries a commuting right
$H_d$-action.

**The pyramid, the finite W-algebra and Whittaker vectors.**
[[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]]
constructs the type-A pyramid good grading, the nilpotent $e$, the parabolic
subalgebras $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak m$, the centralizer basis of
$\mathfrak g^e$ and the Whittaker character $\chi$;
[[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]] defines the finite
W-algebra $W(\lambda)$ with its $\eta$-dictionary and the Whittaker category
with its Whittaker-vector functor. The Vust double centralizer
[[thm-vust-double-centralizer-for-the-type-a-nilpotent-centralizer]] is proved
from the local normality [[lem-type-a-nilpotent-orbit-closures-are-normal-via-chain-varieties]]
and covariant extension/polarization
[[lem-nilpotent-orbit-equivariant-tensor-covariants-extend-and-polarize]]
results, for every Jordan type and every degree. The shifted Yangian and its
generators are fixed in
[[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]
with the PBW basis [[thm-ordered-monomial-pbw-basis-for-the-shifted-yangian]];
the loop filtration
[[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]]
and the Gan–Ginzburg/Skryabin inputs
[[lem-gan-ginzburg-skryabin-inputs-hold-for-the-type-a-pyramid-good-grading]]
lead to Skryabin's equivalence
[[thm-skryabins-equivalence-for-the-type-a-whittaker-pair]].

**The cyclotomic quotient and the double centralizer.**
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] fixes the quotient $H_d(\mathbf a)$
with its bounded monomial basis, central blocks and trace form;
[[lem-the-parabolic-highest-weight-truncation-factors-through-the-cyclotomic-quotient]]
computes the minimal polynomial of $x_1$ on the truncated tensor space and
hence the cyclotomic factorization, and
[[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]] defines the
filtered $(W(\lambda),H_d(\mathbf a))$-bimodule structure with associated
graded the Vust tensor space.
[[thm-the-finite-w-and-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-actions-satisfy-double-centralizer]]
proves the mutual centralizers for every origin, the stable-range
faithfulness, and the admissible-origin Morita progenerator statement.

**The Whittaker functor and the Schur quotient.**
[[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]] defines the
genuine Whittaker functor $V$ on the parabolic summand from restricted duality
and Whittaker vectors, and
[[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]]
proves its exactness, its values on the ground and tensor objects, full
faithfulness on all projectives and tiltings, and the Serre-quotient
identification.
[[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]]
defines the projective generator $T$, the Schur functor
$\pi=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ and its right-exact left adjoint,
with the boundaries of the left adjoint stated exactly.
[[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-endomorphism-isomorphism]] identifies
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}$ and its components with
the Hecke image, and [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-double-centralizer]]
assembles the all-origin double centralizer, the admissible Morita equivalence
and the exact Schur Serre quotient.

**Stable range, residues and images.**
[[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
fixes the stable range $q_l\ge d$ and the central block corner outside it;
[[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]]
defines the Hecke residue functors $e_i,f_i$ with their exactness, biadjunction
and duality compatibility.
[[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]]
identifies the images of standard, simple, projective and tilting objects and
the multiplicity dictionary $[S(A):D(B)]=d_{B,A}(1)$, and
[[thm-category-o-translation-intertwines-residue-induction-and-restriction]]
proves the natural isomorphisms intertwining residue induction and restriction
on the two sides. The companion page
[[arakawa-suzuki-functors-and-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality-examples]] works
the smallest instances.

required_interface.heading: page summary
required_interface.text:
**Objective.** This page builds the integral comparison between the ordinary
Dipper-James polytabloid module $P(\lambda)=z_\lambda H$ and the sign-twisted
Murphy cell $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta$ over the generic type-$A$ Hecke
algebra, with every unit, ideal and form tracked exactly over
$A=\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1}]$ and after every base change to a commutative ring $R$
with $q\in R^\times$. All modules are right modules; the normalization is
$(T_i-q)(T_i+1)=0$, $x_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}T_w$,
$y_\lambda=\sum_{w\in S_\lambda}(-q)^{-\ell(w)}T_w$ and
$z_\lambda=x_\lambda T_{w_\lambda}y_{\lambda'}$. Nothing on the page uses
generic semisimplicity for an integral claim, the unavailable primary sources
are never invoked, and no choice principle is used anywhere on the page.

## The row module, its form and the sign automorphism

[[def-dj-bridge-row-column-permutation-modules-and-polytabloids]] fixes the
objects: the Hecke algebra $H$, the star anti-involution $T_i^*=T_i$, the row
permutation module $M(\lambda)=x_\lambda H$, the ordinary Dipper-James
polytabloid module $P(\lambda)=z_\lambda H$, the distinguished coset set
$D_\lambda$ of row-standard right coset representatives, and the permutation
form $\beta$ with diagonal values $\beta(x_\lambda T_d,x_\lambda T_e)=
\delta_{d,e}q^{\ell(d)}$.
[[lem-dj-bridge-row-permutation-module-standard-action]] proves that
$\{x_\lambda T_d:d\in D_\lambda\}$ is a basis of $M(\lambda)$, computes the
three-case action of a generator, and shows that all of this survives base
change, and
[[lem-dj-bridge-permutation-form-invariance-and-restriction]] proves that
$\beta$ is $H$-contravariant, symmetric and well defined and that its
restriction to $P(\lambda)$ — the DJ form — inherits the same identity.
[[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]] constructs the involutive
sign automorphism $\theta$ with $\theta(T_i)=(q-1)-T_i=-qT_i^{-1}$,
$\theta(x_\lambda)=q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}y_\lambda$, its exact action on
modules and on the star-contragredient, and the base-change compatibility that
every later unit is measured against.

## The vanishing lemma and the Murphy cellular structure

[[lem-dj-bridge-parabolic-double-coset-annihilation]] proves the annihilation
identity that all later integral arguments consume: if
$\sum_{i\le k}\alpha_i>\sum_{i\le k}\nu'_i$ for some $k$, then
$x_\alpha Hy_\nu=0$, by an explicit sorting of minimal parabolic double cosets
and the exact quadratic zero product $(1+T_i)(1-q^{-1}T_i)=0$ — no cancellation
of $q+1$ and no division anywhere.
[[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]] then rebuilds the
Murphy theory locally: the Murphy basis $m^\rho_{st}=T_{d(s)}^*x_\rho T_{d(t)}$
of $H$, the dominance ideals $I^{\rhd\rho}$ and $I^{\unrhd\rho}$, the cell
module $C_{\mathrm M}(\rho)=M(\rho)/(M(\rho)\cap I^{\rhd\rho})$ with its
first-index-independent cell law, and the Murphy form $G_\rho$, all over
every coefficient ring and with the form allowed to degenerate.

## The integral polytabloid basis and the two bridge theorems

[[lem-dj-bridge-integral-murphy-and-polytabloid-straightening]] is the
integral heart of the page: it proves that $P(\lambda)$ is free with basis
$e_t=z_\lambda T_{d_{\lambda'}(t)}$ indexed by the standard tableaux of the
conjugate shape, exhibits the unit-triangular embedding minor
$e_t=q^{\ell(d_\mu(t))}b_{t'}+\text{(strictly lower terms)}$, derives the exact
signed Garnir relations $z_\lambda\sum_{d\in D}\theta(T_d)=0$, records the
Gram matrix of the restricted DJ form through the embedding (which need not be
nonsingular), and proves the split inclusion without any generic dimension
count.
[[lem-dj-bridge-theta-transport-of-the-cellular-structure]] transports the
Murphy cellular structure along $\theta$: the transported basis, the image
ideals $\theta(I^{\rhd\lambda})$ and $\theta(I^{\unrhd\lambda})$ (which are
generally different subspaces from the originals — already for $n=2$ and
$\lambda=(2)$ one has $\theta(x_{(2)})=q-T_1\notin R(1+T_1)$), the module
isomorphism $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)^\theta\cong
\theta(M(\lambda))/\theta(M(\lambda)\cap I^{\rhd\lambda})$, and the
transported form.

[[thm-dj-bridge-murphy-cell-is-the-same-shape-specht-dual]] proves the
same-shape perfect cross-pairing $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)\times P(\lambda)\to R$
with determinant a unit, identifies $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ with
$P(\lambda)^\circ$ and pins the kernel of the row quotient to the orthogonal
complement of $P(\lambda)$ — without ever inverting the DJ form.
[[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]] is the
main theorem: a base-change compatible isomorphism
$\Phi_\lambda:P(\lambda)\to C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta$ with the exact
unit $u_\lambda(q)=q^{\ell(w_0(S_{\lambda'}))-\ell(w_\lambda)}$ relating the
DJ form to the transported Murphy form. Its generic uniqueness step is the
only place where the regular trace and Jacobson nilpotence enter;
[[thm-jacobson-radical-is-nilpotent-and-the-quotient-is-semisimple]] supplies
nilpotence, and the semisimplicity and nondegeneracy conclusions are drawn
over $\mathbb Q(q)$ before the already-integral identity is specialized.

## Specialization and the dictionary

[[cor-dj-bridge-specialization-and-composition-multiplicity-dictionary]]
collects the consequences: at $q=1$ over every field the module and its form
specialize to the ordinary integral Specht lattice and the standard tabloid
form with $\theta$ becoming the sign twist; for an arbitrary unit over a field
the composition multiplicities match between $P(\lambda)$ and the conjugate
Murphy cell; and a Schur corner already proved to attach
$W(\lambda)\mapsto C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ and
$L(\lambda)\mapsto D^\lambda_{\mathrm M}$ gives the $\theta$-twisted
dictionary $F(W(\lambda'))\cong P(\lambda)^\theta$ and
$F(L(\lambda'))\cong(D^\lambda_{\mathrm{DJ}})^\theta$, including the zero
case. The companion
[[ordinary-hecke-specht-polytabloids-and-signed-murphy-comparison-examples]]
works the rank-three instances, the singular two-tableau shape and the
untwisted-conjugation counterexample.

required_interface.heading: page summary
required_interface.text:
**Objective.** This page develops the type-A cyclotomic Hecke algebras in the
nondegenerate and degenerate branches, their charged finite-quantum-characteristic
specializations, the central content sectors, and the Brundan-Kleshchev
comparison with the type-A cyclotomic Khovanov-Lauda-Rouquier algebras. The
first part constructs the universal affine and cyclotomic presentations:
ordered-monomial bases, bounded spanning, the polynomial spectra that split
over the residue values, canonical CRT content projectors, the level-one
identification with the finite Hecke algebra, and the comparison maps between
the Hecke and KLR presentations in both directions. The second part develops
the arbitrary-level Murphy cellular theory with its Jucys-Murphy triangularity,
the semistandard bases of permutation modules, the Schur algebra and the
ordinary Schur functor, and the Jantzen/filtration theory: the DVR Gram
valuation, the monic seminormal Gram determinants, their signed rim-hook
valuation expansion, the Jantzen sum formula, and the resulting classification
of blocks through Jantzen equivalence and content classes. The closing section
identifies the central content sectors with the blocks, proves the
Brundan-Kleshchev blockwise isomorphism, and transports the KLR grading to the
Hecke blocks.

**Conventions.** The field is arbitrary and $e\ge2$ is finite; the
nondegenerate branch uses a Hecke parameter $q_H\ne1$ of quantum
characteristic $e$, while the degenerate branch has $q_H=1$ and
$\operatorname{char}F=e$. The grading variable $v$ of the KLR side is
independent of $q_H$. The cyclotomic relation is imposed on the first
polynomial generator and induction appends strands on the right. The e=0
($A_\infty$) branches are outside this page's cyclic scope and are recorded
as a deferred boundary.

**Reading order.** The affine and cyclotomic presentations come first, then
their bases and spectra, then the Hecke-KLR comparison; the Murphy/cellular and
Schur theory follows the same dependency order, and the Jantzen and block
theory is built on the completed trace and cell machinery. Items on this page
are draft and are consumed by the examples companion and by the Ariki
categorification pair.
